The number recurs across history: the typical size of hunter-gatherer bands, the basic unit of the Roman army, the headcount at which many companies start to feel they 'need formal management' — all strikingly close to 150.
More usefully, he notes that the 150 is not flat but a set of concentric circles: an innermost layer of about 5 closest people (the ones you'd turn to in a crisis), then about 15 friends you can deeply trust, about 50 friends, about 150 stable acquaintances, and beyond that roughly 500 people you know and 1,500 you can name. Each outward layer brings a sharp drop in both the strength of the tie and the energy you're willing to spend on it.
He also has a charming 'grooming-to-language' hypothesis: monkeys build alliances and soothe relationships by grooming each other, but grooming reaches only one partner at a time — too inefficient to sustain a large group. Humans evolved language, especially 'gossip' — chatting is like 'grooming with the voice,' soothing several people at once while also passing on social information about who can be trusted and who should be watched. That is what let us break past grooming's headcount bottleneck and sustain larger networks.
This work offers a sober reminder for today: social media may give you thousands of 'friends,' but it cannot break the brain's hard constraint — the people you truly care about and truly maintain are still that small inner circle. Relationships have a cost and decay; they need time and face-to-face investment to 'top up.' Recognizing this actually helps you pour your limited energy into the few relationships that really matter.

assessments.text: 『社会脑假说』与『邓巴数』成为进化心理学与社会网络研究的经典框架，被广泛引用于人类学、组织行为乃至网络科学。
指出 150 只是粗略均值、个体差异极大，且部分重复研究未能稳定复现该数字，认为不应把它当成精确的『定律』。
从军队编制、企业团队规模到早期社群产品的人数上限，都有人援引邓巴数作为组织规模设计的参考。

assessments_en.text: The 'social brain hypothesis' and 'Dunbar's number' became classic frameworks in evolutionary psychology and social-network research, widely cited across anthropology, organizational behavior, and even network science.
Note that 150 is only a rough average with large individual variation, and that some replication studies failed to reproduce the number reliably, arguing it should not be treated as a precise 'law.'
From army formations and corporate team sizes to the membership caps of early online communities, the number has been invoked as a reference for organizational scale.

quotes: 你能维持的真正关系，大约就是 150 个——这是你大脑容量决定的。（对邓巴数的通俗表述，大意）
社交媒体能减缓友谊的自然衰减，却无法凭空造出原本不存在的亲密。（其线上社交研究观点，大意）
quotes_en: The number of genuine relationships you can keep up is about 150 — it's set by the capacity of your brain. (a popular rendering of Dunbar's number; paraphrased)
Social media can slow the natural decay of a friendship, but it cannot conjure an intimacy that was never there. (his view from research on online social ties; paraphrased)
works_en: Grooming, Gossip, and the Evolution of Language
Friends: Understanding the Power of Our Most Important Relationships
How Many Friends Does One Person Need?
dunbar.lineage: 承达尔文进化论与灵长类社会行为研究（如珍·古道尔一脉）的传统，把『社会脑』思路引入对人类的解释；其工作与进化心理学（科斯米德斯、托比）、社会网络分析（如『六度分隔』研究）互相呼应，深刻影响了组织设计、社群产品与当代友谊科学。
dunbar.lineage_en: Heir to Darwinian evolution and the study of primate social behavior (in the line of Jane Goodall), he brought the 'social brain' idea to bear on humans; his work resonates with evolutionary psychology (Cosmides and Tooby) and social-network analysis (the 'six degrees of separation' research) and has deeply influenced organizational design, community products, and the modern science of friendship.
dunbar.trivia: 他最初推算邓巴数，用的是不同灵长类物种『新皮层比例 vs 群体规模』的回归曲线，再把人类代入外推得约 150；有趣的是，从新石器村落、英格兰《末日审判书》里村庄的平均人口，到现代人寄圣诞贺卡的名单统计，这个数字一再浮现。
dunbar.trivia_en: He first derived the number from a regression of 'neocortex ratio vs. group size' across primate species, then extrapolated humans onto the curve to get about 150; intriguingly, the figure keeps resurfacing — from Neolithic villages and the average village population in England's Domesday Book to modern studies of how many people we send Christmas cards to.

hume.bio: 大卫·休谟（1711–1776），苏格兰启蒙运动的核心人物，哲学家、历史学家。他早慧，二十多岁便写出《人性论》，却在当时反响寥寥；后以随笔和多卷本《英国史》闻名于世、生活优裕。他性情温和豁达，朋友众多，临终时的从容令探访的鲍斯威尔大为震动。
hume.bio_en: David Hume (1711–1776) was a central figure of the Scottish Enlightenment, philosopher and historian. Precocious, he wrote A Treatise of Human Nature in his twenties to little notice, then won fame and a comfortable life through his essays and multi-volume History of England. Genial and easygoing, with many friends, his serenity on his deathbed astonished the visiting Boswell.
hume.ideas:
休谟是彻底的经验论者：他主张一切观念最终都来自感官印象，凡是找不到经验来源的概念都值得怀疑。他最著名的一击是对因果的分析——我们从未真正『看到』原因产生结果，看到的只是两类事件反复相继（他称之为『恒常联结』），于是习惯性地期待，并把这种心理习惯误当成客观的必然联系。

他还提出两个影响深远的观点：其一，『是』推不出『应当』——事实判断无法单靠逻辑得出价值判断（休谟之叉／是非之别）；其二，『理性是激情的奴隶』——真正驱动行动的是情感与欲望，理性只负责为它们盘算手段。在自由意志上他是相容论者：自由不等于无因，而是不受强迫地按自己的意愿行动。
hume.ideas_en:
Hume was a thoroughgoing empiricist: all ideas, he held, ultimately derive from sense impressions, and any concept with no experiential source is suspect. His most famous stroke is the analysis of causation — we never actually 'see' a cause produce an effect; we see only two kinds of event repeatedly following one another (his 'constant conjunction'), form a habit of expectation, and mistake that mental habit for an objective necessary connection.

He also advanced two far-reaching claims: first, one cannot derive 'ought' from 'is' — no value judgment follows by logic alone from statements of fact (the is-ought gap); second, 'reason is the slave of the passions' — what actually drives action is feeling and desire, with reason only reckoning the means. On free will he was a compatibilist: freedom is not the absence of causes but acting on one's own will without compulsion.

assessments.text: 坦承是休谟『打断了我的独断论迷梦』，激发他写出《纯粹理性批判》。
视休谟为经验论传统的顶峰，其怀疑论深刻规训了后世的分析哲学。

assessments_en.text: admitted that Hume 'interrupted my dogmatic slumber,' spurring the Critique of Pure Reason.
regarded Hume as the peak of the empiricist tradition, whose skepticism deeply disciplined later analytic philosophy.

quotes: 理性是、且只应是激情的奴隶。
习惯是人生的伟大指南。
一个明智的人，会让他的信念与证据相称。
quotes_en: Reason is, and ought only to be, the slave of the passions.
Custom is the great guide of human life.
A wise man proportions his belief to the evidence.
hume.lineage: 继承洛克、贝克莱的经验论并推向彻底的怀疑论；直接惊醒康德、催生批判哲学；其对因果与归纳的诘问成为后世科学哲学（波普尔等）与分析哲学的共同起点。
hume.lineage_en: He carried the empiricism of Locke and Berkeley to a thoroughgoing skepticism; directly awakened Kant and prompted critical philosophy; his challenge to causation and induction became a shared starting point for later philosophy of science (Popper and others) and analytic philosophy.
hume.trivia: 他生前因宗教上的怀疑倾向，两度求教席而不得。据载他晚年面对死亡异常平静，还幽默地设想向冥河船夫讨价还价多活几年——这份从容一度让笃信来世的友人难以理解。
hume.trivia_en: His religious skepticism cost him a university chair twice. He is said to have faced death with remarkable calm, even joking about bargaining with the ferryman of the underworld for a few more years — a composure his more devout friends found hard to fathom.

kant.bio: 伊曼努尔·康德（1724–1804），德国哥尼斯堡人，近代哲学的分水岭式人物。他一生几乎未离开故乡，生活极其规律，据说邻人靠他每日散步的时间对表。他年近六旬才接连出版三大批判，奠定其体系，晚年声名遍及欧洲。
kant.bio_en: Immanuel Kant (1724–1804), of Königsberg in Germany, was a watershed figure of modern philosophy. He scarcely left his hometown, lived by an extraordinarily fixed routine — neighbors were said to set their clocks by his daily walk — and only near sixty published his three great Critiques in succession, laying down his system and winning Europe-wide fame in his later years.
kant.ideas:
康德要在休谟的怀疑论与理性主义的独断之间开辟第三条路。他的『哥白尼式革命』是：不是我们的认识去符合对象，而是对象必须符合我们认识的先天形式（时间、空间、因果等范畴）。由此他区分『现象界』（我们能认识的、被因果规定的世界）与『物自体／本体』（事物自在的一面，超出认识）。

在伦理学上，他主张道德不能建立在后果或情感上，而必须源于理性的自我立法——『绝对命令』：只按你愿意它成为普遍法则的准则行动；永远把人当作目的，而非仅仅是手段。自由与道德在此交汇：正因为人能出于责任、违抗欲望去行动，人才是自律的、自由的；『你应当』预设了『你能够』。现象界的我被决定，本体的我却是自由的。
kant.ideas_en:
Kant sought a third path between Hume's skepticism and rationalist dogmatism. His 'Copernican revolution': it is not our cognition that conforms to objects, but objects that must conform to the a priori forms of our cognition (space, time, and categories such as causation). He thus distinguished the 'phenomenal' world (what we can know, governed by causation) from the 'thing-in-itself / noumenon' (the in-itself of things, beyond knowledge).

In ethics he held that morality cannot rest on consequences or feeling but must arise from reason's self-legislation — the 'categorical imperative': act only on a maxim you could will to be a universal law; always treat humanity as an end, never merely as a means. Freedom and morality meet here: precisely because a person can act from duty against desire, a person is autonomous and free; 'ought' presupposes 'can.' The phenomenal self is determined, yet the noumenal self is free.

assessments.text: 在批判中承接康德，认为其哲学是近代思想不可回避的中枢。
称康德『把人的尊严奠基于自律』，深刻塑造了现代的自由与人权观念。

assessments_en.text: built on and criticized Kant, treating his philosophy as the unavoidable hinge of modern thought.
credited Kant with 'grounding human dignity in autonomy,' profoundly shaping the modern idea of liberty and human rights.

quotes: 位我上者灿烂星空，道德律令在我心中。
要这样行动：使你意志的准则始终能成为一条普遍立法的原则。
人是目的，永远不可只当作手段。
quotes_en: Two things fill the mind with ever new admiration: the starry heavens above me and the moral law within me.
Act only according to that maxim whereby you can at the same time will that it should become a universal law.
So act as to treat humanity always as an end and never merely as a means.
works_en: Groundwork of the Metaphysics of Morals
kant.lineage: 被休谟从『独断论迷梦』中唤醒，综合了理性主义与经验论；开启德国观念论（费希特、谢林、黑格尔）；其义务论伦理与自律概念至今是道德哲学与人权论述的支柱。
kant.lineage_en: Awakened by Hume from his 'dogmatic slumber,' he synthesized rationalism and empiricism; he opened German idealism (Fichte, Schelling, Hegel); his deontological ethics and concept of autonomy remain pillars of moral philosophy and human-rights discourse.
kant.trivia: 康德生活规律到近乎传奇：终身未婚、几乎从不远行，却在书斋里想象整个世界。他早年也讲授自然地理与天文，曾提出关于太阳系起源的星云假说的早期版本。
kant.trivia_en: Kant's routine was almost legendary: never married, scarcely traveled, yet imagined the whole world from his study. In earlier years he lectured on physical geography and astronomy, and proposed an early version of the nebular hypothesis about the origin of the solar system.

darwin.bio: 1809–1882，生于英格兰什鲁斯伯里。英国博物学家，因乘「小猎犬号」环球考察五年而积累了海量观察。1859年出版《物种起源》，提出以自然选择为机制的演化论，彻底改变了人类对生命与自身的理解。
darwin.bio_en: 1809–1882, born in Shrewsbury, England. A British naturalist who amassed vast observations during a five-year voyage around the world aboard HMS Beagle. In 1859 he published On the Origin of Species, setting out the theory of evolution by natural selection and transforming forever how humanity understands life and itself.
darwin.ideas:
达尔文要解释一个古老的谜：地球上为什么会有这么多种类的生物，而且每一种都和它的生活环境配合得如此精妙？啄木鸟的喙正好凿木，眼睛的构造精密如相机。在他之前，最自然的答案是：必定有一位神圣的设计师，逐一精心造就。达尔文给出了一个截然不同、却同样能解释「精巧」的答案——「自然选择」。
这个机制可以从零拆解成三步。第一，「变异」：同一物种的个体并非完全相同，有的跑得快些、毛厚些、喙长些，这些差异有的能遗传给后代。第二，「生存竞争」：生物繁殖出的后代，远多于环境所能养活的数量，于是它们不得不为食物、配偶、生存而竞争，大部分注定夭折。第三，「差别繁殖」：在这场竞争里，那些恰好带有有利变异的个体，活下来、留下后代的机会更大，于是它们的特征就更多地传给下一代。一代代累积，物种就慢慢「适应」了环境。
举个具体例子：一群兔子里，偶然有几只跑得更快。狐狸来了，跑得慢的更容易被吃掉，跑得快的更容易活下来繁殖。它们把「快」的特征传下去，下一代里快兔子的比例就高了。如此重复成千上万代，整个种群都变得善跑。注意：没有谁在「设计」快兔子，也没有兔子「想要」变快——只是跑得慢的被淘汰了。这就是关键洞见：看似精巧的「设计」，其实是一个盲目的、无目的的过程，在极其漫长的「深时间」里一点点累积出来的结果。设计的表象是真的，但背后并没有设计师。
由此他还推出第二个震撼的结论——「共同祖先」。如果物种会随时间分化，那么把时间往回倒，不同的物种就会汇聚到共同的祖先上。所有生命因此连成一棵巨大的「生命之树」：人与黑猩猩是近枝，与橡树是远亲，但归根结底同根同源。在《人类的由来》中，他鼓起勇气把人也放进这幅图景——人并非凌驾于自然之上的特殊造物，而是这棵树上的一根枝条。
值得一提的是达尔文本人的审慎。他深知此说会激起怎样的风暴，因而反复打磨证据二十余年才发表。他在宗教上倾向于不可知，自称「不可知论者」；他也并不歌颂自然，反而为其中的残酷而不安——他在信中提到，一想到某些寄生蜂把卵产在活生生的毛虫体内、幼虫从内部将其吃空，便难以相信有一位仁慈而全能的神会刻意如此设计。今天，从医学、农业到对抗细菌耐药性，演化论依然是整个现代生物学的统一基石。
darwin.ideas_en:
Darwin set out to solve an ancient riddle: why are there so many kinds of living things on Earth, each fitted so exquisitely to where it lives? A woodpecker's beak is just right for drilling wood; the eye is as intricate as a camera. Before him, the most natural answer was that a divine designer must have crafted each one with care. Darwin gave a wholly different answer that could explain the same intricacy—"natural selection."
The mechanism can be unpacked from scratch in three steps. First, "variation": individuals of the same species are not identical—some run faster, have thicker fur, or longer beaks, and some of these differences can be passed to offspring. Second, "the struggle for existence": creatures produce far more offspring than the environment can support, so they must compete for food, mates, and survival, and most are bound to perish. Third, "differential reproduction": in that struggle, the individuals that happen to carry favorable variations are more likely to survive and leave offspring, so their traits pass more often to the next generation. Accumulated over generations, the species gradually "adapts" to its environment.
A concrete example: among a population of rabbits, a few by chance run faster. When foxes come, the slower ones are more easily caught and the faster ones more likely to survive and breed. They pass on their "fast" trait, and the next generation has a higher proportion of fast rabbits. Repeat this over thousands of generations and the whole population becomes good at running. Notice: no one "designed" the fast rabbit, and no rabbit "wanted" to become faster—the slow ones were simply weeded out. Here is the key insight: what looks like exquisite "design" is in fact the product of a blind, purposeless process, built up little by little over the immense span of "deep time." The appearance of design is real, but there is no designer behind it.
From this he drew a second startling conclusion—"common descent." If species diverge over time, then running the clock backward, different species converge on shared ancestors. All life thus links into one vast "tree of life": humans and chimpanzees are near branches, humans and oaks distant cousins, but ultimately of one root. In The Descent of Man he found the courage to place humanity into this picture too—not as a special creation lording over nature, but as one branch on the tree.
Darwin's own caution is worth noting. He knew well what a storm this would stir, and so refined his evidence for over twenty years before publishing. On religion he leaned toward the unknowable, calling himself an "agnostic"; nor did he glorify nature—he was instead troubled by its cruelty. In a letter he remarked that he could not believe a benevolent and omnipotent God would deliberately design certain parasitic wasps to lay their eggs inside living caterpillars, the larvae devouring them alive from within. Today, from medicine and agriculture to the fight against antibiotic resistance, evolution remains the unifying foundation of all modern biology.

assessments.text: 读完《物种起源》后说：「我竟没想到这一点，真是太蠢了！」此后自称「达尔文的斗犬」，公开为演化论辩护。

assessments.by: 特奥多修斯·杜布赞斯基
assessments.text: 提出名言：「若无演化之光，生物学中的一切都将无从理解。」
称达尔文的自然选择理论是「人类有史以来最伟大的思想之一」。

assessments_en.text: On reading the Origin he exclaimed, "How extremely stupid not to have thought of that!" and thereafter called himself "Darwin's bulldog," publicly defending evolution.
He coined the famous dictum: "Nothing in biology makes sense except in the light of evolution."
He called Darwin's theory of natural selection "one of the greatest ideas ever conceived by the human mind."

quotes: 并非最强壮的物种存活下来，也非最聪明的，而是最能适应变化的。（大意，常归于达尔文，实为后人的概括）
如此简单的开端，无尽美丽而奇异的生命形式，曾经并且仍在不断演化出来。（《物种起源》结尾）
我们对所有生灵的爱，是人最高贵的品质。（《人类的由来》）
quotes_en: It is not the strongest of the species that survives, nor the most intelligent, but the one most adaptable to change. (paraphrased; widely attributed to Darwin but actually a later summary of his ideas)
From so simple a beginning endless forms most beautiful and most wonderful have been, and are being, evolved. (closing of the Origin of Species)
The love for all living creatures is the most noble attribute of man. (The Descent of Man)
works_en: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals
The Variation of Animals and Plants under Domestication
darwin.lineage: 受莱尔的地质学「渐变」思想与马尔萨斯人口论启发；与华莱士各自独立提出自然选择。其理论经20世纪与遗传学融合为「现代综合论」，奠定了整个现代生物学。
darwin.lineage_en: He was inspired by Lyell's gradualist geology and Malthus's essay on population; he and Wallace arrived at natural selection independently. In the twentieth century his theory fused with genetics into the "Modern Synthesis," the foundation of all of modern biology.
darwin.trivia: 1858年，年轻的华莱士寄来一篇独立得出相同结论的论文，促使一向迟疑的达尔文加紧发表——两人的成果于同年共同宣读，次年《物种起源》才问世。
darwin.trivia_en: In 1858 the young Wallace sent Darwin a paper that had independently reached the same conclusion, spurring the long-hesitant Darwin to publish—their work was read jointly that year, and Origin of Species appeared only the year after.

einstein.bio: 阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦（1879–1955），德裔理论物理学家，二十世纪科学的象征。他以狭义与广义相对论重塑了人类的时空观，因光电效应获 1921 年诺贝尔物理学奖。纳粹上台后他移居美国，晚年在普林斯顿从事统一场论研究，并成为和平与人道主义的公共良心。
einstein.bio_en: Albert Einstein (1879–1955), German-born theoretical physicist, is the symbol of twentieth-century science. His special and general relativity reshaped humanity's view of space and time, and he won the 1921 Nobel Prize in Physics for the photoelectric effect. After the Nazis' rise he emigrated to the United States, spent his later years at Princeton pursuing a unified field theory, and became a public conscience for peace and humanitarianism.
einstein.ideas:
爱因斯坦相信宇宙有一种可被理性把握的、客观而和谐的秩序——这既是他的科学信念，也是他所谓的『宗教感』（他常说信仰『斯宾诺莎的神』：显现于万物法则、而非干预人事的神）。正因如此，他难以接受量子力学的根本随机性，留下名言『上帝不掷骰子』，并与玻尔就实在的本质长期论辩。

在自由意志上，他是坚定的决定论者。他钟爱叔本华的名句『人能够做他所想要的，但不能想要他所想要的』，认为人的意志同样嵌在因果之中，没有例外。但他把这一信念引向温柔的伦理：既然人人都被前因塑造，我们便该少一些苛责、多一些理解与宽容——这份『决定论的谦卑』贯穿他对道德与人生的态度。
einstein.ideas_en:
Einstein believed the universe has a rationally graspable, objective and harmonious order — at once his scientific conviction and what he called his 'religious feeling' (he often said he believed in 'Spinoza's God': one revealed in the laws of all things, not one who intervenes in human affairs). For this reason he could not accept the fundamental randomness of quantum mechanics, leaving the famous line 'God does not play dice,' and debated the nature of reality with Bohr for years.

On free will he was a firm determinist. He loved Schopenhauer's line 'a man can do what he wills, but he cannot will what he wills,' holding that the human will too is embedded in causation, without exception. But he turned this conviction toward a gentle ethic: since everyone is shaped by prior causes, we should judge less harshly and understand and forgive more — a 'determinist humility' that runs through his attitude to morality and life.

assessments.text: 在著名的玻尔–爱因斯坦论战中回敬：『别指挥上帝该怎么做。』
虽在量子随机性上判爱因斯坦『输』了论战，却公认其质疑（如 EPR）催生了量子纠缠与量子信息的研究。

assessments_en.text: retorted in the famous Bohr–Einstein debates: 'Stop telling God what to do.'
though it judged Einstein to have 'lost' the debate on quantum randomness, credits his objections (e.g. EPR) with spurring the study of entanglement and quantum information.

quotes: 上帝不掷骰子。
关于宇宙最不可理解之处，在于它竟然是可以理解的。
我信仰斯宾诺莎的神——那显现于存在之秩序的神。
quotes_en: God does not play dice.
The most incomprehensible thing about the universe is that it is comprehensible.
I believe in Spinoza's God, who reveals himself in the orderly harmony of what exists.
works: 《论动体的电动力学》(狭义相对论)
《物理学的进化》(与英费尔德合著)
works_en: 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies' (special relativity)
The field equations of general relativity
The Evolution of Physics (with Leopold Infeld)
einstein.lineage: 站在牛顿经典物理的肩上又将其超越；与玻尔、海森堡等量子先驱既合作又论战；其决定论与实在论立场承自斯宾诺莎与叔本华，并深刻影响了后世关于科学哲学与自由意志的讨论。
einstein.lineage_en: He stood on Newtonian physics and surpassed it; both collaborated and quarreled with quantum pioneers such as Bohr and Heisenberg; his determinism and realism descend from Spinoza and Schopenhauer and deeply shaped later debates in the philosophy of science and free will.
einstein.trivia: 1952 年他被邀出任以色列第二任总统，婉拒了，说自己不懂如何与人打交道、只懂方程。他的大脑在死后被保存研究；他也曾说想象力比知识更重要。
einstein.trivia_en: In 1952 he was offered the presidency of Israel and declined, saying he had no aptitude for dealing with people, only with equations. His brain was preserved for study after his death; he also remarked that imagination is more important than knowledge.

hawking.bio: 1942–2018，生于英国牛津。21 岁被诊断患有渐冻症（肌萎缩侧索硬化，ALS），医生断言他只剩几年寿命，他却带病工作了半个多世纪。作为剑桥大学的理论物理学家，他在黑洞与宇宙起源上做出奠基性贡献，更以科普巨著《时间简史》让全世界仰望星空。
hawking.bio_en: 1942–2018, born in Oxford, England. At twenty-one he was diagnosed with motor neurone disease (ALS) and told he had only a few years to live, yet he worked for more than half a century despite it. As a theoretical physicist at Cambridge, he made foundational contributions to the study of black holes and the origin of the universe, and through his blockbuster A Brief History of Time he taught the whole world to look up at the stars.
hawking.ideas:
霍金一生追问的是宇宙最极端的两端：黑洞，和时间的开端。
先说黑洞。所谓黑洞，是一团质量大到连光都逃不出去的天体——它的引力强到把周围的时空压成一个无底洞，任何东西一旦越过那道叫「事件视界」的边界，就再也回不来。按经典理论，黑洞应该是绝对的「黑」，只进不出。但霍金 1974 年的惊人发现彻底改写了这一点：把量子力学考虑进去后，黑洞其实会极其微弱地「发光」、缓缓向外辐射能量——这就是「霍金辐射」。打个比方，真空并非空无一物，而是不断有成对的虚粒子瞬间冒出又湮灭；在事件视界边缘，偶尔一个粒子掉进黑洞、另一个逃了出来，看上去就像黑洞在往外吐东西。这意味着黑洞并非永恒，它会极其缓慢地「蒸发」，最终消失。这一发现第一次把引力、量子论和热力学三大支柱联系在了一起，被公认为现代物理学最深刻的洞见之一。
再说宇宙的开端。霍金早年与彭罗斯合作证明：如果广义相对论成立，宇宙必然始于一个「奇点」——一个密度无穷大、时空曲率无穷大的起点，也就是「大爆炸」。这等于用数学说明，宇宙有一个明确的开始。这里他有一个常被误解、却极优雅的想法：很多人问「大爆炸之前是什么？」，霍金说这个问题本身可能是问错了——因为「时间」本身就是从大爆炸那一刻才开始的。就像问「北极的北边是哪里？」——到了北极，再没有「更北」可言。既然时间有起点，「之前」二字便失去了意义。
基于此，他还提出一个大胆主张：宇宙未必需要一位创世者。在他看来，由于引力这样的物理定律存在，宇宙完全可以从「无」中自发地、自然地诞生，无需谁去点燃第一把火。这并非要证明上帝不存在，而是说：用物理学本身，就足以解释宇宙为何会无中生有。
他毕生的终极梦想，是找到一套「万有理论」——一组能同时解释从最微小的粒子到最宏大的星系、把所有物理定律统一起来的方程，让人类「读懂上帝的心思」。这个梦至今未竟，却指引着无数后来者。
而所有这些思考，都是在一具几乎完全瘫痪的身体里完成的。渐冻症逐渐夺走了他的行动与声音，最后他只能靠脸颊肌肉操控一台语音合成器，一个字一个字地「说话」。他活了七十六岁，远超医生预言，本身就是对人类意志的礼赞。
hawking.ideas_en:
Hawking spent his life questioning the two most extreme ends of the cosmos: black holes, and the beginning of time.
First, black holes. A black hole is an object so massive that not even light can escape it—its gravity crushes the surrounding spacetime into a bottomless pit, and once anything crosses the boundary called the "event horizon," it can never return. By classical theory a black hole should be utterly "black," letting things in but never out. But Hawking's astonishing 1974 discovery rewrote this entirely: once you bring quantum mechanics into the picture, a black hole actually "glows" ever so faintly, slowly radiating energy outward—this is "Hawking radiation." By way of analogy, the vacuum is not truly empty; pairs of virtual particles constantly flicker into being and annihilate. At the edge of the event horizon, now and then one particle falls in while the other escapes, so it looks as if the black hole is spitting something out. This means black holes are not eternal—they very slowly "evaporate" and eventually vanish. The discovery, for the first time, tied together the three great pillars of gravity, quantum theory, and thermodynamics, and is regarded as one of the most profound insights of modern physics.
Now, the beginning of the universe. Working early on with Roger Penrose, Hawking proved that if general relativity holds, the universe must have begun in a "singularity"—a starting point of infinite density and infinite spacetime curvature, the "Big Bang." This was, in effect, a mathematical demonstration that the universe had a definite beginning. Here he had an idea often misunderstood yet wonderfully elegant: many people ask "what came before the Big Bang?", and Hawking said the question itself may be malformed—because "time" itself began only at the moment of the Big Bang. It is like asking "what lies north of the North Pole?"—once you reach the Pole, there is no "further north." If time has a starting point, the word "before" loses its meaning.
On this basis he made a bold claim: the universe need not require a creator. As he saw it, because physical laws such as gravity exist, the universe could perfectly well arise spontaneously and naturally from "nothing," with no one needed to light the first spark. This was not meant to prove God does not exist, but to say: physics itself suffices to explain why there is something rather than nothing.
His ultimate lifelong dream was to find a "theory of everything"—a single set of equations uniting all physical laws, from the tiniest particle to the grandest galaxy, that would let humanity "read the mind of God." That dream remains unfulfilled, yet it guides countless successors.
And all of this thinking was done inside an almost completely paralyzed body. ALS gradually robbed him of movement and voice, until at last he could "speak" only by twitching a cheek muscle to drive a speech synthesizer, one word at a time. He lived to seventy-six, far beyond his doctors' prediction—an event that is itself a tribute to the human will.

assessments.text: 在霍金的讣告中，这位合作者与后来的诺奖得主称他的工作「在结合广义相对论与量子论上做出了最杰出的贡献」，并赞其面对病痛的坚韧。
在霍金辞世时公开悼念，称他的离去在宇宙学的知识版图上留下了一片真空。

assessments_en.text: In Hawking's obituary, his collaborator and later Nobel laureate wrote that his work made "the most outstanding contribution" toward combining general relativity with quantum theory, praising his resilience in the face of illness.
On Hawking's death he paid public tribute, saying his passing left a kind of intellectual vacuum on the map of cosmology.

quotes: 我的目标很简单：就是把宇宙彻底理解透——它为何如此，以及它究竟为何存在。（《时间简史》相关访谈，大意）
记得仰望星空，而不要总盯着自己的脚。（公开讲话，大意）
无论生活看起来多么艰难，总有你能做、并能做好的事。（公开讲话，大意）
quotes_en: My goal is simple: a complete understanding of the universe—why it is as it is, and why it exists at all. (from interviews around A Brief History of Time, paraphrased)
Remember to look up at the stars and not down at your feet. (from a public address, paraphrased)
However difficult life may seem, there is always something you can do, and succeed at. (from a public address, paraphrased)
works: 《时空的大尺度结构》（与埃利斯合著，1973，专著）
works_en: The Large Scale Structure of Space-Time (with George Ellis, 1973, monograph)
Brief Answers to the Big Questions (2018, posthumous)
hawking.lineage: 学术上承爱因斯坦的广义相对论与量子理论传统，与彭罗斯合作奠定奇点定理；其黑洞热力学的洞见深刻影响了贝肯斯坦、萨斯坎德等人，并直接推动了今日关于量子引力与黑洞信息悖论的研究。
hawking.lineage_en: Academically he carried forward Einstein's general relativity and the quantum tradition, and with Penrose laid the singularity theorems; his insights into black-hole thermodynamics deeply influenced Bekenstein, Susskind, and others, and directly drive today's research on quantum gravity and the black-hole information paradox.
hawking.trivia: 他曾在 2009 年为「时间旅行者」举办过一场派对——却故意在派对结束后才发出请柬，结果无人赴约，他以此幽默地「证明」了时间旅行行不通；他还客串过《辛普森一家》《星际迷航》和《生活大爆炸》。
hawking.trivia_en: In 2009 he threw a party for time travelers—but sent out the invitations only after the party was over, and when no one showed up he wryly took it as "proof" that time travel does not work; he also made cameo appearances on The Simpsons, Star Trek, and The Big Bang Theory.

nagarjuna.bio: 龙树（约 150–250），梵名 Nāgārjuna，古印度大乘佛教思想家，中观学派（Madhyamaka）的创立者，被后世大乘诸宗尊为『八宗共祖』。相传出身南印度婆罗门，聪慧绝伦，早年遍学世间学问，后入佛门，深研般若经典，造《中论》等论著，以严密的辩证法阐扬『空』义，奠定了大乘中观哲学的根基，影响遍及印度、汉传与藏传佛教。
nagarjuna.bio_en: Nāgārjuna (c. 150–250) was an Indian Mahāyāna Buddhist thinker, founder of the Madhyamaka ('Middle Way') school, honored by later Mahāyāna traditions as a common patriarch of eight schools. By tradition a brilliant South Indian Brahmin who mastered worldly learning before entering the Buddhist order, he studied the Perfection of Wisdom scriptures deeply and composed treatises such as the Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way, using rigorous dialectic to expound 'emptiness' and laying the foundation of Mahāyāna Madhyamaka philosophy, with influence across Indian, Chinese, and Tibetan Buddhism.
nagarjuna.ideas:
龙树思想的核心是一个字：**空（śūnyatā）。但『空』极易被误解——它不是说什么都不存在，而是说：一切事物都没有独立、恒常、自己成就自己的『自性』。**桌子、你、一个念头，都是种种条件（因缘）聚合而暂时显现的，条件散了它就变、就灭；找不到一个不依赖他物、永恒不变的内核。所以说它『空』——空掉的是那个想象中的固定本质，而非现象本身。这与佛陀的『缘起』是同一件事的两面：正因为万物缘起，所以无自性；正因为无自性，缘起才可能。

他最锋利的工具是辩证法。在《中论》里，他不正面立一套主张，而是把对手（以及常识）关于『生/灭、常/断、一/异、来/去』的种种执定，一一推到自相矛盾，令其自行瓦解——著名的『八不中道』（不生不灭、不常不断……）就是要人放下这些两极的执著，走一条不落两边的中道。

但龙树绝非虚无主义者。他提出『二谛』来化解误会：在世俗谛（约定俗成的日常层面），因果宛然、善恶分明、做事修行样样都算数；在胜义谛（究竟层面），一切无自性、不可执取。二谛不相冲突——恰恰因为事物是空的、可变的，努力与修行才有意义（若一切有固定自性，反倒什么都改不了）。理解了空，人便能松开对『我』和万物的死执，既积极入世，又不被得失系缚，这正是大乘慈悲与智慧得以展开的地基。
nagarjuna.ideas_en:
The heart of Nāgārjuna's thought is one word: **emptiness (śūnyatā). But 'emptiness' is easily misread — it does not say nothing exists, but that no thing has an independent, permanent 'self-nature' by which it is itself.** A table, you, a passing thought are all the temporary appearance of gathered conditions; when the conditions disperse, they change and cease, and no unchanging core independent of everything else can be found. Hence 'empty' — what is emptied is the imagined fixed essence, not the phenomenon itself. This is the flip side of the Buddha's 'dependent arising': because all things arise dependently they lack self-nature, and because they lack self-nature dependent arising is possible.

His sharpest tool is dialectic. In the Fundamental Verses he advances no positive thesis of his own but drives every fixed position his opponents (and common sense) hold about 'arising and ceasing, permanence and annihilation, identity and difference, coming and going' into self-contradiction, letting it collapse of itself — the famous 'eight negations of the middle way' (neither arising nor ceasing, neither permanent nor annihilated...) aim to make one release these polar clingings and walk a middle way that falls to neither extreme.

Yet Nāgārjuna is no nihilist. He offers the 'two truths' to dispel the misunderstanding: at the conventional level, cause and effect hold, good and bad are distinct, and action and practice all count; at the ultimate level, all lacks self-nature and cannot be grasped. The two do not conflict — precisely because things are empty and changeable, effort and practice have meaning (were everything fixed in self-nature, nothing could be changed at all). Understanding emptiness, a person can loosen the death-grip on 'self' and on all things, engaging the world actively yet unbound by gain and loss — the very ground on which Mahāyāna compassion and wisdom unfold.

assessments.text: 东晋时译出《中论》《十二门论》《大智度论》等龙树要典，使中观之学传入汉地，后成三论宗所依，尊龙树为祖。
藏传佛教格鲁派宗师，视龙树中观为了义之极，于《菩提道次第》与中观诸论中反复阐扬其空性与缘起不二之旨。

assessments_en.text: In the Eastern Jin he translated key Nāgārjuna treatises — the Middle Way, the Twelve Gates, the Great Perfection of Wisdom — bringing Madhyamaka into China, where it became the basis of the Sanlun school that honors Nāgārjuna as founder.

The Gelug master of Tibetan Buddhism regarded Nāgārjuna's Madhyamaka as the height of definitive meaning, expounding its non-duality of emptiness and dependent arising throughout the Stages of the Path and his Madhyamaka works.

quotes: 众因缘生法，我说即是空，亦为是假名，亦是中道义。
以有空义故，一切法得成；若无空义故，一切则不成。
不生亦不灭，不常亦不断，不一亦不异，不来亦不出。
quotes_en: What arises through conditions, I declare to be emptiness; it is also a provisional name, and is itself the meaning of the middle way.
Because there is emptiness, all things can be established; were there no emptiness, nothing could be established.
Neither arising nor ceasing, neither permanent nor annihilated, neither one nor many, neither coming nor going.
works_en: Mūlamadhyamakakārikā (Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way)
Great Treatise on the Perfection of Wisdom (attributed)
nagarjuna.lineage: 上承般若经系与佛陀缘起之教，创中观一派；下开提婆、佛护、清辨、月称诸大家，经鸠摩罗什传入汉地成三论宗，又为藏传中观应成派之根本，影响华严、天台、禅诸宗。
nagarjuna.lineage_en: Inheriting the Perfection of Wisdom scriptures and the Buddha's teaching of dependent arising, he founded the Madhyamaka school; his lineage opened onto Āryadeva, Buddhapālita, Bhāvaviveka, and Candrakīrti, passed through Kumārajīva into China as the Sanlun school, became the root of the Tibetan Prāsaṅgika Madhyamaka, and shaped the Huayan, Tiantai, and Chan traditions.
nagarjuna.trivia: 围绕龙树的生平有许多传说，其一说他曾入龙宫取回般若经典，故名『龙树』；这类神话固不可尽信，却折射出后世对他『深探智慧之海、取回甚深教法』的崇敬。
nagarjuna.trivia_en: Many legends surround his life; one holds that he retrieved Perfection of Wisdom scriptures from the palace of the nāgas (dragons), hence the name 'Nāgārjuna.' Such myths are not to be taken literally, yet they reflect posterity's reverence for one who 'dived into the ocean of wisdom and brought back the most profound teaching.'

sunzi.bio: 约前544–前496，春秋末期军事家、《孙子兵法》作者，相传名孙武，齐国人，后仕于吴。史载他以兵法十三篇见吴王阖闾，受任为将，助吴大破强楚、威震诸侯。其书是世界上现存最早、影响最深远的兵学经典。
sunzi.bio_en: c. 544–496 BC, a military thinker of the late Spring and Autumn period and author of The Art of War. Traditionally named Sun Wu, a native of the state of Qi who later served Wu. The histories say he presented his thirteen chapters on war to King Helu of Wu, was made a general, and helped Wu crush the powerful state of Chu. His book is the oldest and most influential treatise on strategy that survives.
sunzi.ideas:
孙子最颠覆的一点，是把战争从『比谁更勇猛』变成了『比谁更会算』。在他之前，打仗常被当成血气与英雄主义的较量；他却冷静地说，真正的高手，是在开打之前就已经在沙盘上算清了胜负——『多算胜，少算不胜』。
他最有名的两句话是骨架。一是『知己知彼，百战不殆』：先把自己的家底（人力、补给、士气）和对手的虚实都摸清，再决定打不打、怎么打；信息不足就不要轻举妄动。二是『不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也』：能不打就达成目的，才是最高明的——打仗（哪怕赢）本身就是巨大的消耗。
他还提出一个对管理极有启发的概念：『势』。与其指望手下每个人都是英雄，不如把局面、节奏、赏罚、地形布置好，让一块普通的石头放到陡坡上也能滚出千钧之力——『求之于势，不责于人』。这其实是在说：好的系统能让平凡的人做出不凡的事，而坏的系统会浪费掉最好的人。
后世常误以为《孙子兵法》是教人耍诈，其实它的底色是『慎战』：因为深知战争的代价，所以反复劝人不要轻易开战、不要因愤怒而出兵。它早已超出军事，被广泛用于商业竞争、谈判、管理与人生决策。
sunzi.ideas_en:
Sun Tzu's most subversive move was to turn war from a contest of who is braver into a contest of who calculates better. Before him, battle was often treated as a clash of blood and heroism; he coolly insisted that the real master has already worked out victory or defeat on the planning table before the fighting starts: 'more calculation wins, less calculation loses'.
Two lines form his skeleton. First, 'know yourself and know the other, and in a hundred battles you are never in peril': understand your own resources (manpower, supply, morale) and the real state of your opponent before deciding whether and how to fight, and do not act rashly when information is short. Second, 'to subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme excellence': achieving your aim without battle is the highest skill, because war, even when won, is itself a vast drain.
He also offered a concept rich for management: shi, configuration or momentum. Rather than hope every subordinate is a hero, arrange the situation, timing, rewards, and terrain so that even an ordinary stone, placed on a steep slope, rolls with enormous force: 'seek victory from configuration, not from individuals'. In effect: a good system lets ordinary people do extraordinary things, while a bad system wastes even the best people.
Later readers often mistook The Art of War for a manual of trickery, but its undertone is caution about war: precisely because he knew its cost, he repeatedly urged against fighting lightly or out of anger. The work long ago outgrew the military and is widely applied to business competition, negotiation, management, and life decisions.

assessments.text: 司马迁在《孙子吴起列传》中记其『以兵法见于吴王阖闾』，并以『吴宫教战、斩美姬立威』之事，描述他治军纪律之严。
三国曹操为《孙子》作注（《孙子略解》），称『吾观兵书战策多矣，孙武所著深矣』，是历史上最重要的注家之一。

assessments_en.by: Records of the Grand Historian (Sima Qian)
assessments_en.text: Sima Qian's biography records that Sun Tzu 'presented his art of war to King Helu of Wu', and through the episode of drilling the palace women and beheading two royal favorites to establish authority, depicts the severity of his military discipline.
Cao Cao of the Three Kingdoms wrote the most important early commentary on The Art of War, saying 'I have read many books on war and strategy, but what Sun Wu wrote is the most profound'.

quotes: 知己知彼，百战不殆。（《孙子兵法·谋攻》）
不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也。（《孙子兵法·谋攻》）
善战者，求之于势，不责于人。（《孙子兵法·势篇》）
quotes_en: Know yourself and know the other, and in a hundred battles you will never be in peril. (The Art of War, 'Strategic Attack')
To subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme excellence. (The Art of War, 'Strategic Attack')
The skilled warrior seeks victory from the configuration of force, not from individuals. (The Art of War, 'Configuration')
sunzi.lineage: 上承春秋兵学传统，下启孙膑、《吴子》《尉缭子》等兵家；自曹操注本后，历代注家辈出。其思想东传日本（武田信玄『风林火山』即出于此），近世经《战争论》对照与商业管理引用，影响遍及全球军事、商战与战略研究。
sunzi.lineage_en: He drew on the military traditions of the Spring and Autumn era and gave rise to a lineage including Sun Bin and the Wuzi and Weiliaozi treatises; after Cao Cao's commentary, annotators multiplied through the dynasties. His thought spread to Japan (Takeda Shingen's 'wind, forest, fire, mountain' banner derives from it), and in modern times, read alongside Clausewitz and cited in business management, it shapes military, commercial, and strategic study worldwide.
sunzi.trivia: 《孙子兵法》是史上被翻译、研究最多的兵书之一，从拿破仑到现代商学院都奉为经典；硅谷与体育界也常引用。书中虽以战争为题，却通篇反对好战，主张『慎战』『全胜』——以最小代价、甚至不流血达成目标。
sunzi.trivia_en: The Art of War is among the most translated and studied books on war in history, revered from Napoleon to modern business schools, and often quoted in Silicon Valley and sport. Though its subject is war, the whole text argues against bellicosity, urging caution and 'complete victory': achieving the aim at minimal cost, even without bloodshed.

wangyangming.bio: 王阳明（1472–1529），名守仁，字伯安，浙江余姚人，因筑室于会稽阳明洞、世称阳明先生，明代大儒、心学的集大成者，亦是罕见的能带兵平乱的哲学家。早年遍历辞章、骑射、佛老，屡试始第；因忤宦官刘瑾，谪贬贵州龙场驿，于绝境中大彻大悟，史称『龙场悟道』。此后讲学不辍，又屡平叛乱、军功赫赫，立德、立功、立言，被后世推为『真三不朽』。
wangyangming.bio_en: Wang Yangming (1472–1529), personal name Shouren, was a native of Yuyao in Zhejiang, known as Master Yangming after the Yangming Grotto where he built his study. A great Confucian of the Ming dynasty and the culminating figure of the School of Mind (xinxue), he was also that rare thing — a philosopher who could command armies. In his youth he ranged across literature, archery, and Buddhism and Daoism before passing the exams; having offended the eunuch Liu Jin, he was banished to a remote post station at Longchang in Guizhou, where amid extremity he attained a great awakening, the famed 'enlightenment at Longchang.' Thereafter he never ceased teaching, repeatedly quelled rebellions with distinguished military merit, and, uniting virtue, achievement, and words, was honored by posterity as 'truly thrice-immortal.'
wangyangming.ideas:
王阳明的学问，是对朱熹一系理学的一次反动。朱熹教人『格物穷理』——到万事万物上一件件去探求那个外在的『理』；王阳明青年时对着竹子『格』了七天七夜，格出一场大病，也格出一个疑问：理若在心外，人穷尽一生也追不完。龙场悟道后他给出另一条路：**『心即理』——天理不在身外，就在你本心之中；求理不必外驰，只需向内。**

由此生出他最著名的两个主张。其一是『知行合一』：真正的知，本身就含着行；一个人若真知道该孝、该善，就不会知而不做——知而不行，只说明他还没有真知。把知与行拆成两段、以为可以先知个透再去做，正是一切拖沓与自欺的根源。其二是『致良知』：每个人心里都本有一个能当下辨别是非善恶的『良知』，如同明镜；修养的全部功夫，不过是把这面被私欲遮蔽的镜子擦亮，并把它照见的东西切实做出来。

他特别强调『事上磨练』——功夫不在打坐空谈，而在具体事务的应对中磨。喜怒得失当前，正是练心的道场。这套学问把道德的根据从外在权威、经典条文，转回到每个普通人自己的良心，因而极具解放性：人人皆可为圣，圣人之道，吾性自足。它后来东传日本，深刻影响了近世东亚的精神世界。
wangyangming.ideas_en:
Wang Yangming's thought was a revolt against the Neo-Confucianism of Zhu Xi. Zhu taught 'investigating things to exhaust their principle' — seeking, item by item, the external 'principle' (li) in all things and affairs. As a young man Wang 'investigated' a stalk of bamboo for seven days and nights, and got from it a serious illness and a doubt: if principle lies outside the mind, a lifetime will never run it down. After his awakening at Longchang he offered another road: **'the mind is principle' — the principle of Heaven is not outside you but within your own original mind; to seek it, do not race outward but turn inward.**

From this grow his two most famous doctrines. First, the 'unity of knowing and acting': true knowing already contains action; a person who truly knows he should be filial or good will not know it and fail to act — to know and not act only shows he does not yet truly know. To split knowing from acting, imagining one may know thoroughly first and act later, is the very root of all procrastination and self-deception. Second, 'extending the innate conscience' (zhi liangzhi): everyone possesses within an innate moral knowing that discerns right from wrong in the moment, like a bright mirror; the whole work of cultivation is to polish this mirror clouded by selfish desire and to actually carry out what it reveals.

He stressed 'polishing oneself amid affairs' — the real work is not in silent meditation or empty talk but in the handling of concrete matters. Joy and anger, gain and loss before you are precisely the training ground for the mind. This teaching moves the ground of morality from external authority and canonical text back to the conscience of every ordinary person, and is thus deeply liberating: anyone can become a sage, for the way of the sage is complete within one's own nature. Later carried to Japan, it profoundly shaped the spiritual world of early-modern East Asia.

assessments.text: 在《明儒学案》中推尊阳明之学，谓有明一代学术，至白沙始入精微，至阳明而后大明，良知之说使圣学得以豁然。
极力表彰阳明知行合一之教，视其为救治空疏、砥砺意志、可以立身任事的活学问，倡以之振作国民精神。

assessments_en.text: In his Case Studies of Ming Confucians he exalts Yangming's learning, holding that the scholarship of the Ming reached subtlety with Chen Baisha and full brightness only with Yangming, whose doctrine of innate conscience opened up the sages' teaching.

He vigorously championed Yangming's unity of knowing and acting as a living learning that cures emptiness, tempers the will, and equips one to stand and take on affairs, calling for it to rouse the national spirit.

quotes: 知是行之始，行是知之成。
破山中贼易，破心中贼难。
圣人之道，吾性自足，向之求理于事物者误也。
你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂；你来看此花时，则此花颜色一时明白起来。
quotes_en: Knowing is the beginning of acting; acting is the completion of knowing.
To defeat the bandits in the mountains is easy; to defeat the bandit in the heart is hard.
The way of the sage is complete within my own nature; to have sought principle in external things was the error.
Before you looked at this flower, it and your mind were alike in stillness; when you came to look, its colors at once grew clear.
wangyangming.lineage: 上溯陆九渊『心即理』一脉，反朱熹理学而自成心学；门下分化为浙中、江右、泰州诸王学流派，泰州学派尤趋平民化。其学东传日本，形成阳明学，影响幕末志士；近世稻盛和夫等实业家亦奉为圭臬。
wangyangming.lineage_en: Tracing back to Lu Jiuyuan's 'the mind is principle,' he stood against Zhu Xi's Neo-Confucianism to found the School of Mind; his followers split into the Zhezhong, Jiangyou, and Taizhou branches, the Taizhou school turning especially toward the common people. His learning passed to Japan as Yōmeigaku, influencing late-Tokugawa reformers, and modern industrialists such as Inamori Kazuo have taken it as a guide.
wangyangming.trivia: 他不仅是书斋里的哲人，更是能征善战的统帅——曾以少胜多、仅用一月余平定宁王朱宸濠之乱，用兵诡谲，被赞『狡诈专兵』；这段以哲学家之身建立赫赫军功的经历，正是他『事上磨练』『知行合一』的亲身注脚。
wangyangming.trivia_en: He was no mere study-bound philosopher but a capable commander — with inferior numbers he put down the rebellion of the Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, in little more than a month, his tactics so cunning he was called a master of deception in war; this record of building brilliant military merit as a philosopher is the living footnote to his 'polishing oneself amid affairs' and 'unity of knowing and acting.'

jobs.bio: 1955–2011，美国企业家、苹果公司联合创始人，个人电脑、智能手机与数字媒体时代的关键塑造者。1976 年与沃兹尼亚克创立苹果，1985 年被逐出公司，创办 NeXT、收购并壮大皮克斯，1997 年回归苹果并带领其推出 iMac、iPod、iPhone、iPad，把濒临破产的苹果变为全球市值最高的公司之一。
jobs.bio_en: 1955–2011, an American entrepreneur and co-founder of Apple, a key shaper of the personal-computer, smartphone, and digital-media eras. He co-founded Apple with Wozniak in 1976, was forced out in 1985, founded NeXT and built up Pixar, then returned to Apple in 1997 and led it through the iMac, iPod, iPhone, and iPad, turning a near-bankrupt company into one of the most valuable in the world.
jobs.ideas:
乔布斯的核心信念可以浓缩成一句被他改写的话：『设计不只是它看起来怎样、感觉怎样，设计是它如何运作。』在他眼里，美不是表面装饰，而是把复杂的东西想透、再做到极简之后，自然浮现的结果。他对细节的偏执近乎传奇——连用户永远看不到的电路板内部，他也要求做得漂亮。
他反复强调『科技与人文的十字路口』：纯粹的工程师造得出强大的机器，却未必造得出人愿意爱的产品；苹果的差异，在于让技术服务于审美、直觉与情感。由此延伸出他著名的『聚焦』哲学——他回归苹果后大砍产品线，因为他相信『决定不做什么，和决定做什么同样重要』。
在用人上，他笃信『A 级人才』：第一流的人只愿与第一流的人共事，一旦放进平庸者，团队会逐级稀释。他用近乎苛刻的高标准逼出人们自己都不知道能达到的水准，称之为对人的尊重；但这也使他以暴躁、不留情面著称，是其管理风格中长期被争议的一面。
他还有一种罕见的、近乎艺术家的产品直觉：不靠用户调研，而是『为用户造出他们还不知道自己想要的东西』。这套方法极难复制——它依赖一个人对品味的极致自信，成也萧何、败也萧何。理解乔布斯，既要看到他点石成金的远见，也要看到这种风格对身边人的代价。
jobs.ideas_en:
Jobs's core belief can be compressed into a line he liked to reframe: 'Design is not just what it looks like and feels like; design is how it works.' To him, beauty was not surface decoration but what emerges naturally once you have thought a complex thing through and then made it ruthlessly simple. His obsession with detail was near-legendary, demanding that even the inside of a circuit board, which a user would never see, be made beautiful.
He stressed again and again 'the intersection of technology and the liberal arts': pure engineers can build powerful machines but not necessarily products people love, and Apple's difference was to put technology in the service of aesthetics, intuition, and feeling. From this flowed his famous philosophy of focus: after returning to Apple he cut the product line drastically, believing that 'deciding what not to do is as important as deciding what to do'.
On people he was a believer in 'A-players': the first-rate only want to work with the first-rate, and the moment mediocrity enters, a team dilutes level by level. He used standards harsh to the point of cruelty to pull from people a level they did not know they could reach, calling it a form of respect; but it also made him famous for being volatile and merciless, the long-contested side of his management style.
He also had a rare, almost artistic product intuition: rather than relying on user research, he aimed to 'make for users what they don't yet know they want'. This method is very hard to copy, resting on one person's extreme confidence in their own taste, which was both his making and his undoing. To understand Jobs is to see both his Midas-touch vision and the cost of that style on those around him.

assessments.text: 其授权传记作者艾萨克森评价：乔布斯把对完美的偏执与现实扭曲力场结合，既能激励团队做出不可能之事，也常因苛刻与情绪化伤害身边的人——是天才与难处并存的复杂人物（大意）。
长期对手兼同行盖茨曾表示，乔布斯在『品味、对人的本能判断和产品营销』上有近乎魔法般的天赋，是自己难以企及的（大意）。

assessments_en.text: His authorized biographer judged that Jobs fused a perfectionist obsession with a 'reality distortion field', able both to inspire teams to do the impossible and, through harshness and volatility, to wound those around him, a complex figure of genius and difficulty (paraphrased).
His longtime rival and peer remarked that Jobs had an almost magical gift for 'taste, an instinct for people, and product marketing' that he himself could not match (paraphrased).

quotes: 求知若饥，虚心若愚。（Stay hungry, stay foolish，2005 斯坦福毕业演讲）
你的时间有限，不要浪费时间活在别人的生活里。（2005 斯坦福毕业演讲）
专注与简单……一旦你抵达那里，便能撼动山岳。（大意）
quotes_en: Stay hungry, stay foolish. (2005 Stanford commencement address)
Your time is limited, so don't waste it living someone else's life. (2005 Stanford commencement address)
Focus and simplicity... once you get there, you can move mountains. (paraphrased)
jobs.lineage: 师法包豪斯与极简设计、禅宗美学与日本工艺，深受其早年印度之行与禅修影响；其产品哲学经由乔纳森·艾夫等设计师延续，并定义了此后整个消费电子与移动互联网时代的审美与交互范式。
jobs.lineage_en: He drew on Bauhaus and minimalist design, Zen aesthetics, and Japanese craft, deeply marked by his early trip to India and his Zen practice; his product philosophy carried on through designers such as Jony Ive and defined the aesthetic and interaction paradigm of the entire consumer-electronics and mobile-internet era that followed.
jobs.trivia: 乔布斯长期只穿黑色高领衫配牛仔裤，是有意为之的『个人制服』，以减少日常决策的消耗。他年轻时曾赴印度寻道、长期修习禅宗，这份对简约与专注的执念，深刻影响了苹果的产品哲学。
jobs.trivia_en: Jobs wore the same black turtleneck and jeans for years, a deliberate 'personal uniform' to cut the drain of daily decisions. In youth he traveled to India seeking the spiritual and practiced Zen for years, and this devotion to simplicity and focus deeply shaped Apple's product philosophy.

munger.bio: 1924–2023，美国投资家、律师，伯克希尔·哈撒韦公司副主席，沃伦·巴菲特长达数十年的事业搭档与思想挚友。早年从军、学法，后转向投资。他以渊博、犀利、毒舌的智慧著称，被巴菲特称为深刻影响了自己投资哲学的人。享年九十九岁。
munger.bio_en: 1924–2023, an American investor and lawyer, vice-chairman of Berkshire Hathaway, and for decades Warren Buffett's business partner and intellectual companion. He served in the military, trained in law, then turned to investing. Famous for erudite, sharp, acerbic wisdom, he was credited by Buffett with profoundly shaping his own investment philosophy. He lived to ninety-nine.
munger.ideas:
芒格最核心的主张，是建立一套跨学科的『思维模型格栅』。他打了个有名的比方：『在手里拿着锤子的人看来，全世界都像钉子。』只懂一门学科的人，会把所有问题都硬塞进自己那一套框架里。解药是去掌握各大学科（数学、物理、生物、心理、经济、历史）里真正重要的几十个基本模型，遇到问题时让它们交叉印证——这才接近世界本来的复杂样子。
他另一件招牌武器是『逆向思维』（反过来想）。与其拼命想『怎样才能成功』，不如先问『怎样会必败』，把通往灾难的路一条条找出来、避开。他常说：『我只想知道我将来会死在哪里，这样我就永远不去那儿。』在他看来，避免愚蠢，比追求聪明，回报高得多也可靠得多。
他极重视『能力圈』：诚实地知道自己懂什么、不懂什么，只在圈内下注，对圈外的诱惑坚决说不。配套的还有他对『激励』近乎执念的强调——『给我看激励机制，我就告诉你结果』。他认为人的行为绝大部分由所处的奖惩结构决定，所以设计制度时，第一要务是别让激励逼着好人做坏事。
这些看似投资和商业的智慧，本质是一套『如何少犯错地过一生』的实用理性。芒格反复推崇诚实、耐心、可靠这些『无聊的美德』，并尖锐批判嫉妒、自怜与意识形态。他的思想对管理者尤其有用：与其当个事必躬亲的聪明人，不如请来正直可靠的人、对齐激励、然后管住自己别添乱。
munger.ideas_en:
Munger's central proposal was to build a cross-disciplinary 'latticework of mental models'. He gave a famous analogy: 'To the man with only a hammer, every problem looks like a nail.' Someone who masters only one discipline forces every problem into that single frame. The remedy is to grasp the few dozen truly important basic models across the great disciplines (mathematics, physics, biology, psychology, economics, history) and let them cross-check one another when a problem arises, which comes closer to the world's actual complexity.
His other signature weapon was inversion (turning it around). Rather than strain to think 'how do I succeed', first ask 'how would I surely fail', and find and avoid each road to disaster. He often said, 'All I want to know is where I'm going to die, so I'll never go there.' To him, avoiding stupidity pays far better and far more reliably than chasing brilliance.
He prized the 'circle of competence': honestly knowing what you do and don't understand, betting only within the circle, and firmly saying no to temptations outside it. Alongside came his near-obsessive emphasis on incentives: 'Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.' He held that most behavior is decided by the surrounding structure of reward and punishment, so the first duty in designing a system is not to let incentives force good people into bad acts.
This seemingly investment-and-business wisdom is at bottom a practical rationality for 'how to go through life making fewer mistakes'. Munger repeatedly praised the 'boring virtues' of honesty, patience, and reliability, and sharply criticized envy, self-pity, and ideology. His thought is especially useful for managers: rather than be a clever person who does everything himself, hire upright, reliable people, align incentives, and then restrain yourself from meddling.

assessments.text: 巴菲特多次表示，芒格让自己从『以便宜价格买平庸公司』转向『以合理价格买伟大公司』，深刻改变了他的投资哲学，称其为最好的合伙人与老师（大意）。
该书汇编其演讲与格言，将芒格塑造为本杰明·富兰克林式的实用智者——以多元学科、逆向思维与道德常识，教人理性地避免愚蠢（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Buffett said repeatedly that Munger moved him from 'buying mediocre companies at cheap prices' to 'buying great companies at fair prices', profoundly changing his investment philosophy, and called him the best partner and teacher (paraphrased).

The volume gathering his speeches and maxims casts Munger as a Benjamin-Franklin-style practical sage who teaches one to rationally avoid stupidity through multiple disciplines, inversion, and moral common sense (paraphrased).

quotes: 给我看激励机制，我就告诉你结果。
反过来想，总是反过来想。（Invert, always invert.）
我这辈子遇到的聪明人，没有不每天阅读的——一个都没有。（大意）
quotes_en: Show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.
Invert, always invert.
In my whole life, I have known no wise people who didn't read all the time, none, zero. (paraphrased)
works: 历年伯克希尔股东大会问答
works_en: Berkshire annual-meeting Q&A over the years
munger.lineage: 承本杰明·富兰克林的实用理性与格言传统，融汇达尔文、亚当·斯密及现代心理学；与巴菲特共同塑造了价值投资的现代形态，其『多元思维模型』与『逆向思维』广泛影响投资界、商界与理性决策研究。
munger.lineage_en: He carried on Benjamin Franklin's tradition of practical reason and maxim, blending Darwin, Adam Smith, and modern psychology; together with Buffett he shaped the modern form of value investing, and his 'latticework of mental models' and 'inversion' widely influence investing, business, and the study of rational decision-making.
munger.trivia: 芒格年轻时遭遇离婚、幼子病逝、一只眼睛因手术并发症失明等接连打击，却始终以斯多葛式的坚韧面对，从不自怜。他酷爱建筑设计，曾亲自为大学设计宿舍楼；也是本杰明·富兰克林的终身崇拜者。
munger.trivia_en: In his youth Munger endured divorce, the death of a young son to leukemia, and the loss of an eye to surgical complications in succession, yet faced it all with Stoic toughness and never self-pity. He loved architecture and personally designed university dormitories, and was a lifelong admirer of Benjamin Franklin.

damasio.bio: 1944–，葡萄牙裔美国神经科学家，南加州大学脑与创造力研究所所长。以研究情绪、决策与意识的神经基础著称，通过对脑损伤病人的长期观察，挑战了『理性与情绪对立』的传统观念。著有《笛卡尔的错误》《感受发生的一切》等多部影响广泛的著作。
damasio.bio_en: Born 1944, a Portuguese-American neuroscientist and director of the Brain and Creativity Institute at the University of Southern California. Renowned for studying the neural basis of emotion, decision-making, and consciousness, he challenged the traditional opposition of reason and emotion through long observation of brain-damaged patients. He is the author of widely influential books including Descartes' Error and The Feeling of What Happens.
damasio.ideas:
达马西奥毕生反对一个根深蒂固的偏见：以为理性是高贵的、情绪是干扰理性的杂音，最好的决策应当『冷静而无情』。他的研究把这个观念彻底翻了过来。
关键证据来自他的脑损伤病人，尤其是一位被他称为现代『盖奇』的患者：手术切除了一小块负责连接情绪的脑区（腹内侧前额叶）后，这个人智商、记忆、逻辑全部正常，却变得无法做决定——哪怕只是选今天用哪支笔、约哪天见面，他都能没完没了地理性权衡，却迟迟定不下来。原来，情绪并非理性的敌人，而是帮我们在选项间『赋予权重、快速取舍』的关键机制；情绪一旦缺席，纯逻辑反而瘫痪。
由此他提出著名的『躯体标记假说』：过往的经验会把某种身体感受（比如一想到某选择就胃里发紧、心头一沉）和特定选项绑定，像给选项贴上情绪标签。当你面对复杂决定时，这些『躯体标记』会先于缜密推理，给你一个直觉性的趋避信号——那种『说不清但就是觉得不对』，往往是身体在替你预警。
他把这一切上升为对哲学的批判，即《笛卡尔的错误》：笛卡尔『我思故我在』把心灵与身体、理性与情感截然二分，是错的。在达马西奥看来，心智是从身体里长出来的，情绪、感受、意识都根植于维持生命的生理过程。这一思想深刻影响了管理、教育与人工智能：它提醒我们，一个忽视情绪与身体信号的『纯理性』组织或机器，恰恰会在真实决策上变得愚蠢。
damasio.ideas_en:
Damasio spent his career opposing a deep-seated bias: that reason is noble and emotion is noise interfering with it, and that the best decisions should be 'cool and unfeeling'. His research turned that idea completely around.
The key evidence came from his brain-damaged patients, especially one he likened to a modern Phineas Gage: after surgery removed a small region linking emotion (the ventromedial prefrontal cortex), the man's IQ, memory, and logic were all intact, yet he became unable to decide, weighing endlessly and rationally over even which pen to use today or which day to schedule a meeting, never settling. It turned out that emotion is not reason's enemy but the very mechanism that lets us 'assign weight and choose quickly' among options; remove emotion and pure logic itself seizes up.
From this he proposed the famous somatic marker hypothesis: past experience binds a bodily feeling (a tightening in the stomach, a sinking in the chest at the thought of some choice) to particular options, like an emotional tag. Facing a complex decision, these somatic markers fire ahead of careful reasoning and give you an intuitive approach-or-avoid signal, and that 'I can't say why but it just feels wrong' is often the body warning you in advance.
He raised all this into a critique of philosophy in Descartes' Error: Descartes' 'I think therefore I am', splitting mind from body and reason from feeling, is mistaken. For Damasio the mind grows out of the body, and emotion, feeling, and consciousness are all rooted in the physiology that sustains life. This thought has deeply influenced management, education, and artificial intelligence, warning us that a 'purely rational' organization or machine that ignores emotional and bodily signals becomes, precisely, stupid at real decisions.

assessments.text: 《笛卡尔的错误》被广泛评为以严谨的神经科学证据，优雅地重写了理性与情绪的关系，对心智哲学影响深远（大意）。
达马西奥的躯体标记假说被视为情感神经科学的奠基性贡献之一，虽具体机制仍有争论，但『情绪参与决策』已成主流共识（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Descartes' Error has been widely judged to rewrite, elegantly and on rigorous neuroscientific evidence, the relationship between reason and emotion, with deep influence on philosophy of mind (paraphrased).

Damasio's somatic marker hypothesis is regarded as a founding contribution to affective neuroscience; while its precise mechanism is still debated, 'emotion participates in decision-making' has become mainstream consensus (paraphrased).

quotes: 我们不是会思考的机器，我们是会感受的机器，恰好也会思考。
笛卡尔的错误，是把心灵与身体截然分开。（大意）
情绪是理性大厦的根基，而非它的对立面。（大意）
quotes_en: We are not thinking machines that feel; we are feeling machines that think.
Descartes' error was the abrupt separation of mind and body. (paraphrased)
Emotion is the foundation of the edifice of reason, not its opposite. (paraphrased)
damasio.lineage: 批判笛卡尔身心二元论，思想上亲近斯宾诺莎与威廉·詹姆斯的情绪理论；其工作奠定了情感神经科学，影响了具身认知、决策科学、行为经济学乃至情感计算与人工智能伦理的讨论。
damasio.lineage_en: Critiquing Cartesian dualism, he stands intellectually close to Spinoza and to William James's theory of emotion; his work founded affective neuroscience and shaped embodied cognition, decision science, behavioral economics, and debates in affective computing and the ethics of artificial intelligence.
damasio.trivia: 达马西奥常以十九世纪铁路工人菲尼亚斯·盖奇的著名病例开篇：一根铁棍穿过其前额叶后，盖奇智力如常，性情与决策能力却剧变——这成了情绪参与理性决策的经典证据。他与同为神经科学家的妻子汉娜·达马西奥长期合作研究。
damasio.trivia_en: Damasio often opens with the famous nineteenth-century case of the railway worker Phineas Gage: after an iron rod passed through his prefrontal lobe, Gage's intelligence was unchanged but his temperament and decision-making were transformed, a classic proof that emotion participates in rational decision. He has long collaborated with his wife, the neuroscientist Hanna Damasio.

covey.bio: 1932–2012，美国管理学家、教育家、演说家，全球畅销书《高效能人士的七个习惯》作者。该书自 1989 年出版以来售出数千万册，被译为数十种语言，深刻影响了现代领导力与个人成长领域。他拥有哈佛 MBA 与杨百翰大学博士学位，长期从事组织领导力培训。
covey.bio_en: 1932–2012, an American management thinker, educator, and speaker, author of the global bestseller The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People. Published in 1989, the book has sold tens of millions of copies in dozens of languages and deeply shaped modern leadership and personal-development thought. He held an MBA from Harvard and a doctorate from Brigham Young University, and spent his career in organizational leadership training.
covey.ideas:
柯维的出发点是一个尖锐的观察：市面上多数成功学只教『技巧』——如何说服、如何给人好印象、如何快速搞定。他称之为『个人魅力论』，并指出它治标不治本。真正可持续的效能，必须『由内而外』：先打磨内在的品格与原则，外在的方法才有根基。一个内心算计的人，再高超的沟通技巧也会被对方的直觉识破。
他把这套修炼组织成著名的『七个习惯』，分三个阶段。前三个走向『独立』：①积极主动——在刺激与回应之间，人永远有选择的自由，别把人生交给情绪和环境；②以终为始——先想清楚你真正要的结果（甚至你希望葬礼上别人怎么评价你），再倒推今天怎么做；③要事第一——按重要性而非紧急性安排时间，优先做那些不紧急却真正重要的事。
中间三个走向『互赖』，是其领导思想的精华：④双赢思维——把人际当成可以共同把饼做大的合作，而非你死我活；⑤知彼解己——先真正理解对方，再求被理解，这是多数人最缺的沟通习惯；⑥统合综效——尊重并融合差异，让合作产生『一加一大于二』的结果。第七个『不断更新』则贯穿始终：定期『磨刀』，在身体、心智、情感、精神四个维度自我修复。
柯维有一句广为流传的区分：『管理是把梯子爬得更快，领导是确认梯子搭对了墙。』他提醒人们，在拼命提升效率之前，先确认方向是对的——这对今天被各种效率工具裹挟、却忘了问『为什么』的人，格外有警醒意义。
covey.ideas_en:
Covey began from a sharp observation: most success literature teaches only technique, how to persuade, how to make a good impression, how to close fast. He called this the 'personality ethic' and argued it treats symptoms, not causes. Truly sustainable effectiveness must work 'inside-out': polish inner character and principles first, and only then do outer methods have a foundation. A person calculating within will have even the finest communication skill seen through by the other's intuition.
He organized this cultivation into the famous 'seven habits', in three stages. The first three move toward independence: (1) be proactive, since between stimulus and response a person always has the freedom to choose, so don't hand your life to mood and circumstance; (2) begin with the end in mind, first clarifying the result you truly want (even how you wish to be remembered at your funeral) and working back to what to do today; (3) put first things first, arranging time by importance rather than urgency and prioritizing what is not urgent yet truly matters.
The middle three move toward interdependence and are the heart of his leadership thought: (4) think win-win, treating relationships as cooperation that can grow the pie together rather than a zero-sum fight; (5) seek first to understand, then to be understood, the communication habit most people most lack; (6) synergize, respecting and combining differences so cooperation yields 'one plus one is greater than two'. The seventh, 'sharpen the saw', runs throughout: renew yourself regularly across the physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual dimensions.
Covey offered a widely quoted distinction: 'Management is climbing the ladder of success faster; leadership is making sure the ladder is leaning against the right wall.' He reminds us to confirm the direction is right before straining to raise efficiency, a warning with special force for people today swept along by productivity tools yet forgetting to ask 'why'.

assessments.text: 《时代》将柯维评为 1996 年全美最具影响力的二十五人之一，肯定其在领导力与个人成长领域的广泛影响（大意）。
评论者普遍认为《七个习惯》的贡献在于把零散的成功建议整合为一套以原则与品格为根基的系统框架，但也有人批评其内容偏常识、缺乏严格实证（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Time named Covey one of the twenty-five most influential Americans of 1996, recognizing his broad influence in leadership and personal development (paraphrased).

Reviewers generally credit The 7 Habits with integrating scattered success advice into a systematic framework grounded in principle and character, while some criticize it as commonsensical and lacking rigorous empirical support (paraphrased).

quotes: 管理是把梯子爬得更快，领导是确认梯子搭对了墙。（大意）
在刺激与回应之间，存在着空间；我们成长与自由的力量，正在这空间里的选择。（大意）
先去理解，再求被理解。
quotes_en: Management is climbing the ladder of success faster; leadership is making sure the ladder is leaning against the right wall. (paraphrased)
Between stimulus and response there is a space; in that space lies our freedom and power to choose, and in our choices lie our growth. (paraphrased)
Seek first to understand, then to be understood.
works_en: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People
covey.lineage: 思想上融汇富兰克林式的品格修养传统、亚里士多德的德性伦理与基督教信仰；其原则中心领导学影响了此后数十年的企业培训、教练文化与个人成长产业，与德鲁克等管理思想家并称大众领导力的奠基者之一。
covey.lineage_en: Intellectually he blended a Franklin-style tradition of character cultivation, Aristotelian virtue ethics, and Christian faith; his principle-centered leadership shaped decades of corporate training, coaching culture, and the personal-development industry, ranking alongside thinkers like Drucker as a founder of popular leadership thought.
covey.trivia: 柯维育有九个子女、数十名孙辈，常以家庭生活作为讲授原则的鲜活案例。他笃信终身学习，晚年仍坚持锻炼与写作；2012 年因骑自行车摔伤并发症去世。其著作长年位居全球商业畅销榜，影响遍及企业、学校与政府。
covey.trivia_en: Covey raised nine children and dozens of grandchildren, often drawing on family life as vivid case material for teaching principles. A believer in lifelong learning, he kept exercising and writing into old age, and died in 2012 from complications of a bicycle fall. His books remained on global business bestseller lists for years, with influence reaching companies, schools, and governments.

epictetus.bio: 约公元 50–135 年，古罗马斯多葛派哲学家。出身为奴，少年时在罗马为奴隶，后获自由，在希腊尼科波利斯开学授徒。他本人一字未留，今天读到的《谈话录》与《手册》都由学生阿里安记录整理。
epictetus.bio_en: c. 50–135 CE, a Roman Stoic philosopher. Born into slavery, he spent his youth as a slave in Rome, was later freed, and opened a school in Nicopolis in Greece. He wrote nothing himself; the Discourses and the Enchiridion (Handbook) we read today were recorded by his student Arrian.
epictetus.ideas:
爱比克泰德的整套哲学，可以浓缩成开篇那句话：世上的事分两类，一类「由得了我们」，一类「由不得我们」。由得了我们的，是我们的判断、意愿、欲求与回避——也就是「我怎么看、怎么选、怎么回应」；由不得我们的，是身体、财产、名声、地位、别人怎么待我、明天会不会下雨。他把这叫「控制二分法」。痛苦的根源，几乎总是我们把心思押在了「由不得我们」的那一堆上：想控制控制不了的，于是焦虑、愤怒、患得患失。把注意力收回到「由得了我们」的那一小块，人反而自由了。
这里有个关键转折：让我们难受的，往往不是事情本身，而是我们对事情的判断。「有人骂你」是中性的事件，真正刺痛你的，是你心里那句「他不该这样对我、这太羞辱了」。斯多葛叫这个内在的评判机能 prohairesis（意愿/抉择）——它才是真正属于你、谁也夺不走的东西。改判断，就能改感受；这一思路两千年后被现代认知行为疗法(CBT)直接继承。
爱比克泰德最戳当代人的，是他对「知道却做不到」的态度：哲学不是拿来谈的，是拿来练的。他讥讽那些把斯多葛理论背得滚瓜烂熟、一遇事却原形毕露的学生——「别再空谈你信奉什么，把它活出来给我看」。在他眼里，懂得道理只是第一步，真正算数的是 askēsis（操练）：像运动员一样，在一次次小事上反复演练「分清能控制的与不能控制的、守住自己的判断」，直到它成为临场的本能。他还有个生动的提醒：每天可以先「预演逆境」——出门前想一想可能遇到的添堵、刁难、损失，心里先过一遍，真碰上时就不至于乱了阵脚。
他出身奴隶、腿有残疾、一生清贫，却把斯多葛讲得格外接地气——因为他谈的不是书斋里的玄理，而是一个曾经连人身自由都没有的人，如何在最不由自己的处境里，守住那块谁也拿不走的内在自由。
epictetus.ideas_en:
Epictetus's whole philosophy can be compressed into his opening line: things fall into two kinds — those that are "up to us" and those that are "not up to us." Up to us are our judgments, will, desires, and aversions — how we see, choose, and respond. Not up to us are the body, property, reputation, status, how others treat us, whether it rains tomorrow. He calls this the "dichotomy of control." The root of suffering is almost always that we stake our minds on the pile that is not up to us: we try to control the uncontrollable, and so we churn with anxiety, anger, and clinging. Pull your attention back to the small zone that is genuinely yours, and you become free.
Here is the key pivot: what disturbs us is usually not the thing itself but our judgment about it. "Someone insulted you" is a neutral event; what stings is the line in your head — "he shouldn't treat me this way, this is humiliating." The Stoics call this inner faculty of judgment and choice prohairesis — the one thing that is truly yours and that no one can take. Change the judgment and you change the feeling; two thousand years later this idea was inherited directly by modern cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
What speaks most sharply to us today is his stance on "knowing yet not doing": philosophy is not for discussing, it is for training. He mocked students who could recite Stoic theory flawlessly yet fell apart at the first setback — "don't tell me what you believe, show me by living it." In his eyes, understanding the principle is only step one; what counts is askēsis (practice): like an athlete, you rehearse "separate what you can control from what you can't, and hold your own judgment" over and over in small moments, until it becomes instinct under pressure. He offered a vivid drill: each morning, rehearse adversity in advance — picture the hassles, slights, and losses the day might bring, run through them in your mind, so that when they actually come you are not thrown.
Born a slave, lame in one leg, poor all his life, he made Stoicism unusually down-to-earth — because he was not spinning study-room abstractions but showing how a man who once lacked even bodily freedom could, in the least free of circumstances, hold onto the one inner freedom no one can seize.

assessments.text: 罗马皇帝在自己的私人札记里多次援引爱比克泰德，把他列为对自己影响最深的精神导师之一。
CBT/REBT 公开把『困扰我们的不是事情，而是我们对事情的看法』追溯到爱比克泰德，视其为认知疗法的古代先声。

assessments_en.text: In his private notebooks the Roman emperor repeatedly draws on Epictetus, naming him among the spiritual teachers who shaped him most.
CBT and REBT openly trace the principle 'it is not things that disturb us but our judgments about them' back to Epictetus, treating him as an ancient forerunner of cognitive therapy.

quotes: 困扰人的不是事情本身，而是人对事情的看法。
别再空谈你信奉的哲学，把它活出来。（大意）
quotes_en: Men are disturbed not by things, but by the views they take of things.
Don't explain your philosophy. Embody it. (paraphrased)
epictetus.lineage: 上承芝诺、克律西波斯开创的斯多葛学派，师从穆索尼乌斯·鲁弗斯；下启马可·奥勒留，并经由蒙田、现代 CBT 一路影响至今。
epictetus.lineage_en: He stands in the Stoic line founded by Zeno and Chrysippus, having studied under Musonius Rufus; he in turn shaped Marcus Aurelius, and his influence runs on through Montaigne to modern CBT.
epictetus.trivia: 他终身未婚、生活极简，晚年才收养了一个差点被遗弃的孩子；据传一条腿有残疾（一说为奴时被折磨所致），他却以此平静示人，正是『接受由不得自己的事』的活注脚。
epictetus.trivia_en: He never married and lived with extreme simplicity, adopting a child late in life who would otherwise have been left to die. He was said to be lame in one leg (by one account from mistreatment in slavery), which he bore with calm — a living footnote to his own teaching of accepting what is not up to us.

thaler.bio: 理查德·塞勒（Richard H. Thaler，1945– ），美国经济学家，芝加哥大学布斯商学院教授，行为经济学的奠基人之一，2017 年获诺贝尔经济学奖。他毕生把心理学的真实人性引入经济学，挑战『理性经济人』的假设，著有《助推》（与桑斯坦合著）、《错误的行为》等，并把研究成果化为影响各国公共政策的『助推』实践。
thaler.bio_en: Richard H. Thaler (born 1945) is an American economist, professor at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, a founder of behavioral economics, and the 2017 Nobel laureate in Economics. He spent his career bringing the real psychology of human beings into economics, challenging the assumption of the 'rational economic man,' authoring Nudge (with Cass Sunstein) and Misbehaving, and turning his research into 'nudge' practices that have shaped public policy around the world.
thaler.ideas:
传统经济学假设人是理性的：会算清成本收益、意志坚定、追求自身长远利益最大化。塞勒的一生工作，就是用大量证据说明这个假设错在哪里——**真实的人不是抽象的『经济人』，而是会犯系统性错误的普通人。他戏称前者为 Econs、后者为 Humans，而经济学该研究的是 Humans。**

他揭示了许多可预测的『非理性』。比如『心理账户』：同样一笔钱，人会因为它来自工资还是奖金、装在哪个信封里，而花得完全不同。比如『禀赋效应』：一件东西一旦归你所有，你就会高估它的价值，卖价远高于买价。还有『现在偏误』：人严重偏爱眼前，对当下的成本和快感估得过高、对未来的估得过低，于是明知有益的事（存钱、健身、体检）一再推迟——这正是拖延、储蓄不足等现象的根源。

塞勒的过人之处，是把这些洞察变成温和而有效的解决方案，即『助推』（nudge）。其核心思想叫『自由主义的温和家长制』：不禁止、不强迫、不改变任何人的选项，只是聪明地重新安排『选择架构』，让人更容易做出对自己有利的选择。最著名的例子是把退休金储蓄计划从『想参加要主动登记』改为『默认参加、想退出可退出』——仅仅改变默认项，参与率就大幅提升。他还倡导承诺机制：让人预先给未来的自己设下约束（自动扣款、有代价的期限）。这套思想说明：与其苛责人不够自律，不如改良他所处的环境。
thaler.ideas_en:
Traditional economics assumes people are rational: they reckon costs and benefits clearly, hold firm to their will, and maximize their own long-term interest. Thaler's life's work marshals evidence for where this assumption goes wrong — **real people are not the abstract 'economic man' but ordinary humans who make systematic errors. He jokingly calls the former 'Econs' and the latter 'Humans,' and insists economics should study Humans.**

He revealed many predictable 'irrationalities.' 'Mental accounting': the very same money is spent quite differently depending on whether it came from salary or a bonus, or which envelope it sits in. The 'endowment effect': once something is yours, you overvalue it, your selling price far above your buying price. And 'present bias': people heavily favor the here and now, overrating present costs and pleasures and underrating future ones, so that beneficial things known to matter — saving, exercise, checkups — are deferred again and again, the very root of procrastination and under-saving.

Thaler's genius was to turn these insights into gentle, effective solutions: the 'nudge.' Its core idea is 'libertarian paternalism' — forbidding nothing, forcing nothing, removing no one's options, but cleverly rearranging the 'choice architecture' so people more easily make choices good for themselves. The most famous example switched retirement-savings plans from 'opt in if you want to join' to 'enrolled by default, opt out if you wish' — merely changing the default sharply raised participation. He also champions commitment devices: letting people set constraints in advance on their future selves (automatic deductions, deadlines with a cost). The lesson: rather than scold people for insufficient discipline, improve the environment they act in.

assessments.by: 诺贝尔经济学奖委员会
assessments.text: 2017 年授奖时评价塞勒『把心理学上现实的假设融入经济决策分析』，在有限理性、社会偏好与缺乏自控等方面架起心理学与经济学的桥梁。
这位行为经济学的另一奠基者与塞勒长期合作，称其最大贡献在于坚持不懈地让经济学正视真实的人，而非理想化的理性主体。

assessments_en.text: In awarding the 2017 prize it credited Thaler with 'incorporating psychologically realistic assumptions into analyses of economic decision-making,' bridging psychology and economics on bounded rationality, social preferences, and lack of self-control.

The fellow founder of behavioral economics, a longtime collaborator, held that Thaler's great contribution was his relentless insistence that economics face real humans rather than idealized rational agents.

quotes: 如果你想让人做一件事，就把它变得容易。（大意）
我们无法把人变得理性，但可以把选择环境设计得更友善。（大意）
我研究的对象是『人类』，不是经济学教科书里那种『经济人』。（大意）
quotes_en: If you want people to do something, make it easy. (paraphrased)
We cannot make people rational, but we can design the choice environment to be kinder. (paraphrased)
My subject is Humans, not the 'Econs' of the economics textbook. (paraphrased)
thaler.lineage: 承接卡尼曼与特沃斯基的判断与决策心理学，将其系统引入经济学，与桑斯坦共同开创『助推』与行为公共政策；影响遍及各国政府设立的『行为洞察团队』。
thaler.lineage_en: Building on the judgment-and-decision psychology of Kahneman and Tversky, he brought it systematically into economics and, with Sunstein, launched 'nudge' and behavioral public policy, influencing 'behavioral insights teams' set up by governments worldwide.
thaler.trivia: 塞勒在电影《大空头》里客串本色出演，用赌场里的『热手谬误』向观众解释金融泡沫；他也常自嘲是个懒散、爱走捷径的人，正因如此才对普通人的种种『不理性』感同身受。
thaler.trivia_en: Thaler made a cameo as himself in the film The Big Short, using the casino 'hot-hand fallacy' to explain financial bubbles to the audience; he also often jokes that he is a lazy man fond of shortcuts, which is exactly why he feels such kinship with ordinary people's many 'irrationalities.'

wood.bio: 温迪·伍德（Wendy Wood），美国社会心理学家，南加州大学（USC）心理学与商学教授，是习惯科学领域最具影响力的研究者之一。她以数十年实验研究揭示人类行为中『习惯』所占的巨大比重及其运作机制，著有面向大众的《习惯心理学》（Good Habits, Bad Habits, 2019），把学界成果转译为普通人可用的行为改变方法。
wood.bio_en: Wendy Wood is an American social psychologist and Provost Professor of Psychology and Business at the University of Southern California, one of the most influential researchers in the science of habit. Over decades of experimental work she has documented how large a share of human behavior is habitual and how habits operate, and in her general-audience book Good Habits, Bad Habits (2019) she translated the field's findings into methods for behavior change that ordinary people can use.
wood.ideas:
伍德研究的核心发现，颠覆了我们对自我掌控的直觉：**我们的日常行为中，有相当大一部分（她的研究估计约四成）不是当下有意识决定的，而是习惯——由环境线索自动触发的、无需思考的反应。**你走进厨房就打开冰箱，坐上沙发就摸手机，很多时候并没有真正『决定』要这么做。

她由此解释了一个常见的困惑：为什么『下决心』总是失败。因为意志力和动机是一种昂贵、易耗、随情绪波动的资源，一旦疲惫、分心或压力大，它就先撤退，而旧习惯依然稳稳运转。真正长期塑造行为的，不是一时的决心，而是三个要素的反复配合：稳定的情境线索、顺畅的重复、以及及时的奖赏。习惯一旦养成，就把行为从『意志的战场』转移到『自动的轨道』上。

这带来一个极其务实、也极具解放性的结论：与其苛责自己不够自律，不如去改造环境。想多做的事，就减少它的『摩擦』——把它变得触手可及、门槛极低；想少做的事，就增加摩擦——让它变麻烦、离得远。把健康的选择设成默认，把诱惑藏起来。她强调，持久的改变靠的不是更强的意志，而是更聪明的设计——让好行为变得几乎不必用力，坏行为变得费力。
wood.ideas_en:
Wood's central finding overturns our intuition about self-control: **a sizable share of our daily behavior — her research estimates around 40% — is not a conscious present decision but habit, an automatic, thoughtless response triggered by environmental cues.** You walk into the kitchen and open the fridge, sit on the couch and reach for the phone, often without truly 'deciding' to.

This explains a familiar puzzle: why 'resolving to change' so often fails. Willpower and motivation are an expensive, depletable resource that swings with mood; the moment you are tired, distracted, or stressed, it retreats first, while old habits keep running smoothly. What shapes behavior over the long run is not a burst of resolve but the repeated interplay of three elements: a stable context cue, frictionless repetition, and timely reward. Once formed, a habit moves behavior off the 'battlefield of the will' and onto an 'automatic track.'

This yields a deeply practical and liberating conclusion: rather than berate yourself for insufficient discipline, redesign the environment. For what you want to do more, cut its 'friction' — make it within arm's reach, the threshold near zero; for what you want to do less, add friction — make it a nuisance, keep it far away. Set the healthy choice as the default and hide the temptation. Lasting change, she stresses, rests not on stronger willpower but on smarter design — making good behavior nearly effortless and bad behavior effortful.

assessments.text: 在畅销书《掌控习惯》中大量引用伍德的研究，作为『环境与线索胜过意志』这一核心主张的科学依据。
普遍将伍德视为把『习惯自动性』从理论概念转化为可测量、可干预的实验对象的关键推动者，其情境-重复-奖赏框架被广泛用于健康与公共政策研究。

assessments_en.text: His bestseller Atomic Habits draws heavily on Wood's research as the scientific basis for its core claim that environment and cues outweigh willpower.

The field widely regards Wood as a key figure in turning 'habit automaticity' from a theoretical notion into a measurable, interveneable experimental subject, her cue–repetition–reward framework broadly applied in health and public-policy research.

quotes: 习惯，是我们为应对反复出现的情境而存下的一份行为记忆。（大意）
要改变行为，先改变你身处的情境，而不是先改变你的决心。（大意）
意志力是留给紧要关头的稀缺品；日常要靠的是习惯。（大意）
quotes_en: A habit is a memory of behavior we store up to meet a recurring situation. (paraphrased)
To change behavior, change the situation you are in before you try to change your resolve. (paraphrased)
Willpower is a scarce reserve for critical moments; day to day, we run on habit. (paraphrased)
works: 关于习惯自动性与情境线索的系列实证论文
works_en: A series of empirical papers on habit automaticity and context cues
wood.lineage: 承接从威廉·詹姆斯论习惯、到行为主义、再到当代社会认知心理学的脉络，与 B.J. 福格、查尔斯·杜希格、詹姆斯·克利尔等共同推动了近二十年的『习惯科学』大众化。
wood.lineage_en: She carries a line running from William James on habit, through behaviorism, to contemporary social-cognitive psychology, and together with B. J. Fogg, Charles Duhigg, and James Clear has driven the popularization of 'habit science' over the past two decades.
wood.trivia: 伍德常提醒读者一个反直觉的事实：那些看起来最自律、最有毅力的人，研究发现他们其实并不比别人更能『抵抗诱惑』——他们只是把生活安排得很少遇到诱惑。自律的真相，往往是环境，而非意志。
wood.trivia_en: Wood often reminds readers of a counterintuitive fact: the people who look most disciplined turn out, in studies, to be no better at 'resisting temptation' than anyone else — they have simply arranged their lives to meet temptation rarely. The truth of self-discipline is often environment, not will.

beauvoir.bio: 1908–1986，法国存在主义哲学家、作家、女性主义理论家。生于巴黎天主教中产家庭，索邦大学哲学高材生，在备考最高教师资格考试（agrégation）时认识萨特，二人结成终身的开放式伴侣关系。1949 年出版《第二性》，成为现代女性主义的奠基之作。她拒绝只被当作『萨特的伴侣』，是 20 世纪最重要的哲学家与公共知识分子之一。
beauvoir.bio_en: 1908–1986, a French existentialist philosopher, writer, and feminist theorist. Born in Paris to a Catholic middle-class family, she was a brilliant philosophy student at the Sorbonne; while preparing for the agrégation she met Sartre, with whom she formed a lifelong open partnership. Her 1949 book The Second Sex became a founding work of modern feminism. Refusing to be seen merely as "Sartre's companion," she stands among the most important philosophers and public intellectuals of the twentieth century.
beauvoir.ideas:
波伏娃把存在主义的核心命题——『存在先于本质』，人没有被预先写定的本质，而是通过选择不断造就自己——推到了它最尖锐的社会处境里。她最著名的一句话是：『女人不是天生的，而是后天被塑造成的。』意思是：『女性气质』不是生理决定的命运，而是社会一层层教化、规训出来的角色。这一句把『天经地义』变成了『历史造物』，也就把它变成了可以质疑、可以改变的东西。
在《第二性》里她提出一个贯穿全书的结构：男性被设为『主体』（自我、标准、普遍的人），女性则被设为『他者』（the Other）——被定义、被观看、被当作相对于男人而存在的第二性。她追问：女性如何一步步被困在『内在性』（internal、重复、依附的生活）里，而被剥夺了通往『超越性』（transcendence、去开创、去行动、去自我实现）的机会。她的解放主张不是让女人变成男人，而是让女人也能成为自由的、自我筹划的主体。
在伦理学上（《模糊性的伦理学》），她不接受『既然没有上帝、一切皆虚无』的虚无主义。她认为：正因为人是自由的、生命是有限的、没有现成答案，我们才必须为自己和彼此的自由负责——真正的伦理，是在承认这种『模糊与不确定』的前提下，仍然选择投身、行动、对他人的自由负责。晚年她又写《论老年》，揭露社会如何把老人推入沉默与无用，是最早严肃对待衰老处境的哲学著作之一。
beauvoir.ideas_en:
Beauvoir pushed existentialism's core claim—"existence precedes essence," the idea that we have no pre-written nature but make ourselves through our choices—into its sharpest social setting. Her most famous line is: "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman." Femininity, she argued, is not a biological destiny but a role drilled in, layer by layer, by society. That single sentence turns what looks "natural and self-evident" into a historical product—and therefore into something that can be questioned and changed.
In The Second Sex she lays out a structure that runs through the whole book: man is set up as the "Subject" (the self, the norm, the universal human), while woman is cast as the "Other"—defined, looked at, existing only relative to man, the second sex. She asks how women come to be trapped in "immanence" (a repetitive, dependent life) and denied access to "transcendence" (the freedom to initiate, to act, to realize oneself). Her call for liberation is not for women to become men, but for women, too, to become free, self-projecting subjects.
In ethics (The Ethics of Ambiguity) she refused the nihilist conclusion that "since there is no God, nothing matters." Precisely because we are free, life is finite, and there are no ready-made answers, she held, we are responsible for our own freedom and for one another's. Genuine ethics means choosing to commit and to act while owning that ambiguity. Late in life she wrote The Coming of Age, exposing how society pushes the old into silence and uselessness—one of the first philosophical works to take aging seriously.

assessments.by: 对第二波女性主义的影响
assessments.text: 《第二性》被公认为现代女性主义的奠基文本，深刻影响了贝蒂·弗里丹、凯特·米利特乃至后来的朱迪斯·巴特勒（性别『操演』论可上溯她『成为女人』的洞见）；尽管出版时曾被梵蒂冈列入禁书目录、并遭右翼猛烈攻击。

assessments.by: 长期被低估的哲学原创性
assessments.text: 她生前常被定位为萨特思想的『追随者』；但后世研究（如对《模糊性的伦理学》《皮洛士与西涅阿斯》的重估）日益指出，她在伦理与他者问题上有独立且早于萨特的贡献，是不折不扣的一流哲学家。
