第二把钥匙，是他最有名的概念——**大陆的轴线走向。**欧亚大陆是东西横展的，同一条纬度上气候相近，一种作物、一头牲畜、一项技术、一套文字，能沿着这条带子一路传播上万里；而美洲和非洲是南北纵展的，跨越赤道与不同气候带，作物和牲畜寸步难行，各地只能各自摸索、难以互通。这一横一纵，几千年下来就拉开了巨大的差距。
第三，是**病菌。**长期与牲畜共处的欧亚人，在瘟疫中反复淘洗，携带了天花、麻疹等一身抗体；当他们跨海而来，真正为他们征服美洲的，与其说是枪炮，不如说是随身携带、却对当地人致命的病菌。
把这些拼起来，戴蒙德给出一个冷峻的图景：不同文明的成就差异，追到最根上，是农业起步的早晚、传播的难易、病菌的有无——而这些又都由地理与生态的初始禀赋决定。他并不否认文化、观念、个人会在其间起作用，但坚持这些是在地理划定的大框架内起作用。他的立场常被批评为『地理决定论』过强、低估了人的能动性；但他真正想钉死的，是那个更坏的替代解释——把强弱之别说成血统与智力之别。理解了这一点，才理解他为何写得如此执拗。
diamond.ideas_en:
Diamond spent his life wrestling with one thought: that people too easily attribute the winners and losers of history to certain peoples being 'innately smarter, more industrious, superior.' He held this thought both false and dangerous — the oldest breeding ground of racism. What he set out to do was to find an honest explanation, one owing nothing to racial endowment, for why some societies produced guns and steel while others still used stone tools.
His answer: **look to geography, not race.** It all begins with agriculture. Farming let populations cluster and support specialist classes freed from producing food — bureaucrats, artisans, soldiers, priests — and only then did civilization have a starting point. Whether a region developed agriculture early depended on whether it had 'domesticable' plants and animals at hand: large-grained, high-yield, easily grown wild cereals, and docile large mammals that could be penned and herded. This was pure luck: the Fertile Crescent happened to hold wheat, barley, sheep, goats and cattle all at once, and started thousands of years ahead; most of the world simply held no good cards to domesticate.
The second key is his most famous idea — **the axis orientation of continents.** Eurasia spreads east-west, so along a single latitude the climate is similar and a crop, a beast, a technology, a writing system could travel that belt for thousands of miles; the Americas and Africa spread north-south, across the equator and through different climate zones, so crops and livestock could barely move and each region had to grope forward on its own, cut off from the rest. Over millennia, that one horizontal and one vertical opened an enormous gap.
Third, **germs.** Eurasians, long living alongside livestock and repeatedly winnowed by plagues, carried antibodies to smallpox, measles and more; when they crossed the seas, what truly conquered the Americas for them was less the gun than the germs they carried, harmless to themselves yet lethal to the native peoples.
Put it together and Diamond offers a cold picture: the differences in civilizations' achievements, traced to the root, come down to how early agriculture started, how easily things spread, and the presence or absence of germs — all in turn decided by the initial endowment of geography and ecology. He does not deny that culture, ideas and individuals play a part, but insists they play it within the large frame geography has drawn. His stance is often criticized as too strong a 'geographic determinism' that underrates human agency; but what he really means to nail shut is the worse alternative — explaining strength and weakness as a matter of bloodline and intelligence. Grasp this, and you grasp why he writes with such stubbornness.

assessments.text: 称《枪炮、病菌与钢铁》是『一部里程碑式的著作』，以宏阔的跨学科视野，为人类不平等的起源提供了一个有力而非种族主义的解释。

assessments.by: 批评者（部分历史学家与人类学家）
assessments.text: 批评其『地理决定论』过强，低估了文化、制度与人的能动性，并有将复杂历史简化为环境单因的倾向。

assessments_en.by: The New York Times Book Review
assessments_en.text: Called Guns, Germs, and Steel 'a landmark work,' offering, through a sweeping interdisciplinary lens, a powerful and non-racist account of the origins of human inequality.
Fault its 'geographic determinism' as too strong, underrating culture, institutions and human agency, and tending to reduce complex history to a single environmental cause.

quotes: 历史的不同进程，源于各民族所处环境的差异，而非各民族在生物学上的差异。
在能够写字之前，人类已经存在了数百万年。
健康社会的标志之一，是它愿意重新审视自己最珍视的核心价值，并在必要时加以改变。
quotes_en: History followed different courses for different peoples because of differences among peoples' environments, not because of biological differences among peoples themselves.
Humans existed for millions of years before the first written record.
One of the hallmarks of a healthy society is its willingness to re-examine, and if necessary change, its most cherished core values.
works: 《崩溃：社会如何选择成败兴亡》
《剧变：人类社会与国家危机的转折点》
works_en: Collapse: How Societies Choose to Fail or Succeed
Upheaval: Turning Points for Nations in Crisis
diamond.lineage: 他的思路上承生物地理学与生态学传统，把达尔文式的演化视角推广到人类社会的宏观历史；与孟德斯鸠的气候论、伊本·赫勒敦的环境史观遥相呼应，又与马克思『物质基础决定』的唯物史观在气质上相邻。他影响了尤瓦尔·赫拉利《人类简史》等一批大历史写作，也成为『地理决定论 vs 文化／观念史观』这场持久论战中最响亮的一方。
diamond.lineage_en: His approach descends from the traditions of biogeography and ecology, extending a Darwinian evolutionary lens to the macro-history of human societies; it echoes Montesquieu's climate theory and Ibn Khaldun's environmental history from afar, and stands temperamentally near Marx's materialist conception that the material base is decisive. He influenced a wave of big-history writing, including Yuval Harari's Sapiens, and became the loudest voice on one side of the enduring dispute between 'geographic determinism' and the history of culture and ideas.
diamond.trivia: 他能说十余种语言，早年为研究新几内亚鸟类而反复深入雨林，据说《枪炮、病菌与钢铁》的最初问题，正来自一位新几内亚政治家亚力的发问：『为什么你们白人有这么多货物，我们新几内亚人却几乎没有？』这句话被他放在书的开篇，成为全书的引线。
diamond.trivia_en: He speaks over a dozen languages and, in his early years, repeatedly ventured deep into the rainforest to study the birds of New Guinea. The founding question of Guns, Germs, and Steel is said to have come from a New Guinean politician named Yali, who asked: 'Why is it that you white people have so much cargo, but we New Guineans have so little?' Diamond placed the question at the book's opening, where it becomes the thread running through the whole work.

ibnkhaldun.bio: 伊本·赫勒敦（1332–1406），中世纪北非的阿拉伯史学家、政治家与思想家，生于突尼斯一个安达卢西亚裔的显贵之家。他一生在北非与安达卢西亚的各个王朝间辗转任职——做过大臣、法官、外交使节，几度卷入宫廷倾轧、身陷囹圄，又曾深入柏柏尔部落，亲历游牧与城市两种世界。这段动荡的仕途，成了他观察王朝兴衰的第一手素材。1377 年，他在一座城堡中闭关数月，写下巨著《历史绪论》(Muqaddima)——本意是为一部世界史作导论，却意外奠定了历史哲学与社会学的雏形。晚年他移居开罗讲学、任大法官，并曾与征服者帖木儿会面。
ibnkhaldun.bio_en: Ibn Khaldun (1332–1406) was a medieval North African Arab historian, statesman and thinker, born in Tunis into a distinguished family of Andalusian descent. He served across the various dynasties of North Africa and Andalusia — as minister, judge and diplomatic envoy — repeatedly caught up in court intrigue and even imprisoned, and he also lived among the Berber tribes, experiencing both the nomadic and the urban worlds firsthand. This turbulent career became his primary material for observing the rise and fall of dynasties. In 1377, secluded for several months in a castle, he wrote his masterwork, the Muqaddima ('Prolegomena') — intended as an introduction to a universal history, it unexpectedly laid the seeds of the philosophy of history and of sociology. In his later years he settled in Cairo to teach and serve as chief judge, and once met the conqueror Timur.
ibnkhaldun.ideas:
伊本·赫勒敦想做一件在他那个时代近乎超前的事：把历史当成一门可以探因求律的**科学**，而不只是帝王将相的编年流水账。他要问的不是『发生了什么』，而是『为什么王朝总是逃不过兴起、鼎盛、腐朽、覆灭这条曲线』。
他的答案，围绕一个核心概念——**『asabiyya』，通常译作『团结』或『群体凝聚力』。**它指的是一群人同心协力、彼此效忠、愿为集体牺牲的那股黏合之力。他敏锐地发现：这股力量在**艰苦的环境里最强。**荒漠与草原上的游牧部落，物质匮乏、时刻要抵御外敌，逼得族人必须紧紧抱团，于是练出了最强悍的凝聚力与最能吃苦的身体。
接着是他最精彩的洞察：**凝聚力会转化为权力，而权力又会腐蚀凝聚力。**拥有强大 asabiyya 的部落，能凭这股同心之力征服富庶却涣散的城市、建立王朝。可一旦坐进城里、享受起文明的奢华与安逸，几代之后，子孙在温柔富贵乡中长大，那股共苦的凝聚力便一点点消融——人人开始盘算自己的利益，王朝随之腐化、内耗、衰弱，最终被下一支来自荒漠、凝聚力正盛的强悍部落取代。如此周而复始。他估算，一个王朝大约三到四代、百余年，就会走完这条由盛转衰的曲线。
这套理论的分量在于：它第一次不靠『天命』或『神意』，而是用**环境、世代更替与群体心理**这些可观察的因素，去解释历史的节律。它把物质环境（游牧 vs 定居、贫瘠 vs 富庶）放在了因果链的前端，又不把人简化为纯粹的经济动物——凝聚力终究是一种情感与忠诚。正因如此，他常被后世尊为社会学、人口学乃至经济学思想的先驱之一；二十世纪的历史学家汤因比称《历史绪论》是『同类著作中最伟大的一部』。读他，你会得到一副看穿一时繁华的透镜：任何看似坚不可摧的强盛，都可能正因它的成功而埋下衰败的种子。
ibnkhaldun.ideas_en:
Ibn Khaldun set out to do something almost ahead of his time: to treat history as a **science** that seeks causes and laws, not merely a chronicle of kings and generals. His question was not 'what happened' but 'why do dynasties never escape the curve of rise, peak, decay and fall.'
His answer turns on one core concept — **'asabiyya,' usually rendered 'solidarity' or 'group cohesion.'** It names the binding force by which a group acts as one, stays loyal to itself, and will sacrifice for the collective. He observed keenly that this force is **strongest in harsh environments.** Nomadic tribes of desert and steppe, materially poor and forever fending off enemies, are forced into tight cohesion, and so develop the fiercest solidarity and the hardiest bodies.
Then comes his finest insight: **cohesion converts into power, and power in turn corrodes cohesion.** A tribe rich in asabiyya can, by that force of shared purpose, conquer the wealthy but scattered cities and found a dynasty. But once settled into the city, tasting the luxury and ease of civilization, within a few generations the descendants grow up in soft comfort, and that hard-won solidarity dissolves bit by bit — everyone begins to calculate their own interest, the dynasty rots, turns on itself, weakens, and is finally overthrown by the next fierce tribe out of the desert, its cohesion at full strength. And so it turns, round and round. He reckoned a dynasty runs this curve from peak to decline in about three or four generations, a little over a century.
The weight of this theory lies here: for the first time it explains the rhythm of history not by 'the mandate of heaven' or 'divine will' but by observable factors — **environment, generational turnover, and group psychology.** It places material environment (nomadic versus settled, barren versus rich) at the front of the causal chain, yet does not reduce people to pure economic animals — cohesion is, after all, a matter of feeling and loyalty. For this he is often honored as one of the forerunners of sociology, demography, even economic thought; the twentieth-century historian Toynbee called the Muqaddima 'the greatest work of its kind.' To read him is to gain a lens that sees through momentary splendor: any seemingly unassailable strength may, by its very success, be sowing the seeds of its own decline.

assessments.text: 称《历史绪论》是『任何时代、任何地方、任何头脑所构想出的同类著作中最伟大的一部』。
普遍视其为社会学、历史哲学与人口学的重要先驱，尤以『asabiyya』理论对群体凝聚与文明周期的分析著称。

assessments_en.text: Called the Muqaddima 'undoubtedly the greatest work of its kind that has ever yet been created by any mind in any time or place.'

Widely regarded as a major forerunner of sociology, the philosophy of history and demography, noted especially for the theory of 'asabiyya' and its analysis of group cohesion and civilizational cycles.

quotes: 过去与未来，如水滴之与水滴，彼此相似。
地理与气候塑造着居于其上的民族的性格。
当一个王朝达到顶点，它便再无处可去，只能开始衰落。
quotes_en: The past resembles the future more than one drop of water resembles another.
Geography and climate shape the character of the peoples who dwell upon them.
When a dynasty reaches its peak, it has nowhere left to go but into decline.
works: 《训诫之书》(Kitāb al-ʿIbar，世界史，《绪论》为其导论)
自传《伊本·赫勒敦及其东西之旅》
works_en: Kitāb al-ʿIbar (the universal history, of which the Muqaddima is the introduction)
ibnkhaldun.lineage: 他身处伊斯兰黄金时代晚期的思想土壤，熟稔亚里士多德、法拉比、阿威罗伊等希腊—伊斯兰哲学传统，却另辟蹊径，把哲学的求因精神转用于历史与社会。他的环境史观遥启后世孟德斯鸠的气候论；『物质环境塑造社会』的思路，也常被拿来与马克思的唯物史观、以及戴蒙德式的地理决定论相提并论。在很长时间里，他在西方几乎被遗忘，直到十九世纪才被重新发现、奉为社会科学的远祖。
ibnkhaldun.lineage_en: Rooted in the intellectual soil of the late Islamic Golden Age, he was steeped in the Greek-Islamic philosophical tradition of Aristotle, al-Farabi and Averroes, yet struck out on his own, turning philosophy's spirit of causal inquiry toward history and society. His environmental view of history distantly anticipates Montesquieu's later climate theory; his idea that 'the material environment shapes society' is often set beside Marx's materialist conception of history and Diamond-style geographic determinism. For a long time he was nearly forgotten in the West, until the nineteenth century rediscovered him and enshrined him as a distant ancestor of the social sciences.
ibnkhaldun.trivia: 1401 年，帖木儿大军围攻大马士革，年近七旬的伊本·赫勒敦作为城中显要出城与之会面。据他自述，两人交谈数周，帖木儿对他的学识与见解颇为激赏，向他询问马格里布的地理与政局。这场征服者与史学家的会面，成了历史上著名的一幕。
ibnkhaldun.trivia_en: In 1401, as Timur's army besieged Damascus, Ibn Khaldun — then nearly seventy — went out from the city as one of its notables to meet him. By his own account they conversed over several weeks; Timur admired his learning and insight and questioned him about the geography and politics of the Maghreb. This meeting of conqueror and historian became a celebrated episode in history.

alghazali.bio: 安萨里（al-Ghazālī，1058–1111），生于波斯呼罗珊的图斯，伊斯兰教历史上最有影响力的神学家、法学家与苏菲思想家之一，后世尊称『胡贾特·伊斯兰』（伊斯兰的明证）。早年师从大学者朱韦尼，三十四岁即被塞尔柱帝国权相尼札姆·穆勒克延聘为巴格达尼札米亚学院首席教席，讲学之盛冠绝一时。1095年他突发深刻的精神危机，一度失语、无法授课，遂散尽家财，托词朝觐离开巴格达，在大马士革、耶路撒冷、麦加等地隐修游历约十年，潜心苏菲实践。晚年应邀重返尼沙普尔讲学，最后归隐故乡图斯设帐授徒，直至去世。
alghazali.bio_en: Al-Ghazali (1058–1111), born in Tus in the Persian province of Khorasan, was one of the most influential theologians, jurists and Sufi thinkers in the history of Islam, honored by posterity as Hujjat al-Islam — 'the Proof of Islam.' A student of the great scholar al-Juwayni, he was appointed at thirty-four by the Seljuk vizier Nizam al-Mulk to the chief chair of the Nizamiyya college in Baghdad, where his lectures drew unmatched crowds. In 1095 a profound spiritual crisis struck him — he lost the ability to speak and to teach — whereupon he gave away his wealth, left Baghdad under the pretext of pilgrimage, and spent roughly ten years in retreat and wandering through Damascus, Jerusalem and Mecca, immersed in Sufi practice. In later years he returned, on invitation, to teach at Nishapur, and finally retired to his native Tus, teaching a circle of students until his death.
alghazali.ideas:
安萨里的思想工作，可以概括为一句话：给『理性能走多远』画出边界，再给边界之外的领域找回可靠的认识方式。

第一件事是《哲学家的矛盾》。他先花功夫写了《哲学家的意图》，把法拉比、阿维森纳一系的亚里士多德主义哲学如实转述到连对手都挑不出错，然后逐条拆解。他列出哲学家的二十条主张，判定其中三条——世界无始永恒、真主只知普遍规律不知个别事物、没有肉身复活——已越出理性所能证明的范围却冒充确知。要点不是反对逻辑与数学（他明确承认二者有效，甚至主张神学家都该学逻辑），而是反对哲学在自己够不着的地方伪装成科学。

第二件事影响更深远：对因果必然性的批判。火烧棉花，我们看到的只是『火挨着棉花，棉花烧了』——两件事先后相继；至于火『必然导致』燃烧的那个『必然』，谁也没有观察到过。他由此主张：所谓自然规律只是真主行事的『习惯』，并非逻辑必然。这个论证比休谟的因果怀疑论早了六百多年，结论却相反——休谟把因果归于人心的习惯联想，安萨里把它归于神意的恒常。两人共享同一个洞见：『必然联系』从来不在经验之中。

第三件事是他的怀疑方法。在自传《迷途指津》里，他记录了自己年轻时的认识论危机：感官会骗人（星星看着只有硬币大），那推理呢——谁来担保理性本身不出错？他被这个问题困了近两个月，『心病』到无法确信任何知识，最后靠他所说的『真主投入胸中的一道光』而非任何论证走出困境。这段『系统怀疑一切、再寻找不可怀疑之基点』的历程，比笛卡尔的方法论怀疑早了五个多世纪。

由此他得出知识的等级：最高的知识不是听来的、也不是推出来的，而是亲证的——他称之为 dhawq（体尝）。知道『醉』的定义与真正醉过是两回事，知道『健康』的医理与身体康健是两回事。宗教知识尤其如此：教法学家能告诉你礼拜的规条，只有修行能让你尝到礼拜是什么。

最后是集大成的《宗教科学的复兴》：四十卷的大书，把外在的教法与内在的心灵状态重新缝合——每一项宗教义务，他都既讲『怎么做』，更讲『带着什么心做』。他对 riya（里雅，表演给人看的隐秘虔诚）的解剖尤其锋利：最难缠的名利心，恰恰藏在最体面的善行里。这部书让苏菲主义从受怀疑的边缘进入逊尼派正统的主流，重塑了此后千年伊斯兰的宗教生活。
alghazali.ideas_en:
Al-Ghazali's intellectual project can be put in one sentence: draw the boundary of how far reason can go, then recover a reliable way of knowing for what lies beyond it.

The first move was The Incoherence of the Philosophers. He began by writing The Intentions of the Philosophers, a restatement of the Aristotelianism of al-Farabi and Avicenna so faithful that even its partisans could find no fault — and then dismantled it point by point. Of the philosophers' twenty theses he singled out three — the eternity of the world, God's knowledge of universals but not particulars, and the denial of bodily resurrection — as claims that had strayed beyond what reason can demonstrate while masquerading as certainty. The point was never to reject logic or mathematics (he affirmed both, and even insisted theologians study logic), but to stop philosophy from impersonating science where it cannot reach.

The second move cut deeper: the critique of causal necessity. When fire burns cotton, all we ever observe is contact followed by burning — one event after another. The 'necessity' by which fire must cause burning has never been observed by anyone. Natural law, he concluded, is simply God's habit of acting, not a logical necessity. The argument anticipates Hume's causal skepticism by more than six centuries, though the conclusions diverge — Hume traced causation to habits of the human mind, al-Ghazali to the constancy of divine will. What they share is the insight that 'necessary connection' is never found in experience itself.

The third move was his method of doubt. In his autobiography, Deliverance from Error, he records the epistemic crisis of his younger years: the senses deceive (a star looks the size of a coin) — then what of reasoning, and who vouches for reason itself? The question paralyzed him for nearly two months, unable to trust any knowledge at all, until he escaped not by argument but by what he called 'a light God cast into my breast.' This passage — doubt everything systematically, then seek an indubitable foundation — precedes Descartes's methodological doubt by over five centuries.

From this came his hierarchy of knowledge: the highest knowledge is neither heard nor inferred but tasted first-hand — what he called dhawq. Knowing the definition of drunkenness and having been drunk are two different things; knowing the physiology of health is not the same as being well. Religious knowledge above all: the jurist can recite the rules of prayer, but only practice lets you taste what prayer is.

Last came the summa, The Revival of the Religious Sciences: forty books stitching outward law back onto the inward states of the heart — for every religious duty he explains not only how to perform it but with what heart. His dissection of riya — the hidden piety-for-show — is especially sharp: the most stubborn vanity hides inside the most respectable good works. The book carried Sufism from the suspect margins into the Sunni mainstream and reshaped Islamic religious life for the next thousand years.

assessments.by: 蒙哥马利·瓦特（英国伊斯兰学家）
assessments.text: 安萨里被誉为穆罕默德之后最伟大的穆斯林，这一声誉绝非名不副实。（大意）

assessments.by: 阿威罗伊（伊斯兰亚里士多德主义哲学家）
assessments.text: 为回应《哲学家的矛盾》，他专门写下《矛盾的矛盾》逐章反驳——以对手的规格，反证其分量。

assessments.by: 弗兰克·格里费尔（耶鲁大学伊斯兰思想史学者）
assessments.text: 安萨里是伊斯兰思想史上最具原创性的思想家之一，其影响几乎波及此后每一个流派。（大意）

assessments_en.by: W. Montgomery Watt (British scholar of Islam)
assessments_en.text: Al-Ghazali has been acclaimed as the greatest Muslim after Muhammad, and the acclaim is by no means unmerited. (paraphrased)
He wrote The Incoherence of the Incoherence expressly to rebut al-Ghazali chapter by chapter — the caliber of the opponent measuring the weight of the man.

assessments_en.by: Frank Griffel (historian of Islamic thought, Yale)
assessments_en.text: Al-Ghazali stands among the most original thinkers in the history of Islam, his influence touching virtually every school that came after. (paraphrased)

quotes: 知道『醉』的定义，与真正醉了，是两回事。——《迷途指津》（大意）
我审视自己的教学，发现驱动它的并非纯然为了真主，而是对名望与地位的欲求。——《迷途指津》（大意）
火挨着棉花，棉花烧了——燃烧与接触之间，我们只见相继，未见必然。——《哲学家的矛盾》（大意）
quotes_en: Knowing the definition of drunkenness and being drunk are two different things. — Deliverance from Error (paraphrased)
I examined my teaching and found that what drove it was not purely God, but the craving for renown and position. — Deliverance from Error (paraphrased)
Fire touches cotton and the cotton burns — between the contact and the burning we observe only succession, never necessity. — The Incoherence of the Philosophers (paraphrased)
works_en: The Incoherence of the Philosophers (Tahafut al-Falasifa)
The Revival of the Religious Sciences (Ihya' 'Ulum al-Din)
alghazali.lineage: 承：师从艾什尔里派大家朱韦尼，教义学上属艾什尔里传统；苏菲一脉上承穆哈西比与麦基的内省功夫。批判对象：法拉比—阿维森纳一系的亚里士多德主义。启：使苏菲主义融入逊尼正统，重塑此后伊斯兰宗教生活；阿威罗伊为回应他写下《矛盾的矛盾》；以拉丁名 Algazel 进入中世纪欧洲经院讨论；其偶因论与怀疑方法，后世常与休谟、笛卡尔、马勒伯朗士对读。
alghazali.lineage_en: Upstream: trained under the great Ash'arite theologian al-Juwayni, he stood in the Ash'arite tradition of doctrine; his Sufi practice drew on the introspective discipline of al-Muhasibi and al-Makki. Target of critique: the Aristotelianism of the al-Farabi–Avicenna line. Downstream: he carried Sufism into Sunni orthodoxy and reshaped Islamic religious life thereafter; Averroes wrote The Incoherence of the Incoherence in reply; under the Latin name Algazel he entered medieval European scholastic debate; his occasionalism and method of doubt are routinely read alongside Hume, Descartes and Malebranche.
alghazali.trivia: 他离开巴格达时正值声望顶点，对外只说去朝觐，实为一去十年。危机发作时他患的是字面意义的失语——舌头发不出声，医生断言『病根在心，药石无用』。弟弟艾哈迈德·安萨里也是著名苏菲导师。拉丁欧洲通过《哲学家的意图》的译本认识他，一度把『Algazel』误当成一位亚里士多德主义者——因为那本书本是他为批判而写的如实转述。
alghazali.trivia_en: He left Baghdad at the very peak of his fame, telling people he was going on pilgrimage — and stayed away ten years. During his crisis he suffered literal aphonia: his tongue would produce no sound, and the physicians pronounced the root to be in the heart, beyond medicine. His brother Ahmad al-Ghazali was himself a famous Sufi master. Latin Europe first met him through a translation of The Intentions of the Philosophers and for a time mistook 'Algazel' for an Aristotelian — the book being the faithful restatement he had written only in order to refute.

festinger.bio: 1919–1989，美国社会心理学家，生于纽约布鲁克林的一个犹太移民家庭。师从『场论』大师库尔特·勒温，先后任教于明尼苏达、斯坦福等校。1954 年提出社会比较理论，1957 年出版《认知失调论》，两项工作共同奠定了实验社会心理学的基石。他以巧妙、甚至戏剧化的实验设计著称：为验证认知失调，他潜入一个相信世界末日将至的邪教团体，观察预言落空后信徒如何反而更坚信不疑。晚年转向考古学与人类史研究，学术兴趣之广令人惊讶。
festinger.bio_en: 1919–1989, American social psychologist, born in Brooklyn, New York, into a Jewish immigrant family. A student of the 'field theory' pioneer Kurt Lewin, he taught at Minnesota, Stanford and elsewhere. His 1954 social comparison theory and his 1957 book A Theory of Cognitive Dissonance together laid the cornerstone of experimental social psychology. He was famous for ingenious, even dramatic experimental designs: to test dissonance, he infiltrated a doomsday cult and watched believers grow more convinced, not less, after the prophecy failed. In later life he turned, strikingly, to archaeology and the study of human history.
festinger.ideas:
费斯廷格一生给心理学留下两件利器，都在讲同一件事：人无法忍受内心的不一致，会主动做点什么去消除它。

第一件是『社会比较理论』（1954）。他的出发点很朴素：人有一种评估自己的内在需要——我到底聪不聪明、能力强不强、观点对不对？可很多东西没有客观的尺子（体温计能量体温，却没有『能力计』量能力）。于是人退而求其次，拿别人当尺子。关键在于：我们不跟差距悬殊的人比，只跟处境相近的人比——你不会拿自己和奥运冠军比跑步，只会和同一个跑步群里的人较劲。这解释了一个反直觉的现象：为什么身边人的成功，往往比遥远名人的成功更刺痛我们。

第二件是『认知失调』（1957），影响更为深远。当一个人的两个念头彼此冲突（比如『我很聪明』与『我做了件蠢事』），或行为与信念不符（『我明知抽烟有害』却『天天抽』），内心会产生一种类似口渴的不适感，他称之为失调。人会本能地想消除它——但往往不是通过改变行为（太难），而是通过扭曲认知（太容易）：抽烟的人会说『我爷爷抽到九十岁』。他最惊人的验证，是那个著名的实验：让人做极枯燥的活儿，事后付一美元或二十美元请他们向别人谎称有趣。结果拿一美元的人，反而真的觉得任务更有趣——因为二十美元足以为撒谎开脱，而一美元不够，只能靠说服自己『其实没那么无聊』来消除失调。这个发现颠覆了当时的常识：报酬越少，态度改变反而越大。

这两个理论合起来，画出了一幅冷峻的人性图景：人并非追求真相的理性动物，而是追求内心一致的辩护动物——我们常常先有立场，再为它编造理由。
festinger.ideas_en:
Festinger left psychology two sharp instruments, both making one point: people cannot tolerate inner inconsistency and will actively do something to remove it.

The first is social comparison theory (1954). Its starting point is plain: humans have an inner need to evaluate themselves — am I smart, capable, right? Yet many things have no objective yardstick (a thermometer reads temperature, but there is no 'ability-meter'). So people fall back on the next best thing: using other people as the ruler. The crucial twist is that we do not compare with those far above us, only with those close to our own situation — you don't measure your running against an Olympic champion, you stew over the others in your own running group. This explains a counterintuitive fact: why the success of those near us so often stings more than the success of distant celebrities.

The second, cognitive dissonance (1957), proved even more influential. When two of a person's thoughts clash ('I am smart' and 'I did something stupid'), or behavior contradicts belief ('I know smoking harms me' yet 'I smoke daily'), an uneasiness arises much like thirst; he called it dissonance. People instinctively want it gone — but usually not by changing the behavior (too hard), rather by distorting the cognition (too easy): the smoker says, 'my grandfather smoked to ninety.' His most stunning demonstration was the famous experiment: subjects did a crushingly dull task, then were paid one dollar or twenty to tell the next person it was fun. Those paid one dollar actually came to find the task more interesting — twenty dollars was ample justification for the lie, but one dollar was not, leaving no way to resolve the dissonance except to convince themselves 'it really wasn't so dull.' The finding overturned common sense: the smaller the reward, the greater the change of attitude.

Together the two theories sketch a bracing picture of human nature: we are not rational animals in pursuit of truth but justifying animals in pursuit of inner consistency — we often take a position first and manufacture the reasons afterward.

assessments.text: 认知失调论被广泛视为二十世纪社会心理学最具影响力的理论之一，重塑了人们对态度、说服与自我辩护的理解。

assessments.by: 埃利奥特·阿伦森（其学生）
assessments.text: 『他是我见过最聪明的人。和他共事既令人振奋又令人害怕——他能一眼看穿你论证里的漏洞。』（大意）
常被誉为库尔特·勒温之后最重要的实验社会心理学家，把社会心理学从思辨引向严格的实验科学。

assessments_en.text: Cognitive dissonance is widely regarded as one of the most influential theories in twentieth-century social psychology, reshaping how we understand attitudes, persuasion and self-justification.
'He was the most brilliant person I ever knew. Working with him was exhilarating and terrifying — he could see the hole in your argument instantly.' (paraphrased)
Often named the most important experimental social psychologist after Kurt Lewin, the man who moved the field from speculation to rigorous experiment.

quotes: 人有评估自身能力与观点的内在驱力。
当行动无法收回，态度便会转过来追随它。
给一个人足够的理由去做某事，他不会改变想法；给的理由刚好不够，他反而会说服自己。（大意）
quotes_en: There exists, in the human organism, a drive to evaluate his opinions and his abilities.
When an action cannot be undone, the attitude turns to follow it.
Give a man ample reason to do something and he won't change his mind; give him barely too little, and he'll talk himself into it. (paraphrased)
works: 《人际传播理论》等社会比较奠基论文（1954）
festinger.lineage: 上承：师从场论创始人库尔特·勒温，属勒温开创的群体动力学一脉。旁及：与海德的平衡理论、奥斯古德的一致性理论同属『认知一致性』大家族。下启：学生埃利奥特·阿伦森、达里尔·贝姆（提出自我知觉理论与之争鸣）等人将失调研究推向纵深；其思想深刻影响了行为经济学对『非理性辩护』的研究，与卡尼曼一脉遥相呼应。
festinger.lineage_en: Upstream: trained under Kurt Lewin, founder of field theory, in Lewin's lineage of group dynamics. Alongside: his work belongs to the 'cognitive consistency' family together with Heider's balance theory and Osgood's congruity theory. Downstream: students such as Elliot Aronson and Daryl Bem (whose self-perception theory rivaled dissonance) deepened the research; his ideas profoundly shaped behavioral economics' study of 'irrational justification,' echoing across to the Kahneman tradition.
festinger.trivia: 他最著名的田野研究近乎间谍行动：1954 年他和同事假扮信徒，混入一个笃信外星人将在特定日期拯救世界的芝加哥小教派，只为亲眼观察末日预言落空那一刻会发生什么。结果印证了他的预测——预言没有兑现，核心信徒非但没有醒悟，反而更狂热地对外传教，因为唯有拉来更多人相信，才能消除『我押上一切却扑了空』的巨大失调。这段经历写成了《当预言落空》，成为社会心理学史上的经典案例。
festinger.trivia_en: His most famous field study read almost like espionage: in 1954 he and colleagues posed as believers and infiltrated a small Chicago sect convinced that aliens would rescue the world on a set date — purely to witness what happens the moment a doomsday prophecy fails. The result confirmed his prediction: when the prophecy did not come true, the core believers, far from waking up, proselytized more fervently than ever, because only by recruiting more believers could they dispel the enormous dissonance of having bet everything and lost. The episode became the book When Prophecy Fails, a classic case in the history of social psychology.

carstensen.bio: 1953年生，美国心理学家，斯坦福大学心理学教授、斯坦福长寿研究中心（Stanford Center on Longevity）创始主任，社会情绪选择理论的提出者，美国国家医学院院士。她把毕生发展心理学从『记录衰退』的学问改写成『解释动机如何随时间变化』的学问，是当代老化与长寿研究最有影响力的声音之一。
carstensen.bio_en: Born in 1953, American psychologist; professor of psychology at Stanford and founding director of the Stanford Center on Longevity; originator of socioemotional selectivity theory and a member of the National Academy of Medicine. She rewrote life-span psychology from a science of documenting decline into a science of how motivation changes with time, becoming one of the most influential voices in the study of aging and longevity.
carstensen.ideas:
她最核心的贡献是社会情绪选择理论（socioemotional selectivity theory）：人的动机不由年龄本身决定，而由『感知到还剩多少时间』决定。当时间地平线显得辽阔（典型如年轻人），人优先追求拓展——认识新朋友、学新东西、为遥远的未来投资；当地平线收窄（典型如老年人，但也包括绝症患者、战乱或疫情中的人），人转向此刻的情感意义——把时间留给最亲近的人、做真正要紧的事。用一个类比：同一部电影，知道自己只能再看十分钟的人，和以为还能看十小时的人，看法完全不同——变的不是眼睛，是剩余时间。

这个理论解开了老化研究里著名的『幸福悖论』：身体在衰退、朋友在减少，老年人报告的情绪幸福感却普遍高于年轻人。她的解释是：老年人不是迟钝了，而是在有限的时间里做了更聪明的动机选择——主动修剪社交圈、留下滋养自己的关系，注意力也更偏向积极信息（她称之为『积极效应』，positivity effect）。社交圈变小因此常常不是孤独的衰退，而是一次主动的战略收缩。

她的另一大主题是『长寿红利的重新设计』：二十世纪人类平均寿命增加了约三十年，这是文明史上前所未有的礼物，可我们的人生脚本——集中上学、集中上班、然后一次性退休的三段式——仍是为六十岁上下的寿命设计的。她主导的斯坦福长寿中心提出『百岁人生的新地图』：学习、工作、休整与照护应交错分布在整个人生，而不是各占一段；工作年限可以更长但强度更疏，教育不该在二十多岁就『毕业』。这套主张深刻影响了关于退休制度、终身学习与老龄化社会的公共讨论。
carstensen.ideas_en:
Her central contribution is socioemotional selectivity theory: motivation is governed not by age itself but by how much time one perceives to remain. When the horizon feels expansive (typically the young), people prioritize expansion — meeting new people, learning new things, investing in a distant future; when the horizon narrows (typically the old, but also the terminally ill, or anyone living through war or plague), people turn toward present emotional meaning — reserving time for those closest to them and for what truly matters. An analogy: the same film looks entirely different to someone who knows they have ten minutes left to watch than to someone who assumes ten hours — what changed is not the eyes but the time remaining.

The theory resolved the famous 'paradox of aging': bodies decline and friends grow fewer, yet older adults consistently report higher emotional well-being than the young. Her explanation: the old are not duller — they make smarter motivational choices with limited time, actively pruning their social circles to keep the nourishing relationships, and attending more to positive information (what she named the positivity effect). A shrinking circle is thus often not lonely decay but deliberate strategic contraction.

Her other great theme is redesigning the longevity bonus: the twentieth century added roughly thirty years to average human life, a gift without precedent, yet our life script — schooling, then work, then one lump-sum retirement — was written for lives of about sixty years. The Stanford Center on Longevity's 'New Map of Life,' developed under her leadership, argues that learning, work, rest and caregiving should interleave across the whole span: longer but less intense working lives, and an education that never 'graduates' in one's twenties. These ideas have deeply shaped public debate on retirement systems, lifelong learning and aging societies.

assessments.text: 在《最好的告别》中用整节篇幅介绍她的研究，称其揭示了一个关键事实：当人意识到时间有限，需求与欲望会随之改变——老年人转向亲近关系与当下意义，并不是衰退，而是视角的转换（大意）。
长期将她列为重新定义『老年』的代表性学者——把老龄化从社会负担的叙事，改写为有待重新设计的文明机遇（大意）。

assessments_en.text: Devoted a full section of Being Mortal to her research, crediting it with revealing a key fact: when people become aware that time is limited, their needs and desires shift — the old turn toward close relationships and present meaning, which is not decline but a change of perspective (paraphrased).
Have long counted her among the scholars who redefined 'old age' — rewriting aging from a story of social burden into a civilizational opportunity awaiting redesign (paraphrased).

quotes: 我们正用为六十岁寿命写好的人生脚本，过着近百年的人生（大意）。
当时间的地平线收窄，人们不再追求『更多』，而开始追求『更深』——目标从拓展转向意义（大意）。
数据一再显示：老年人是情绪上更幸福的人群——这不是鸡汤，是重复验证的实证发现（大意）。
quotes_en: We are living near-hundred-year lives on a script written for sixty-year ones (paraphrased).
As time horizons narrow, people stop pursuing 'more' and start pursuing 'deeper' — goals shift from expansion to meaning (paraphrased).
The data keep showing that older adults are emotionally the happier population — not a platitude but a repeatedly replicated empirical finding (paraphrased).
works: 《认真对待时间：社会情绪选择理论》（Taking Time Seriously, American Psychologist, 1999）
斯坦福长寿研究中心《百岁人生的新地图》（The New Map of Life, 2021，主持）
works_en: "Taking Time Seriously: A Theory of Socioemotional Selectivity" (American Psychologist, 1999)
The New Map of Life (Stanford Center on Longevity report, 2021, directed)
carstensen.lineage: 承接巴尔特斯（Paul Baltes）一脉的毕生发展心理学传统——发展不止于成年、每个年龄段各有得失；她把这一传统与动机心理学、情绪科学嫁接，开出社会情绪选择理论一支。经由斯坦福长寿研究中心，她的影响溢出学术圈，进入退休政策、金融业与城市设计对老龄化社会的重新想象。
carstensen.lineage_en: Heir to the life-span development tradition of Paul Baltes — development does not stop at adulthood, and every age has its gains and losses; she grafted that tradition onto motivation psychology and affective science, founding the branch of socioemotional selectivity theory. Through the Stanford Center on Longevity her influence spilled beyond academia into retirement policy, finance and urban design for aging societies.
carstensen.trivia: 她走上老化研究之路缘于一场车祸：21岁时她遭遇严重车祸，在骨科病房躺了数月，同病房多是年迈的女性——她后来说，那是她第一次长时间近距离观察老年，也是她对『时间怎样改变人』发生兴趣的起点。住院期间她的父亲替她去大学教室录下心理学课程，她在病床上听完了最初的课；后来她拿到临床心理学博士，一路做到斯坦福讲席教授。她的 TED 演讲《老年人更幸福》把『幸福悖论』讲给了数百万普通听众。
carstensen.trivia_en: A car crash set her on the path to studying aging: at 21 she was gravely injured and spent months in an orthopedic ward shared mostly with elderly women — her first prolonged, close-up view of old age, and, as she later said, the origin of her fascination with how time changes people. While she was hospitalized her father recorded university psychology lectures for her, and she completed her first courses from a hospital bed; she went on to a PhD in clinical psychology and a chaired professorship at Stanford. Her TED talk on why older people are happier brought the 'paradox of aging' to millions.

bohr.bio: 尼尔斯·玻尔（1885–1962），丹麦物理学家，1922年因原子结构与原子辐射研究获诺贝尔物理学奖。他在哥本哈根创办理论物理研究所，使之成为两次大战之间世界物理学的圣地；二战中协助大批科学家逃离纳粹欧洲，战后奔走呼吁核武器的国际公开管制。
bohr.bio_en: Niels Bohr (1885–1962), Danish physicist, won the 1922 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on atomic structure and radiation. The Institute for Theoretical Physics he founded in Copenhagen became the Mecca of world physics between the wars; during World War II he helped many scientists escape Nazi Europe, and afterwards campaigned for open international control of nuclear weapons.
bohr.ideas:
玻尔1913年的原子模型是量子观念第一次在原子内部站稳脚跟：电子只能占据一系列分立的轨道，在轨道之间『跳跃』时吸收或放出整份的光。这个『只许台阶、不许斜坡』的图景当时惊世骇俗，却一举解释了氢原子光谱几十年悬而未决的规律。为了让新旧物理衔接，他又提出对应原理——量子规律在大尺度极限下必须逐渐过渡回经典物理，新理论不是推翻旧世界，而是包住它。

他最深远的贡献是互补原理：光与电子既呈现波的一面、又呈现粒子的一面，两幅图像互相排斥，却又缺一不可——哪一面显现，取决于你搭建了哪种实验。由此他主张，『现象』必须连同整个测量安排一起描述，脱离一切观测条件去谈微观对象的性质是没有内容的。这一思想成为量子力学『哥本哈根诠释』的骨架，也把认识论问题第一次逼进了物理学的核心。他晚年相信互补的智慧不限于物理：思想与情感、分析一个生命与体验这个生命、不同文化的价值，都可能是同一实在互斥而互补的两面。

同样传世的还有他的工作方式——所谓『哥本哈根精神』：研究所里不论资历、只论论证，年轻人可以当面顶撞掌门。海森堡、泡利、狄拉克、朗道都在这种连珠炮式的对话里淬炼成才。他与爱因斯坦绵延三十年的论战，被公认为科学史上质量最高的争论：两人都把对方的反驳当成打磨自己思想的砥石。
bohr.ideas_en:
Bohr's 1913 model of the atom was the first time quantum ideas gained a foothold inside the atom: electrons may occupy only a discrete set of orbits, and 'jump' between them by absorbing or emitting whole packets of light. This 'stairs only, no ramps' picture was scandalous at the time, yet at a stroke it explained decades-old regularities in the hydrogen spectrum. To stitch new physics to old he added the correspondence principle — in the large-scale limit, quantum laws must shade back into classical physics: the new theory does not overthrow the old world but encloses it.

His most far-reaching contribution is complementarity: light and electrons show a wave face and a particle face; the two pictures exclude each other, yet neither can be dropped — which face appears depends on which experiment you build. From this he argued that a 'phenomenon' must be described together with the entire measuring arrangement; talk of a micro-object's properties apart from all conditions of observation is empty. This became the backbone of the 'Copenhagen interpretation' of quantum mechanics, and for the first time forced epistemology into the core of physics. In later years he believed complementarity's wisdom extends beyond physics: thought and feeling, analyzing a life and living it, the values of different cultures may be mutually exclusive yet jointly indispensable faces of one reality.

Equally enduring is his style of work — the 'Copenhagen spirit': at his institute, rank counted for nothing and argument for everything; the young could contradict the master to his face. Heisenberg, Pauli, Dirac and Landau were all forged in that rapid-fire dialogue. His thirty-year debate with Einstein is widely judged the highest-quality argument in the history of science: each treated the other's objections as the whetstone of his own thought.

assessments.text: 「他能在如此不稳固、矛盾的基础上发现原子的主要规律，在我看来是一个奇迹——那是思想领域里最高的音乐性。」（《自述》，大意）
「玻尔首先是一位哲学家，而不是物理学家；但他懂得，我们时代的自然哲学只有在实验事实的每个细节上都站得住，才有分量。」（大意）

assessments_en.text: 'That this insecure and contradictory foundation was sufficient to enable a man of Bohr's unique instinct and tact to discover the major laws of the spectral lines... appeared to me like a miracle — the highest form of musicality in the sphere of thought.' (Autobiographical Notes, paraphrased)

'Bohr was primarily a philosopher, not a physicist; but he understood that natural philosophy in our day carries weight only if its every detail can stand the severe test of experiment.' (paraphrased)

quotes: 在存在这出伟大的戏剧里，我们既是观众，又是演员。
一个普通真理的反面是谬误；但一个深刻真理的反面，可能是另一个深刻真理。（大意）
别去指挥上帝该怎么做。（对爱因斯坦『上帝不掷骰子』的回敬，转述）
quotes_en: In the great drama of existence, we ourselves are both actors and spectators.
The opposite of a correct statement is a false statement; but the opposite of a profound truth may well be another profound truth. (paraphrased)
Stop telling God what to do. (his retort to Einstein's 'God does not play dice,' as commonly recounted)
works: 《论原子和分子的构造》（1913年『三部曲』论文）
《致联合国的公开信》（呼吁开放世界与核管制）
works_en: 'On the Constitution of Atoms and Molecules' (the 1913 'trilogy' papers)
Atomic Theory and the Description of Nature
Open Letter to the United Nations (urging an open world and nuclear control)
bohr.lineage: 在曼彻斯特师从卢瑟福，把老师的原子核模型量子化；他的哥本哈根研究所培养或深刻影响了海森堡、泡利、狄拉克、朗道、伽莫夫等整整一代量子物理学家。与爱因斯坦的论战塑造了此后一切关于量子力学诠释的讨论。儿子奥格·玻尔亦获诺贝尔物理学奖，父子同奖成为佳话。
bohr.lineage_en: He studied under Rutherford in Manchester and quantized his teacher's nuclear model of the atom; his Copenhagen institute trained or profoundly shaped a whole generation of quantum physicists — Heisenberg, Pauli, Dirac, Landau, Gamow. His debate with Einstein has framed every discussion of quantum interpretation since. His son Aage Bohr also won the Nobel Prize in Physics, a celebrated father-and-son double.
bohr.trivia: 年轻时是出色的足球守门员，效力于哥本哈根AB俱乐部（弟弟哈拉尔德还代表丹麦踢过奥运会）。嘉士伯啤酒厂把紧邻酿酒厂的『荣誉宅邸』给他居住。1962年去世前一晚，他还在书房黑板上画着与爱因斯坦论战用过的『光子箱』草图。第107号元素𨨏（Bohrium）以他命名。
bohr.trivia_en: In his youth he was a fine football goalkeeper for Copenhagen's AB club (his brother Harald played for Denmark at the Olympics). The Carlsberg brewery granted him its 'House of Honour' beside the brewery. On the last evening of his life in 1962, the blackboard in his study still bore his sketch of the 'photon box' from the debates with Einstein. Element 107, bohrium, is named after him.

heisenberg.bio: 维尔纳·海森堡（1901–1976），德国物理学家，量子力学的主要创立者之一，1932年获诺贝尔物理学奖。23岁在赫尔戈兰岛上写下矩阵力学的第一份手稿，26岁提出不确定性原理。二战期间任德国核研究计划的学术负责人，此节至今聚讼纷纭；战后主持重建西德科学体系。
heisenberg.bio_en: Werner Heisenberg (1901–1976), German physicist, was a principal founder of quantum mechanics and won the 1932 Nobel Prize in Physics. At 23, on the island of Helgoland, he drafted the first manuscript of matrix mechanics; at 26 he formulated the uncertainty principle. During World War II he was scientific head of Germany's nuclear research program — a role still fiercely debated; after the war he led the rebuilding of West German science.
heisenberg.ideas:
1925年的矩阵力学出自一个激进的方法论决断：既然没人能看见电子的轨道，理论就不该谈论它——只用可观测的量（光谱线的频率与强度）搭建力学。他把这些量排成表格（数学上即矩阵），发现两个量相乘竟与次序有关：p乘q不等于q乘p。这个当时看来怪异的『不对易』，正是量子世界与经典世界的分水岭。

1927年他从中提炼出不确定性原理：位置测得越准，动量必然越模糊，两者不确定度的乘积有一条普朗克常数量级的下限。要紧的是，这不是仪器粗糙，而是自然的语法——『同时精确的位置与动量』这个短语在量子世界里根本没有所指。它宣告了拉普拉斯式决定论蓝图的终结：连『知道现在的一切』这个前提本身都无法成立。

晚年他转向物理学的哲学根基。他重新起用亚里士多德的『潜能』（potentia）来刻画量子态：介于可能与现实之间的一种倾向性的实在，观测则是潜能向现实的过渡。他反复申说：『我们观测到的不是自然本身，而是暴露在我们提问方式之下的自然』——科学并非站在自然之外的旁观者，而是人与自然之间对话的一部分。他还强调日常语言与经典概念的不可替代：物理学家哪怕描述最反直觉的实验，最终仍须用『仪器』『读数』这些经典词汇向同行交代——语言的边界，就是可交流知识的边界。
heisenberg.ideas_en:
The matrix mechanics of 1925 sprang from a radical methodological decision: since no one can see an electron's orbit, the theory should not speak of it — mechanics must be built from observable quantities alone (the frequencies and intensities of spectral lines). Arranging these quantities in tables (mathematically, matrices), he found that multiplying two of them depends on their order: p times q does not equal q times p. This 'non-commutativity,' bizarre at the time, is precisely the watershed between the quantum and classical worlds.

In 1927 he distilled from it the uncertainty principle: the more precisely position is measured, the blurrier momentum becomes, the product of their uncertainties bounded below on the order of Planck's constant. Crucially this is not instrumental clumsiness but the grammar of nature — the phrase 'exact position and exact momentum at once' simply has no referent in the quantum world. It announced the end of the Laplacean blueprint of determinism: even the premise 'knowing everything about the present' cannot be had.

In later life he turned to the philosophical foundations of physics. He revived Aristotle's potentia to characterize the quantum state: a reality of tendencies, standing between possibility and actuality, with observation as the passage from one to the other. He never tired of repeating that 'what we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning' — science is not a spectator standing outside nature but part of the dialogue between man and nature. He also insisted on the irreplaceability of ordinary language and classical concepts: however counterintuitive the experiment, the physicist must finally answer to colleagues in classical words like 'instrument' and 'reading' — the limits of language are the limits of communicable knowledge.

assessments.text: 读到海森堡从赫尔戈兰岛带回的手稿时，立即认出其中的表格就是数学家的矩阵，并称这份手稿一举打开了通往新力学的大门。（大意）
普遍将1925–1927年间他与玻恩、约当、狄拉克、薛定谔等人的工作并称为科学史上最密集的理论革命；同时，他在纳粹德国核计划中的角色（尤其1941年哥本哈根之行）始终是道德评价上最具争议的一章。

assessments_en.text: On reading the manuscript Heisenberg brought back from Helgoland, he recognized at once that its tables were the mathematician's matrices, and said the manuscript had thrown open the door to a new mechanics. (paraphrased)

generally rank the 1925–1927 work of Heisenberg with Born, Jordan, Dirac and Schrödinger as the densest theoretical revolution in the history of science — while his role in Nazi Germany's nuclear program (above all the 1941 visit to Copenhagen) remains the most morally contested chapter of his life.

quotes: 我们观测到的不是自然本身，而是暴露在我们提问方式之下的自然。
专家就是知道本领域里一些最严重的错误、并懂得如何避开它们的人。（大意）
自然比人类的思维更精妙；接受量子力学的人，首先要学会放下『图像』。（大意）
quotes_en: What we observe is not nature itself, but nature exposed to our method of questioning.
An expert is someone who knows some of the worst mistakes that can be made in his subject, and how to avoid them. (paraphrased)
Nature is subtler than human thought; whoever accepts quantum mechanics must first learn to let go of 'pictures.' (paraphrased)
works: 《关于运动学和力学关系的量子论重新诠释》（1925，矩阵力学奠基论文）
《论量子论运动学与力学的直观内容》（1927，不确定性原理论文）
works_en: 'Quantum-Theoretical Reinterpretation of Kinematic and Mechanical Relations' (1925, the founding paper of matrix mechanics)
'On the Perceptual Content of Quantum Theoretical Kinematics and Mechanics' (1927, the uncertainty paper)
Der Teil und das Ganze (intellectual autobiography, tr. Physics and Beyond)
heisenberg.lineage: 在慕尼黑师从索末菲、在哥廷根师从玻恩，又在哥本哈根经玻尔淬炼——集三大学派于一身；与泡利终生互为最严苛的批评者。矩阵力学与薛定谔的波动力学后来被证明等价，合流为今日的量子力学。战后创建并长期主持马克斯·普朗克物理研究所。
heisenberg.lineage_en: Trained under Sommerfeld in Munich and Born in Göttingen, then tempered by Bohr in Copenhagen — heir to all three great schools; Pauli was his most merciless critic and lifelong correspondent. Matrix mechanics was later proved equivalent to Schrödinger's wave mechanics, the two merging into quantum mechanics as we know it. After the war he founded and long directed the Max Planck Institute for Physics.
heisenberg.trivia: 1925年6月，花粉症折磨得他满脸肿胀，他躲到几乎寸草不生的赫尔戈兰岛疗养，就在那里的一个凌晨完成了矩阵力学的突破，激动得爬上岛角的岩石等日出。他是造诣接近职业水准的钢琴家。1941年他到哥本哈根拜访玻尔的那次谈话不欢而散、内容成谜，后来被写成名剧《哥本哈根》。战争结束时他与德国核计划同僚被软禁在英国农庄别墅，盟军的窃听录音（『农庄别墅纪录』）成为研究那段历史的第一手史料。
heisenberg.trivia_en: In June 1925, hay fever so swelled his face that he retreated to the nearly grassless island of Helgoland — where, in the small hours one morning, he made the matrix-mechanics breakthrough and climbed a rock at the island's tip to await the sunrise. He was a nearly concert-level pianist. His 1941 conversation with Bohr in Copenhagen ended badly and its content remains a mystery — later the subject of the celebrated play Copenhagen. At the war's end he and his nuclear-program colleagues were interned at an English country house, and the Allies' secret recordings (the 'Farm Hall transcripts') became primary sources for that history.

vonneumann.bio: 约翰·冯·诺依曼（1903–1957），匈牙利裔美国数学家，常被称为『最后的通才』：纯数学、量子力学的数学基础、博弈论、计算机体系结构、自动机理论、数值天气预报，他都是奠基人或开创者之一。普林斯顿高等研究院首批教授，曼哈顿计划的核心顾问。
vonneumann.bio_en: John von Neumann (1903–1957), Hungarian-born American mathematician, is often called 'the last of the great polymaths': pure mathematics, the mathematical foundations of quantum mechanics, game theory, computer architecture, automata theory and numerical weather prediction all count him among their founders. He was one of the first professors at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton and a core adviser to the Manhattan Project.
vonneumann.ideas:
冯·诺依曼的第一件大事是给混沌初开的量子力学立规矩：1932年的《量子力学的数学基础》把整套理论安放在希尔伯特空间的严格框架上，让物理学家的直觉计算第一次有了数学地基。书中他把『测量』本身写成公理，并证明测量链条上那道著名的分界线可以任意移动而不改变任何预言——把量子力学最深的概念难题摆上了台面，而不是扫到地毯下。

第二件是发明博弈论。1928年他证明极小极大定理，1944年与经济学家摩根斯坦合著《博弈论与经济行为》，把讨价还价、扑克、军备竞赛这类『我的最优取决于你怎么做』的策略处境变成可以定理化的数学。此前的数学模拟的是无心的自然，博弈论第一次让数学正面处理会算计对方的对手——经济学、演化生物学与冷战战略学从此改写。

第三件塑造了你此刻用来阅读这段话的机器。1945年的《EDVAC报告初稿》提出存储程序体系：程序与数据存在同一个存储器里，指令本身也是可以被读写的数据。今天几乎每一台手机与电脑仍是『冯·诺依曼机』。晚年他把眼光投向计算与生命的交界：自复制自动机理论先于DNA结构的发现，从纯逻辑推出『一个机器要复制自己，必须携带并复制一份自身的描述』；《计算机与人脑》则开启了把大脑当作信息处理系统研究的先河。
vonneumann.ideas_en:
Von Neumann's first great deed was to give the young, unruly quantum mechanics its rulebook: Mathematical Foundations of Quantum Mechanics (1932) set the whole theory on the rigorous frame of Hilbert space, giving physicists' intuitive calculations a mathematical floor for the first time. In it he axiomatized 'measurement' itself and proved that the famous dividing line in the measurement chain can be moved at will without altering a single prediction — laying quantum mechanics' deepest conceptual puzzle on the table rather than sweeping it under the rug.

The second was the invention of game theory. In 1928 he proved the minimax theorem; in 1944, with the economist Oskar Morgenstern, he published Theory of Games and Economic Behavior, turning strategic situations — bargaining, poker, arms races, wherever 'my best move depends on yours' — into mathematics with theorems. Mathematics had previously modeled mindless nature; game theory made it confront opponents who calculate back. Economics, evolutionary biology and Cold War strategy were rewritten.

The third shaped the machine on which you are reading this sentence. The First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC (1945) proposed the stored-program architecture: program and data live in one memory, and instructions are themselves readable, writable data. Nearly every phone and computer today is still a 'von Neumann machine.' In his last years he turned to the border of computation and life: his theory of self-reproducing automata, predating the discovery of DNA's structure, derived from pure logic that a machine able to copy itself must carry and copy a description of itself; The Computer and the Brain opened the study of the brain as an information-processing system.

assessments.text: 「我有时怀疑，像冯·诺依曼这样的大脑，是否表明存在一个比人更高级的物种。」
被问及为何同时代的布达佩斯产出了那么多天才时答：天才只有一个，那就是冯·诺依曼。（转述）

assessments_en.text: 'I have sometimes wondered whether a brain like von Neumann's does not indicate a species superior to that of man.'
asked why Budapest of his generation produced so many geniuses, replied that there was only one genius: von Neumann. (as recounted)

quotes: 如果人们不相信数学是简单的，那只是因为他们没有意识到人生有多复杂。
给我四个参数，我能拟合一头大象；给我五个，我能让它摆动鼻子。（经费米、戴森转述）
对自己都没弄清在说什么的事，谈精确毫无意义。（大意）
quotes_en: If people do not believe that mathematics is simple, it is only because they do not realize how complicated life is.
With four parameters I can fit an elephant, and with five I can make him wiggle his trunk. (as recounted by Fermi and Dyson)
There's no sense in being precise when you don't even know what you are talking about. (paraphrased)
works: 《博弈论与经济行为》（与摩根斯坦合著）
works_en: Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (with Oskar Morgenstern)
First Draft of a Report on the EDVAC (the stored-program architecture)
vonneumann.lineage: 希尔伯特公理化纲领最锋利的继承人；在普林斯顿与图灵有直接交往，两人的名字分别刻在现代计算机的体系结构与理论模型上；博弈论经纳什、谢林等人之手长成整个学科；『技术奇点』一词的早期使用，也出自友人乌拉姆对他谈话的追记。
vonneumann.lineage_en: The sharpest heir to Hilbert's axiomatic program. At Princeton he knew Turing personally — their names are inscribed, respectively, on the architecture and the theoretical model of the modern computer. Game theory grew into a full discipline through Nash, Schelling and others; even the early use of the phrase 'technological singularity' comes from his friend Ulam's memoir of their conversations.
vonneumann.trivia: 六岁能心算八位数除法，据说能整页背诵电话簿以娱宾客；对自己唯一承认的不足是钢琴弹不好。车技出名地糟糕，普林斯顿一处路口因他屡屡出事被戏称『冯·诺依曼拐角』。他家的派对是普林斯顿最热闹的，他常在震耳的留声机音乐里同时演算。临终于病榻上仍为国防部做咨询，警卫守在门外——怕他昏迷中说出机密。
vonneumann.trivia_en: At six he could divide eight-digit numbers in his head, and reportedly recited pages of the phone book to amuse guests; the only deficiency he admitted to was his piano playing. His driving was notoriously bad — a Princeton intersection where he kept crashing was nicknamed 'von Neumann corner.' His parties were the liveliest in Princeton, and he often calculated through the blare of the gramophone. On his deathbed he was still consulting for the Defense Department, with a military guard at the door — lest he betray secrets in his sleep.

shannon.bio: 克劳德·艾尔伍德·香农(1916–2001)，美国数学家、电气工程师，被公认为『信息论之父』。他生于密歇根，1936 年在密歇根大学取得电气工程与数学双学位，后入麻省理工。1948 年在贝尔实验室发表《通信的数学理论》，凭一篇论文近乎独力开创了一整门学科。他一生兼具第一流的理论深度与孩子气的玩心，常把最严肃的问题当成游戏来玩。
shannon.bio_en: Claude Elwood Shannon (1916–2001) was an American mathematician and electrical engineer, universally regarded as the 'father of information theory.' Born in Michigan, he earned dual degrees in electrical engineering and mathematics at the University of Michigan (1936) before moving to MIT. In 1948, at Bell Labs, he published 'A Mathematical Theory of Communication,' founding an entire discipline almost single-handedly with a single paper. Throughout his life he paired first-rate theoretical depth with a childlike playfulness, forever treating the most serious problems as games.
shannon.ideas:
香农最深远的贡献，是教会世界如何『度量信息』。在他之前，信息是个模糊的日常词；他把它精确化：一条消息带来的信息量，等于它消除了多少不确定性。抛一枚公平硬币，结果带来的信息恰好是『1 比特』——比特(bit)这个基本单位，正是伴随他的理论被命名和推广的，如今是整个数字世界的计量单位。

他引入了『信息熵』：一个消息源越不可预测，它的熵越高、携带的信息越多；反过来，越是套路化、越容易被猜到的东西，信息量越低。这个公式与物理学统计力学里的『熵』形式相同——据香农回忆，是冯·诺依曼建议他借用『熵』这个名字的。

他还证明了两条改写了工程的定理。其一是『信道容量』：任何一条通信线路(电话线、光纤、无线电)每单位时间能可靠传输的信息量，都有一个由带宽与噪声决定的硬上限，越不过去。其二更反直觉——『有噪信道编码定理』：只要传输速率不超过这个容量，人就总能设计出一种编码，把出错率压到任意接近零。这意味着噪声不是宿命，可以靠巧妙的编码几乎完全战胜；今天的手机、硬盘、深空探测器能在杂讯里精确通信，根子都在这条定理。

而这一切的前提，是他做了一个大胆的切割：把信息从『意义』里剥离出来。一条消息对人而言是感人的情书还是一串股票代码，在工程上无关紧要；要紧的只是它从多少种可能里选出了哪一个。正是这种把语义悬置、只留下结构的抽象，让信息第一次能被数学处理，也让『信息』成了横跨通信、计算机、密码学、乃至生物学与神经科学的通用货币。
shannon.ideas_en:
Shannon's deepest contribution was teaching the world how to *measure* information. Before him, 'information' was a vague everyday word; he made it precise: the amount of information in a message equals how much uncertainty it removes. The toss of a fair coin carries exactly one 'bit' of information — and the bit, now the basic unit of the entire digital world, was named and popularized alongside his theory.

He introduced 'information entropy': the more unpredictable a source, the higher its entropy and the more information it carries; the more formulaic and guessable something is, the less it tells you. His formula has the same form as entropy in statistical mechanics — by Shannon's own account, it was von Neumann who suggested he borrow the name 'entropy.'

He also proved two theorems that rewrote engineering. The first is 'channel capacity': any communication line (a phone wire, an optical fiber, a radio link) has a hard ceiling, set by bandwidth and noise, on how much information it can reliably carry per unit time. The second is more counterintuitive — the 'noisy-channel coding theorem': as long as you transmit below that capacity, you can always design a code that pushes the error rate arbitrarily close to zero. Noise, in other words, is not destiny; clever coding can nearly defeat it. That your phone, hard drive, and deep-space probes can communicate flawlessly through static all traces back to this result.

All of it rested on one bold cut: he stripped information away from *meaning*. Whether a message is a tender love letter or a string of stock tickers is irrelevant to the engineering; all that matters is which of the many possibilities it selects. By suspending the semantics and keeping only the structure, he made information mathematically tractable for the first time — and turned 'information' into a common currency running across communication, computing, cryptography, and even biology and neuroscience.

assessments.text: （大意）香农几乎凭一己之力创立了信息论——不是改良某个已有领域，而是从无到有立起一门完整的学科，且一出手就近乎完备，后人几十年都在填他勾出的框架。
他 1937 年的硕士论文《继电器与开关电路的符号分析》把布尔代数与电路开关一一对应，奠定了一切数字电路与计算机逻辑设计的基础，常被誉为 20 世纪最重要的硕士论文之一。

assessments_en.text: (paraphrased) Shannon founded information theory almost single-handedly — not by improving an existing field but by raising a complete discipline from nothing, and arriving nearly fully formed; researchers spent decades filling in the framework he had sketched.

His 1937 master's thesis, 'A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits,' mapped Boolean algebra onto electrical switches one-to-one, laying the foundation for all digital circuitry and computer logic design — often called one of the most important master's theses of the twentieth century.

quotes: 通信的根本问题，是在一点精确或近似地重现在另一点选定的消息。
（大意）我一向只凭兴趣做事，很少考虑它有没有金钱价值、对世界有没有用——我在完全无用的东西上花了大量时间。
（大意）我只是好奇，事物到底是怎么拼装到一起的。
quotes_en: The fundamental problem of communication is that of reproducing at one point either exactly or approximately a message selected at another point.
(paraphrased) I have always pursued my interests without much regard to their financial value or value to the world — I've spent lots of time on totally useless things.
(paraphrased) I just wondered how things were put together.
works: 《通信的数学理论》(A Mathematical Theory of Communication, 1948)
《继电器与开关电路的符号分析》(硕士论文, 1937)
works_en: 'A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits' (master's thesis, 1937)
shannon.lineage: 上承 布尔的逻辑代数、奈奎斯特与哈特利对信息传输的早期量化，并与维纳的控制论同代呼应；下启 整个数字通信、数据压缩、纠错编码与现代密码学，其『信息』概念更被分子生物学、神经科学广泛借用。
shannon.lineage_en: He built on Boole's algebra of logic and the early attempts of Nyquist and Hartley to quantify transmission, and ran parallel to Wiener's cybernetics; downstream he launched all of digital communication, data compression, error-correcting codes and modern cryptography, while his notion of 'information' was widely borrowed by molecular biology and neuroscience.
shannon.trivia: 香农玩心极重：他会在贝尔实验室的走廊上一边骑独轮车一边抛接杂耍球；造过一只能自己走出迷宫的机械鼠『忒修斯』，是最早的机器学习演示之一；还做过一个『终极机器』——按下开关，盒子里伸出一只手把开关关掉，别无他用。他和数学家索普合作造过预测轮盘赌的可穿戴计算机，可能是世界上第一台。晚年他罹患阿尔茨海默症。
shannon.trivia_en: Shannon was irrepressibly playful: he would ride a unicycle down the halls of Bell Labs while juggling; he built 'Theseus,' a mechanical mouse that could find its own way out of a maze, one of the earliest demonstrations of machine learning; and he made an 'Ultimate Machine' whose only function was that, when you flipped its switch on, a hand emerged from the box to switch it off. With the mathematician Ed Thorp he built a wearable computer to predict roulette — possibly the world's first. In his later years he suffered from Alzheimer's disease.

marmot.bio: 1945–，英国流行病学家、伦敦大学学院教授。以『白厅研究』揭示健康的社会梯度而闻名，曾任世界卫生组织『健康社会决定因素委员会』主席、世界医学会主席。
marmot.bio_en: Born 1945, a British epidemiologist and professor at University College London, famous for the Whitehall studies revealing the social gradient in health. He chaired the WHO Commission on Social Determinants of Health and served as president of the World Medical Association.
marmot.ideas: 马尔莫追问一个反直觉的问题：在一群都有工作、都不算穷、都享有公费医疗的英国公务员里，为什么健康还会差这么多？『白厅研究』给出的答案是一条连续的『社会梯度』——从最高级到最低级，官阶每降一档，心脏病与全因死亡率就升一档，而且抽烟、血压、肥胖这些老风险因素加起来只能解释其中一小部分。他由此把因果重心从『生活方式』挪到两样更深的东西：对自己工作与生活的『掌控感』，以及地位本身带来的尊严与社会参与。低掌控、高要求的处境，通过长期的慢性应激，实实在在地折人寿命。他把这套发现推成一句公共卫生主张——不平等不是道德话题，而是一个可测量的健康问题：衡量它的尺子，应该是『它让底层折了多少寿』。他因此主张的对策不是劝个人往上爬（地位是零和的，人人都爬不可能人人受益），而是压平梯度、给每个人更多掌控与更公平的早年起点。
marmot.ideas_en: Marmot asks a counter-intuitive question: among British civil servants who all have jobs, aren't poor, and all enjoy public healthcare, why is health still so unequal? The Whitehall studies answer with a continuous social gradient — from the top grade to the bottom, each step down in rank brings a step up in heart disease and all-cause mortality, and the old risk factors like smoking, blood pressure and obesity together explain only a fraction of it. He therefore shifts the causal weight from lifestyle to two deeper things: how much control you have over your work and life, and the dignity and social participation that status itself confers. Low-control, high-demand conditions shorten lives for real, through chronic stress. He presses this into a public-health thesis: inequality is not a moral topic but a measurable health problem, best gauged by how much life it costs those at the bottom. His remedy is therefore not to urge individuals to climb (status is zero-sum; not everyone can benefit by climbing) but to flatten the gradient and give everyone more control and a fairer early start.

assessments.text: 『白厅研究』被视为社会流行病学的奠基性工作，把『社会决定因素』推上全球卫生议程。
有人质疑从相关到因果的跨度，以及『掌控感』这类变量在多大程度上能被政策直接干预。

assessments_en.text: The Whitehall studies are seen as foundational to social epidemiology, putting 'social determinants' on the global health agenda.
Some question the leap from correlation to causation, and how far variables like 'sense of control' can be directly acted on by policy.

quotes: 为什么处在社会阶梯较低一级的人，健康就要差一截？这道梯度贯穿了整个社会。（大意）
把健康的不平等留着不管，是一种社会的不公。（大意）
quotes_en: Why should those a rung lower on the social ladder have worse health? The gradient runs through the whole of society. (paraphrased)
To leave health inequalities unaddressed is a form of social injustice. (paraphrased)
works: WHO『用一代人弥合差距』报告
works_en: WHO 'Closing the Gap in a Generation' report
marmot.lineage: 承社会医学与流行病学传统，与威尔金森同属『不平等有害健康』一派；影响了各国『健康公平』政策与 WHO 议程。
marmot.lineage_en: He extends the traditions of social medicine and epidemiology, shares the 'inequality harms health' camp with Wilkinson, and has shaped health-equity policy and the WHO agenda in many countries.
marmot.trivia: 他因这项工作被封为爵士；常说自己研究的不是『病』，而是『病的成因的成因』(the causes of the causes)。
marmot.trivia_en: He was knighted for this work, and often says he studies not disease but 'the causes of the causes.'

wilkinson.bio: 1943–，英国社会流行病学家，诺丁汉大学荣休教授，与凯特·皮凯特合著《不平等的痛苦》(The Spirit Level)，并共同创办『平等信托』。
wilkinson.bio_en: Born 1943, a British social epidemiologist and emeritus professor at the University of Nottingham. With Kate Pickett he co-authored The Spirit Level and co-founded The Equality Trust.
wilkinson.ideas: 威尔金森想回答的问题是：为什么有些富裕国家问题成堆，另一些却安稳健康？他和皮凯特把二十多个富国、以及美国各州放到一起比对，得出一个尖锐结论——决定一个社会好坏的，往往不是它多有钱，而是它内部的收入差距有多大。在预期寿命、心理疾病、吸毒、肥胖、凶杀、青少年生育、监禁率、社会信任、阶层流动这一长串指标上，越不平等的社会几乎无一例外地更糟。更反直觉的是：受害的不只是穷人——在更不平等的社会里，连中产和富人也比在平等社会里的同侪过得差。他给的机制是心理社会的：巨大的差距把生活变成一场处处被评判的地位竞赛，『社会评价威胁』带来的长期焦虑与慢性压力，一点点侵蚀身心与彼此的信任。于是他主张，缩小差距不是劫富济贫式的慈善，而是让整个社会（包括上层）都活得更好的公共利益。
wilkinson.ideas_en: Wilkinson's question is: why are some rich countries riddled with problems while others are stable and healthy? With Pickett he lined up two dozen wealthy nations, and the US states, and reached a sharp conclusion — what makes a society better or worse is often not how rich it is but how large its internal income gap is. Across a long list of measures — life expectancy, mental illness, drug use, obesity, homicide, teen births, imprisonment, social trust, mobility — more unequal societies do worse almost without exception. More counter-intuitively, it is not only the poor who suffer: in more unequal societies even the middle class and the rich fare worse than their peers in equal ones. His mechanism is psychosocial: a wide gap turns life into a status contest where you are judged everywhere, and the chronic anxiety of 'social-evaluative threat' slowly erodes body, mind, and mutual trust. So narrowing the gap, he argues, is not charity that robs the rich but a public good that makes the whole society, top included, better off.

assessments.text: 《不平等的痛苦》被誉为把『不平等有害』从直觉变成可视化数据的畅销力作，深刻影响了公共辩论。
经济学家对其相关性证据、变量选择与因果推断提出争议，认为部分结论过强。

assessments_en.text: The Spirit Level is hailed as a bestseller that turned 'inequality is harmful' from intuition into vivid data, deeply shaping public debate.
Economists have contested its correlational evidence, variable choices and causal inference, arguing some conclusions are overstated.

quotes: 更平等的社会几乎在每一件事上都做得更好。（大意）
不平等之害不止落在穷人身上，它拉低了整个社会。（大意）
quotes_en: More equal societies almost always do better on nearly everything. (paraphrased)
The harm of inequality does not fall on the poor alone; it drags down the whole society. (paraphrased)
works: 《不平等的痛苦》(The Spirit Level，与凯特·皮凯特合著)
wilkinson.lineage: 承社会流行病学与理查德·蒂特马斯式的社会政策传统，与马尔莫同阵营；其数据方法也招致经济学界的方法论反驳。
wilkinson.lineage_en: He extends social epidemiology and a Titmuss-style social-policy tradition, sharing a camp with Marmot; his data methods have also drawn methodological rebuttals from economists.
wilkinson.trivia: 他与皮凯特为推广书中理念创办了『平等信托』；《不平等的痛苦》书名 The Spirit Level 一语双关，既指木匠的水平仪，也指社会的『心气水平』。
wilkinson.trivia_en: He and Pickett founded The Equality Trust to spread the book's ideas; the title 'The Spirit Level' puns on a carpenter's level and the mood-level of a society.

illich.bio: 1926–2002，奥地利裔思想家、还俗的天主教神父，激进的现代制度批评家，以对医疗、教育、交通等大制度的根本批判闻名。
illich.bio_en: Born 1926, died 2002; an Austrian-born thinker and former Catholic priest, a radical critic of modern institutions, famous for his fundamental critiques of medicine, education, and transport.
illich.ideas: 伊里奇的招牌论点是『反生产力』：现代的大制度发展到一定规模，会反过来摧毁它本要服务的目标。医疗是最有名的例子。在《医学的报复》里他提出『医源性疾病』(iatrogenesis)，分三层：临床医源病——药物副作用、误诊、过度治疗直接把人弄伤弄病；社会医源病——医疗系统把越来越多的正常人生状态（出生、衰老、痛苦、死亡）重新定义成需要专业干预的『医疗问题』，让人一步步丧失自己照料自己的能力；文化医源病——医疗抽走了一个文化原本用来面对痛苦与死亡的意义框架，让人连怎么受苦、怎么死去都要交给专家。他的结论不是『要更多更好的医疗』，而是把健康的自主权还给普通人：重建一个节制的、人人能掌控工具而非被工具与专家反噬的『欢愉』社会。
illich.ideas_en: Illich's signature idea is counterproductivity: a modern institution, grown past a certain scale, starts to destroy the very goal it was meant to serve. Medicine is his most famous case. In Medical Nemesis he names iatrogenesis in three layers: clinical — drugs, misdiagnosis, and overtreatment that directly injure; social — the medical system redefining ever more ordinary states of life (birth, aging, pain, death) as 'medical problems' requiring experts, so people lose the capacity to care for themselves; and cultural — medicine stripping away the framework a culture once used to face suffering and death, so that even how to suffer and how to die is handed to specialists. His conclusion is not 'more and better medicine' but returning health autonomy to ordinary people: rebuilding a restrained, 'convivial' society where people command their tools rather than being consumed by tools and experts.

assessments.text: 《医学的报复》被视为对现代医疗最深刻的制度性批判之一，深刻影响了病人自主与去医疗化的讨论。
批评者认为他低估了现代医学（疫苗、抗生素、外科）实打实的救命成就，论点有过度浪漫化之嫌。

assessments_en.text: Medical Nemesis is seen as one of the deepest institutional critiques of modern medicine, shaping debates on patient autonomy and de-medicalization.
Critics argue he underrates the real life-saving gains of modern medicine (vaccines, antibiotics, surgery) and romanticizes his case.

quotes: 医疗行业本身已成为健康的一大威胁。（大意）
一个社会最深的病，是它让人丧失了自己面对痛苦与死亡的能力。（大意）
quotes_en: The medical establishment has become a major threat to health. (paraphrased)
A society's deepest sickness is that it strips people of the power to face suffering and death themselves. (paraphrased)
illich.lineage: 承无政府主义与制度批判传统；与福柯的『生命权力』相呼应又不同；影响了病人自主、去医疗化与『慢医学』等运动。
illich.lineage_en: He extends anarchist and institution-critique traditions, echoing yet differing from Foucault's 'biopower,' and has influenced patient autonomy, de-medicalization, and 'slow medicine' movements.
illich.trivia: 晚年他脸上长了一个巨大的肿瘤，却拒绝主流的手术与止痛，选择用自己的方式面对——以身践行他毕生的主张。
illich.trivia_en: In his last years he refused mainstream surgery and painkillers for a large facial tumor, choosing to face it on his own terms — living out the argument of his life's work.

szasz.bio: 1920–2012，匈牙利裔美国精神病学家、纽约州立大学教授，古典自由主义者，以《精神病的神话》与对强制精神医学的批判闻名。
szasz.bio_en: Born 1920, died 2012; a Hungarian-born American psychiatrist and professor at SUNY, a classical liberal, famous for The Myth of Mental Illness and his critique of coercive psychiatry.
szasz.ideas: 萨斯毕生的核心主张极具挑衅性：严格说来，『精神病』不是病。他区分得很硬——真正的『病』是身体（器官、组织、生化）的可查病变；而抑郁、焦虑、精神分裂被称作『病』，其实是一个隐喻：我们把『生活中的困境』和『偏离常规的行为』用医学语言重新包装了。在《精神病的神话》里他警告，这个隐喻一旦被当真，就打开两扇危险的门：其一，免除个人的责任与能动——『不是我的错，是我的病』；其二，给国家用『治疗』的名义强制干预、剥夺自由（非自愿住院、强制用药）提供了正当性。他因此毕生反对精神科的强制权力，捍卫每个人对自己身心的自主权、以及随之而来的责任。要点是：他并不否认人会痛苦、会行为异常，他反对的是把这些一律医学化、并交给强制性的机构去处理。
szasz.ideas_en: Szasz's lifelong thesis is deliberately provocative: strictly speaking, 'mental illness' is not an illness. He draws a hard line — a real 'disease' is a demonstrable bodily lesion (organ, tissue, biochemistry); calling depression, anxiety, or schizophrenia a 'disease' is a metaphor, repackaging 'problems in living' and behavior that deviates from the norm in medical language. In The Myth of Mental Illness he warns that once the metaphor is taken literally, it opens two dangerous doors: it excuses personal responsibility and agency ('not my fault, it's my illness'), and it legitimizes the state's coercive intervention in the name of 'treatment' (involuntary commitment, forced medication). He therefore opposed coercive psychiatry all his life and defended each person's autonomy over their own mind and body, and the responsibility that comes with it. The key: he does not deny that people suffer or behave abnormally — he opposes medicalizing all of it and handing it to coercive institutions.

assessments.text: 被奉为反强制精神医学与个人自由的旗手，对病人权利与知情同意运动影响深远。
多数精神科医生认为他走得太远——否认精神疾病的现实会让重症患者得不到必要治疗。

assessments_en.text: Hailed as a standard-bearer against coercive psychiatry and for individual liberty, deeply influencing patients' rights and informed consent.
Most psychiatrists think he went too far — denying the reality of mental illness can leave severely ill patients without needed care.

quotes: 身体才会得病；心灵得的是隐喻的病。（大意）
精神病学的关键问题不是诊断，而是强制。（大意）
quotes_en: The body has diseases; the mind has them only metaphorically. (paraphrased)
The core issue in psychiatry is not diagnosis but coercion. (paraphrased)
works: 《精神病的神话》(The Myth of Mental Illness)
szasz.lineage: 承古典自由主义（密尔式的自主与责任），与反精神病学运动同期而立场独特；与主流生物精神病学、以及福柯的规训分析各有交锋。
szasz.lineage_en: He extends classical liberalism (Millian autonomy and responsibility), stands alongside yet apart from the anti-psychiatry movement, and clashes with both mainstream biological psychiatry and Foucault's analysis of discipline.
szasz.trivia: 他是自由至上主义组织的共同创始人之一，坚持行医时从不违背病人意愿用药或收治——把理论贯彻到自己的临床。
szasz.trivia_en: A co-founder of a libertarian anti-coercion group, he refused throughout his practice to medicate or commit patients against their will — carrying his theory into his own clinic.

piaget.bio: 让·皮亚杰（1896–1980）是瑞士心理学家、哲学家，二十世纪最有影响力的发展心理学家之一，被称为『发生认识论』的创立者。他少年时代痴迷生物学，十岁左右就发表关于软体动物的论文。后来他把研究儿童如何一步步建立起对世界的理解当作毕生课题，长期在日内瓦工作，甚至以细致观察自己三个孩子的成长作为研究素材。他的理论深刻改变了人们对儿童、学习与教育的看法。
piaget.bio_en: Jean Piaget (1896–1980) was a Swiss psychologist and philosopher, one of the most influential developmental psychologists of the twentieth century and the founder of 'genetic epistemology.' As a boy he was captivated by biology, publishing a paper on molluscs around the age of ten. He later made it his life's work to study how children build up, step by step, their understanding of the world; he worked for decades in Geneva and even used meticulous observation of his own three children as research material. His theory profoundly changed how people think about children, learning and education.
piaget.ideas:
皮亚杰最核心的洞见是：儿童不是『小大人』，也不是被动接受灌输的容器，而是**主动的建构者**——他们像小科学家一样，通过与世界互动，自己一点点搭建起理解。这就是『建构主义』。他用两个概念解释这个过程：『同化』（把新经验塞进已有的认识框架）与『顺应』（当旧框架装不下时，改造框架本身）；两者的反复平衡（『平衡化』）推动认识不断升级。

他提出著名的认知发展四阶段：感知运动期（婴儿靠动作和感官认识世界，逐渐懂得『看不见的东西仍然存在』）、前运算期（会用语言符号，但思维自我中心、易被表象迷惑）、具体运算期（能进行逻辑推理，懂得『水倒进不同杯子总量不变』的守恒）、形式运算期（青少年能作抽象和假设性思考）。关键在于，这些阶段有大致的顺序和成熟节奏，**你无法把高阶的理解硬塞给尚未准备好的孩子**——揠苗助长行不通。

他还专门研究儿童的道德判断，写了《儿童的道德判断》。他发现小孩子最初持一种『他律』道德：规则是大人定的、神圣不可违、按后果大小判对错；随着与同伴平等地游戏、协商、轮流，他们逐渐转向『自律』道德——懂得规则是人们约定的、可以商量，看重动机与公平。这意味着道德感很大程度上是在互动中长出来的，而非单靠说教灌输。
piaget.ideas_en:
Piaget's central insight is that a child is not a 'little adult,' nor a passive vessel to be filled, but **an active builder** — like a small scientist, constructing understanding piece by piece through interaction with the world. This is 'constructivism.' He explained the process with two concepts: 'assimilation' (fitting new experience into an existing mental framework) and 'accommodation' (reshaping the framework itself when the old one will not stretch); the repeated balancing of the two ('equilibration') drives understanding to ever higher levels.

He proposed his famous four stages of cognitive development: the sensorimotor stage (the infant knows the world through action and the senses, gradually grasping that 'a thing still exists when out of sight'); the preoperational stage (able to use language and symbols, but self-centred in thought and easily misled by appearances); the concrete operational stage (capable of logical reasoning, grasping 'conservation' — that a quantity of water poured into different glasses stays the same); and the formal operational stage (adolescents able to think abstractly and hypothetically). Crucially, these stages come in a rough order and ripen at their own pace, and **you cannot cram a higher understanding into a child who is not yet ready** — forcing the seedling does not work.

He also studied children's moral judgement specifically, writing The Moral Judgment of the Child. He found that young children first hold a 'heteronomous' morality: rules are laid down by adults, sacred and unbreakable, and right and wrong are judged by the size of the consequence; but as they play, negotiate and take turns as equals with peers, they shift toward an 'autonomous' morality — grasping that rules are agreements people make and can revise, and weighing intention and fairness. This implies that a moral sense grows largely out of interaction, not out of instruction alone.

assessments.text: 在皮亚杰道德发展研究的基础上，进一步提出著名的『道德发展三水平六阶段』，将其框架发扬光大。
在肯定其贡献的同时提出批评，认为皮亚杰低估了社会、语言与文化对认知发展的塑造作用，主张学习可以走在发展之前。

assessments_en.text: Building on Piaget's study of moral development, went on to propose his famous 'three levels and six stages' of moral reasoning, extending and popularising the framework.

While acknowledging his contribution, criticised him for underestimating the role of society, language and culture in shaping cognitive development, arguing that learning can run ahead of development.

quotes: 教育的目标，是培养能够创新、而非只会重复前人所为的人。（大意）
智力，就是当你不知道该怎么办时所动用的东西。（大意）
每当我们过早地教给孩子一样他本可以自己发现的东西，就妨碍了他去真正发明它、从而彻底理解它。（大意）
quotes_en: The goal of education is to create people capable of doing new things, not simply repeating what other generations have done. (paraphrased)
Intelligence is what you use when you don't know what to do. (paraphrased)
Each time we teach a child something too early, we keep him from inventing it himself, and so from understanding it completely. (paraphrased)
works_en: The Moral Judgment of the Child
The Origins of Intelligence in Children
The Language and Thought of the Child
piaget.lineage: 早年融合生物学与康德式的认识论问题，转向以实证方法研究认识的发生。他创立日内瓦学派，深刻影响发展心理学、认知科学与建构主义教育；柯尔伯格的道德发展论直接承其衣钵，维果茨基则从社会文化角度与之对话、互补。
piaget.lineage_en: Early on he fused biology with Kantian questions about knowledge, then turned to studying the genesis of knowledge by empirical means. He founded the Geneva school and profoundly shaped developmental psychology, cognitive science and constructivist education; Kohlberg's theory of moral development directly inherited his mantle, while Vygotsky engaged and complemented him from a sociocultural angle.
piaget.trivia: 皮亚杰研究的许多经典发现，来自他对自己三个孩子婴幼儿期近乎实验般的日常观察——他会一次次把玩具藏起来，看孩子何时开始去寻找看不见的东西，由此揭示『客体永久性』的形成。把家庭育儿现场变成一流的科学实验室，是他独特的研究方式。
piaget.trivia_en: Many of Piaget's classic findings came from his almost experimental daily observation of his own three children in infancy — again and again he would hide a toy to see when the child began to search for what was out of sight, revealing how 'object permanence' forms. Turning the domestic scene of child-rearing into a first-rate scientific laboratory was his distinctive way of working.

lecun.bio: 1960 年生于巴黎，法裔美国计算机科学家，深度学习的奠基者之一。1980 年代末在贝尔实验室把反向传播用于手写识别，做出最早能实用的卷积神经网络，一度为全美银行读取大量支票。2013 年创立 Facebook（Meta）人工智能研究院 FAIR 并任首席 AI 科学家，同时任教纽约大学。2018 年与辛顿、本吉奥共获图灵奖，三人被称为『深度学习三巨头』。
lecun.bio_en: Born in Paris in 1960, a French-American computer scientist and a founder of deep learning. In the late 1980s at Bell Labs he applied backpropagation to handwriting recognition, producing the first practical convolutional neural networks, which at one point read a large share of the checks in the United States. In 2013 he founded FAIR, Facebook (Meta)'s AI research lab, serving as Chief AI Scientist, while also teaching at New York University. In 2018 he shared the Turing Award with Hinton and Bengio, the three being dubbed the 'godfathers of deep learning.'
lecun.ideas:
杨立昆的核心贡献是卷积神经网络（CNN）。要理解它，先想想大脑怎么看东西：你认出一只猫，靠的不是记住它出现在画面哪个角落，而是抓住『尖耳朵、胡须、毛皮』这些局部特征，无论它在左边还是右边。CNN 就是把这个思路搬进机器——用一小块『滤镜』在整张图上滑动，逐层把边缘拼成纹理、纹理拼成部件、部件拼成整体。这个『局部感受、层层抽象、位置无关』的设计，是今天几乎所有图像识别、人脸解锁、自动驾驶视觉的地基。
他更大的主张，是给机器学习指方向。当下最火的做法叫『监督学习』——喂给机器几百万张贴好标签的图（这是猫、那是狗），它照着学。杨立昆认为这条路太贵也太笨：人类小孩不需要有人给世界贴几百万个标签，光是睁眼看、伸手碰，就无师自通地懂了重力、因果、物体不会凭空消失。他把希望押在『自监督学习』上——让机器像孩子一样，通过预测『被遮住的下一帧会是什么』来自己教自己，从海量未标注的数据里长出对世界的常识。
由此引出他念兹在兹的『世界模型』：一个真正智能的系统，脑子里得有一套对世界如何运作的内部模拟，才能预测后果、提前规划、举一反三。他据此批评当前的大语言模型——它们靠预测下一个词，把人类文字里的规律压缩得极好，却没有一个扎根于物理世界的模型，所以会一本正经地说出违反常识的话。他有句流传很广的话：今天最强的 AI，对真实世界的理解还不如一只家猫。
他也是最著名的『反末日论』者。当很多人担心超级智能即将失控、危及人类，他反驳说：能规划、有自主意图的机器智能还根本不存在，为一个尚未造出的东西恐慌，是本末倒置；真正该做的是把它造出来、并像对待任何技术那样一步步加装安全护栏。他还是开源 AI 的坚定拥护者，主张把强大的模型公开，让全世界共同监督、改进，而不是锁在少数几家公司手里。
lecun.ideas_en:
LeCun's central contribution is the convolutional neural network (CNN). To grasp it, think about how a brain sees: you recognize a cat not by memorizing which corner of the frame it sits in, but by catching local features — pointed ears, whiskers, fur — wherever they appear. The CNN carries this idea into a machine: a small 'filter' slides across the whole image, layer by layer assembling edges into textures, textures into parts, parts into wholes. This design — local perception, layered abstraction, position-independence — is the foundation of almost all image recognition, face unlock, and self-driving vision today.
His larger claim is about where machine learning should head. The dominant method now is 'supervised learning' — feed the machine millions of labeled images (this is a cat, that a dog) and it learns by imitation. LeCun thinks this path is too costly and too dull: a human child doesn't need the world labeled millions of times; just by looking and reaching it grasps gravity, causation, and that objects don't vanish into thin air. He bets instead on 'self-supervised learning' — letting a machine teach itself, like a child, by predicting 'what the hidden next frame will be,' growing common sense about the world from vast unlabeled data.
From this comes the 'world model' he keeps returning to: a genuinely intelligent system needs an internal simulation of how the world works, so it can predict consequences, plan ahead, and generalize. On this basis he criticizes today's large language models — by predicting the next word they compress the regularities of human text superbly, yet have no model grounded in the physical world, so they will state, with a straight face, things that violate common sense. A widely quoted line of his: the strongest AI today understands the real world less well than a house cat.
He is also the best-known 'anti-doomer.' As many worry that superintelligence is about to slip loose and threaten humanity, he counters that machine intelligence able to plan and to hold autonomous intentions does not yet exist at all; panicking over a thing not yet built is backwards. What we should do is build it and, as with any technology, bolt on safeguards step by step. He is likewise a firm champion of open-source AI, arguing that powerful models should be public — so the whole world can watch and improve them — rather than locked inside a few companies.

assessments.text: 表彰他与本吉奥、辛顿在深度神经网络上的概念与工程突破，使深度学习成为现代计算的关键组成部分。

assessments.by: 杰弗里·辛顿（图灵奖共同得主）
assessments.text: 在深度学习的功绩上与他并称，但两人在『AI 是否构成生存性风险』上公开分歧——辛顿深忧，他则一贯淡然。（大意）

assessments_en.text: Honoring him, with Bengio and Hinton, for conceptual and engineering breakthroughs in deep neural networks that made deep learning a critical component of modern computing.
Named alongside him for the achievements of deep learning, yet the two disagree publicly on whether AI poses an existential risk — Hinton deeply worried, LeCun consistently unruffled. (paraphrased)

quotes: 革命不会有监督。（『The revolution will not be supervised』—— 他著名演讲的标题，双关：真正的智能突破将来自自监督学习。）
今天最强的 AI，对世界的理解还不如一只猫或一个四岁孩子。（大意）
没有世界模型、不会规划的系统，谈不上真正的智能。（大意）
担心超级智能统治人类，就像还没造出喷气客机就先怕它撞楼——那东西还不存在。（大意）
quotes_en: The revolution will not be supervised. (The title of a famous talk — a pun: the real breakthrough in intelligence will come from self-supervised learning.)
The most advanced AI today understands the world less well than a cat or a four-year-old child. (paraphrased)
A system with no world model and no ability to plan is not truly intelligent. (paraphrased)
Worrying that superintelligence will dominate humanity is like fearing a jetliner will crash into buildings before the jetliner has even been built — the thing doesn't exist yet. (paraphrased)
works: 《基于梯度的学习应用于文档识别》(Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition, 1998) —— 卷积网络 LeNet 的奠基论文
《深度学习》(Deep Learning) —— 与本吉奥、辛顿合著的《自然》综述, 2015
《一条通向自主机器智能的道路》(A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence, 2022) —— 阐述世界模型与 JEPA 的立场文件
works_en: 'Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition' (1998) — the founding paper of the LeNet convolutional network
'Deep Learning' — a Nature review co-authored with Bengio and Hinton, 2015
'A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence' (2022) — a position paper laying out world models and JEPA
lecun.lineage: 思想上承接福岛邦彦的『神经认知机』与鲁梅尔哈特等人的反向传播算法，早年在辛顿门下做博士后。1980 年代末于贝尔实验室把这些理念落成能读支票的实用系统；2013 年创立 Meta 的 FAIR，与本吉奥、辛顿共同点燃了 2010 年代的深度学习浪潮，门下与合作者遍布今日 AI 学界与工业界。
lecun.lineage_en: Intellectually he builds on Kunihiko Fukushima's 'Neocognitron' and on the backpropagation algorithm of Rumelhart and others, and did his postdoc under Hinton. At Bell Labs in the late 1980s he turned these ideas into a practical check-reading system; in 2013 he founded Meta's FAIR, and together with Bengio and Hinton lit the deep-learning wave of the 2010s, his students and collaborators now spread across AI academia and industry.
lecun.trivia: 他的姓氏原写作『Le Cun』，为免英语读者误当中间名，后来连写成 LeCun。在 AT&T 期间，他还与同事共同发明了 DjVu 图像压缩格式，用于高效存储扫描文档。三位『深度学习教父』里，他以直率好辩、活跃于社交媒体、爱用工程现实给热潮泼冷水著称。
lecun.trivia_en: His surname was originally written 'Le Cun'; to keep English readers from mistaking 'Cun' for a middle name, he later joined it into 'LeCun.'
