While at AT&T he also co-invented the DjVu image-compression format for storing scanned documents efficiently. Of the three 'godfathers of deep learning,' he is the blunt, argumentative one — active on social media and fond of pouring engineering cold water on hype.

godel.bio: 1906–1978，出生于奥匈帝国布尔诺（今属捷克）的逻辑学家、数学家，二十世纪最伟大的逻辑学家，与亚里士多德并称。年轻时活跃于维也纳，与『维也纳学派』往来，却始终是坚定的柏拉图主义者。1931 年发表『不完备定理』，震动整个数学基础界。1940 年为躲避纳粹迁居美国，任普林斯顿高等研究院终身教授，与爱因斯坦结为至交。晚年患严重的被害妄想，惧怕被下毒；1978 年因拒绝进食、极度消瘦而去世。
godel.bio_en: 1906–1978, a logician and mathematician born in Brno (then Austria-Hungary, now the Czech Republic), the greatest logician of the twentieth century, often ranked beside Aristotle. Active in his youth in Vienna and in contact with the 'Vienna Circle,' he remained nonetheless a committed Platonist. In 1931 he published his incompleteness theorems, shaking the entire field of the foundations of mathematics. In 1940, fleeing the Nazis, he moved to the United States as a permanent member of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, where he became a close friend of Einstein. In later life he suffered severe persecutory delusions, fearing he would be poisoned; he died in 1978, refusing to eat and severely emaciated.
godel.ideas:
哥德尔一生最著名的贡献，是 1931 年的『不完备定理』。在此之前，希尔伯特等人怀抱一个宏大的梦想：为全部数学找到一组稳固的公理，再用严格的机械规则，把所有真命题都证明出来——让数学变成一座地基完美、无懈可击的大厦。哥德尔用一个惊人的构造击碎了这个梦。
他的核心手法叫『哥德尔编码』：把每一个数学命题、每一步证明，都编成一个独一无二的数字。这样一来，『某命题能否被证明』这种关于数学的问题，本身也变成了一道算术题，数学第一次能够谈论它自己。借此他造出了一个自指的命题，大意是『这句话在本系统内无法被证明』。你若能证明它，它就成了假的，系统就自相矛盾；你若证不出它，它恰恰说了实话——于是它是一个『真的、却无法证明』的命题。
第一不完备定理由此断言：任何足够丰富、又不自相矛盾的形式系统，内部都必有真而不可证的命题。第二定理更釜底抽薪：这样的系统，连『我自己不会自相矛盾』这件事都无法在内部证明。这并不是说数学不可靠，而是说：真理，永远大于任何一套我们能写下的规则；证明能到达的地方，是有边界的。
哥德尔本人从中读出的，是坚定的『数学柏拉图主义』：正因为真溢出了规则，数学对象必是独立于人心的实在，我们靠一种类似知觉的『数学直觉』去把握它。他还有两项杰作：证明了『选择公理』与『连续统假设』与现有数学不矛盾（后来科恩证明它们也无法被证明，二人合起来说明连续统假设『独立』于标准数学）；以及 1949 年为爱因斯坦的引力方程找到一个惊人的旋转宇宙解，其中时间可以绕回自身、原则上允许回到过去——他借此论证时间的『流逝』或许只是幻觉。
godel.ideas_en:
Gödel's most famous contribution is the incompleteness theorems of 1931. Before them, Hilbert and others cherished a grand dream: to find, for all of mathematics, a firm set of axioms and, by strict mechanical rules, to prove every true statement — to make mathematics a building with a perfect, unassailable foundation. Gödel shattered that dream with a single astonishing construction.
His core device is now called 'Gödel numbering': he encoded every mathematical statement and every step of a proof as a unique number. At a stroke, questions about mathematics — such as 'can this statement be proved?' — themselves became arithmetic problems, and mathematics could, for the first time, talk about itself. With this he built a self-referential statement saying, in effect, 'this sentence cannot be proved within this system.' If you could prove it, it would be false and the system would contradict itself; if you could not, it would be telling the truth — and so it is a statement that is true yet unprovable.
The first incompleteness theorem thus asserts: any sufficiently rich and consistent formal system must contain statements that are true but unprovable within it. The second cuts deeper still: such a system cannot even prove its own consistency from within. This does not mean mathematics is unreliable; it means that truth is forever larger than any set of rules we can write down — that what proof can reach has a boundary.
Gödel himself read from this a firm 'mathematical Platonism': precisely because truth overflows the rules, mathematical objects must be a reality independent of the human mind, grasped through a perception-like 'mathematical intuition.' He achieved two other masterworks: he proved that the 'axiom of choice' and the 'continuum hypothesis' are consistent with existing mathematics (Cohen later proved they also cannot be proved, and together they showed the continuum hypothesis 'independent' of standard mathematics); and in 1949 he found a startling rotating-universe solution to Einstein's gravitational equations, in which time can loop back on itself and, in principle, allow a return to the past — from which he argued that the 'passage' of time may be only an illusion.

assessments.text: 称哥德尔为亚里士多德以来最伟大的逻辑学家，认为其成就在逻辑史上无可替代。1931 年听闻不完备定理后，他随即中止了自己在相近方向的研究。
晚年曾说，自己之所以还愿意去研究院，多半是为了能有和哥德尔一起散步回家的殊荣。
普遍视不完备定理为二十世纪数学与哲学的分水岭，深刻影响了可计算性理论、数学基础与心灵哲学。

assessments_en.text: Called Gödel the greatest logician since Aristotle and held his achievement irreplaceable in the history of logic. On learning of the incompleteness theorem in 1931, he abandoned his own work in a nearby direction.
Said in later years that his own work had by then meant little to him, and that he came to the Institute mainly for the privilege of walking home with Gödel.

Widely regard the incompleteness theorems as a watershed of twentieth-century mathematics and philosophy, deeply shaping computability theory, the foundations of mathematics and the philosophy of mind.

quotes: 任何一个能表达算术的、无矛盾的形式系统，都存在它证明不了的真命题。
要么数学大到人的心智无法容纳，要么人的心智不只是一台机器。（大意 / 据转述）
我不相信自然科学，但我相信数学。（大意 / 据转述）
quotes_en: In any consistent formal system able to express arithmetic, there are true statements it cannot prove.
Either mathematics is too big for the human mind, or the human mind is more than a machine. (paraphrased / as reported)
I don't believe in natural science, but I do believe in mathematics. (paraphrased / as reported)
works: 《论〈数学原理〉及相关系统中形式不可判定的命题》（1931）
《什么是康托尔的连续统问题？》（1947）
works_en: On Formally Undecidable Propositions of Principia Mathematica and Related Systems (1931)
The Consistency of the Continuum Hypothesis (1940)
godel.lineage: 承接弗雷格、罗素以逻辑奠定数学的『逻辑主义』传统，又直接回应并瓦解了希尔伯特的形式主义纲领。在普林斯顿与爱因斯坦、冯·诺依曼、摩根斯特恩交往密切。其不完备定理深刻影响图灵的可计算性理论；连续统问题上的工作由保罗·科恩接续完成，二人共获这一问题『独立性』的结论。
godel.lineage_en: He inherited the 'logicist' tradition of Frege and Russell, who sought to ground mathematics in logic, and directly answered and undid Hilbert's formalist program. In Princeton he was close to Einstein, von Neumann and Morgenstern. His incompleteness theorems deeply shaped Turing's theory of computability; his work on the continuum problem was completed by Paul Cohen, the two together yielding its 'independence.'
godel.trivia: 申请美国公民时，据说他认真研究了美国宪法，宣称发现其中有一个逻辑漏洞、足以让美国合法地变成独裁国家；陪同他出席入籍面试的爱因斯坦与摩根斯特恩一路担心他会当场对法官讲这套，险些坏事。他一生患严重的被害妄想与疑病症，只信任妻子阿黛尔为他做的饭；1978 年阿黛尔住院期间，他因拒绝进食而饿死，去世时体重仅约 30 公斤。
godel.trivia_en: When applying for U.S. citizenship, he is said to have studied the Constitution so seriously that he announced he had found a logical loophole that could legally turn America into a dictatorship; Einstein and Morgenstern, who accompanied him to the naturalization interview, worried the whole way that he would explain this to the judge and nearly ruin it. All his life he suffered severe persecutory delusions and hypochondria, trusting only the food his wife Adele prepared; in 1978, while Adele was hospitalized, he starved himself to death, weighing only about 30 kilograms at the end.

dehaene.bio: 1965 年生，法国认知神经科学家，法兰西公学院实验认知心理学讲席教授，NeuroSpin 脑成像中心认知神经影像团队负责人。早年受数学训练，后转向心理学，师从神经科学家让-皮埃尔·尚热与心理语言学家雅克·梅勒。他用行为实验与脑成像研究人脑如何处理数字、阅读与意识，是『数感』研究的开创者之一。著有《数感》《脑的阅读》《意识与大脑》《我们如何学习》等，皆为畅销科普。2018 年起主持法国国民教育科学委员会，推动以实证为据的教学改革。
dehaene.bio_en: Born 1965, a French cognitive neuroscientist, professor of experimental cognitive psychology at the Collège de France and head of the cognitive neuroimaging unit at the NeuroSpin brain-imaging center. Trained first in mathematics, he turned to psychology under the neuroscientist Jean-Pierre Changeux and the psycholinguist Jacques Mehler. Using behavioral experiments and brain imaging, he studies how the human brain processes number, reading and consciousness, and is a founder of research on the 'number sense.' His books — The Number Sense, Reading in the Brain, Consciousness and the Brain, How We Learn — are all popular-science bestsellers. Since 2018 he has chaired France's scientific council for national education, pressing for evidence-based teaching reform.
dehaene.ideas:
德阿纳最核心的发现，是人类并非白纸一张地面对数字。他大量实验表明：出生几天的婴儿、乃至猴子和乌鸦，都能不数数就分辨『三个』和『五个』这样的粗略数量。这套与生俱来的能力叫『近似数量系统』，通俗地说就是『数感』，它主要落在大脑顶叶的一小片区域。数越接近就越难分辨（3 和 4 难，3 和 30 易），这被称作『距离效应』——它像是刻在神经里的一把模糊的尺。
在此基础上，他提出了两个影响深远的观点。其一是『三重编码模型』：我们处理数字时，会在三种表征间切换——听说读写的语言符号（『七』）、纸面上的阿拉伯数码（『7』）、以及那把心里的、空间化的『数轴』（他发现人往往把小数放在左、大数放在右，即所谓 SNARC 效应）。其二，也是他最大胆的假说——『神经元回收』：像阅读、算术这样几千年前才出现的文化发明，来不及演化出专属脑区，于是『征用』了大脑里本为别的用途（如识别物体、感知空间）准备好的皮层，加以改造挪用。这解释了一个惊人的事实：全世界不同文字的读者，脑中负责识字的竟是同一小块区域。
他把同样的思路推向意识研究，与尚热共同提出『全局神经工作空间』理论：一个信息之所以变成『你意识到了』，是因为它被广播到全脑、供各个系统共享；意识不是某个神秘火花，而是一次全脑范围的『点亮』与共享。
这些研究还有一个温暖的现实指向：既然人人都带着数感的生物底子，学不好数学、读不好书，多半是教学方法与经历的问题，而非天生的定数。他因此大力倡导循证教育——重视注意力、主动参与、及时反馈与间隔复习这四大学习支柱。
dehaene.ideas_en:
Dehaene's central finding is that humans do not face numbers as blank slates. His many experiments show that infants only days old — and monkeys and crows too — can tell 'three' from 'five' as rough quantities without counting. This innate capacity is the 'approximate number system,' or in plain terms the 'number sense,' and it sits mainly in a small region of the brain's parietal lobe. The closer two numbers are, the harder they are to tell apart (3 versus 4 is hard, 3 versus 30 easy), a 'distance effect' — like a blurry ruler etched into the nervous system.
On this base he advanced two far-reaching ideas. The first is the 'triple-code model': in handling numbers we switch among three representations — the spoken or written word ('seven'), the Arabic digit on the page ('7'), and an inner, spatial 'number line' (he found people tend to place small numbers on the left and large on the right, the so-called SNARC effect). The second, his boldest hypothesis, is 'neuronal recycling': cultural inventions such as reading and arithmetic, only a few thousand years old, had no time to evolve dedicated brain areas, so they 'commandeer' cortex prepared for other purposes (recognizing objects, sensing space) and repurpose it. This explains a striking fact: readers of utterly different scripts around the world use the very same small brain region to recognize written words.
He carried the same reasoning into the study of consciousness, proposing with Changeux the 'global neuronal workspace' theory: a piece of information becomes something 'you are conscious of' when it is broadcast across the whole brain to be shared by many systems; consciousness is not a mysterious spark but a brain-wide 'ignition' and sharing.
This research carries a warm practical implication: since everyone carries the biological floor of a number sense, failing at mathematics or reading is mostly a matter of method and history, not a fixed fate. He is therefore a strong advocate of evidence-based education, stressing the four pillars of learning — attention, active engagement, prompt feedback and spaced review.

assessments.text: 公认为数字认知与阅读神经科学的奠基人物之一，其『数感』与『神经元回收』框架被广泛引用，推动了『教育神经科学』这一交叉领域的成形。
作为其师与长期合作者，与他共同发展『全局神经工作空间』理论，视其为把严谨实验带入意识研究的代表人物。
其著作以清晰、实证、善用比喻著称，被广泛认为在弥合脑科学与日常教育、阅读之间做出了罕见贡献。

assessments_en.text: Widely regarded as a founder of the neuroscience of numerical cognition and reading; his 'number sense' and 'neuronal recycling' frameworks are broadly cited and helped shape the interdisciplinary field of 'educational neuroscience.'
His teacher and long-time collaborator, with whom he developed the 'global neuronal workspace' theory, regards him as an exemplar of bringing rigorous experiment into the study of consciousness.
His books, known for clarity, evidence and apt metaphor, are widely held to make a rare contribution in bridging brain science with everyday education and reading.

quotes: 我们并非生来就是一张白纸——每个婴儿都带着一套粗略的『数感』来到世上。（大意）
阅读并没有专属的脑区；它是文化对一块本为别用的皮层的『回收』。（大意）
学得好不好，往往取决于注意力、主动参与、反馈与巩固这几件事，而非天赋。（大意）
quotes_en: We are not born blank slates — every infant arrives with a rough 'number sense.' (paraphrased)
Reading has no dedicated brain area; it is culture's 'recycling' of cortex meant for another use. (paraphrased)
How well we learn depends more on attention, engagement, feedback and consolidation than on talent. (paraphrased)
works: 《脑的阅读：破解人类阅读之谜》（2009）
《我们如何学习：为什么大脑胜过任何机器……至今》（2020）
works_en: The Number Sense: How the Mind Creates Mathematics (1997)
Reading in the Brain: The Science and Evolution of a Human Invention (2009)
How We Learn: Why Brains Learn Better Than Any Machine... for Now (2020)
dehaene.lineage: 师承分子神经生物学家让-皮埃尔·尚热与心理语言学家雅克·梅勒，把行为实验与脑成像结合，接续并革新了数字认知与阅读的研究。其『神经元回收』与『全局神经工作空间』框架，成为教育神经科学与意识科学的重要参照，影响了一代认知神经科学研究者与循证教育改革。
dehaene.lineage_en: A pupil of the molecular neurobiologist Jean-Pierre Changeux and the psycholinguist Jacques Mehler, he fused behavioral experiment with brain imaging to continue and renew the study of numerical cognition and reading. His 'neuronal recycling' and 'global neuronal workspace' frameworks became key references for educational neuroscience and the science of consciousness, shaping a generation of cognitive-neuroscience researchers and evidence-based education reform.
dehaene.trivia: 他最初主修数学，一次读到关于数字如何在大脑中表征的研究后转向心理学——一个研究『数从哪来』的人，自己正是从数学走进大脑的。他领导的 NeuroSpin 拥有世界上磁场最强的人脑磁共振设备之一。他也把研究直接带回课堂：主持法国国民教育科学委员会，推动依据认知科学证据改革识字与算术教学。
dehaene.trivia_en: He first majored in mathematics and turned to psychology after reading research on how numbers are represented in the brain — a man who studies 'where number comes from' came to the brain by way of mathematics himself. The NeuroSpin center he leads houses one of the world's most powerful magnetic-resonance machines for the human brain. He has also carried his research straight back to the classroom, chairing France's scientific council for national education to reform the teaching of literacy and arithmetic according to evidence from cognitive science.

habermas.bio: 1929–，德国哲学家、社会理论家，法兰克福学派第二代核心人物，以《交往行为理论》与对公共领域、商谈民主的研究闻名。
habermas.bio_en: Born 1929, a German philosopher and social theorist, the central figure of the Frankfurt School's second generation, famous for The Theory of Communicative Action and his work on the public sphere and deliberative democracy.
habermas.ideas: 哈贝马斯要救的是『理性』。他承认前辈（阿多诺）与后现代（福柯、尼采）的诊断有力：工具理性、权力与金钱正在『殖民』我们的『生活世界』，把本该靠相互理解运转的领域变成算计与操控。但他不接受由此滑向的犬儒——如果一切都只是权力，那你连『这是压迫、那是解放』都没资格说，批判本身就失去了地基。他的出路是区分两种理性：一种是把人和世界当工具来算计的『工具理性』；另一种是『交往理性』——人们在无强制、信息对称、人人可平等发言的对话里（他称之为『理想言说情境』），只服从『更好的论证』这一种力量，从而达成真正的共识。正当性由此而来：一条规范之所以正当，是因为所有受它影响的人在自由平等的商谈中都能同意。他据此发展出商谈伦理与商谈民主，也据此批评福柯是『隐性的规范主义者』——福柯一边对支配充满道德义愤，一边又否认任何普遍规范，等于一边挥拳一边锯掉自己脚下的地板。
habermas.ideas_en: Habermas sets out to rescue reason. He grants that his predecessors (Adorno) and the postmoderns (Foucault, Nietzsche) diagnose something real: instrumental reason, power and money are 'colonizing' our 'lifeworld,' turning domains that should run on mutual understanding into calculation and manipulation. But he refuses the cynicism that follows — if everything is merely power, you lose the right even to say 'this is oppression, that is liberation,' and critique itself loses its ground. His way out distinguishes two rationalities: instrumental reason, which treats people and world as means to calculate; and communicative rationality, in which people, in an unforced dialogue with symmetrical information where all may speak as equals (his 'ideal speech situation'), submit only to the force of the better argument and reach genuine consensus. Legitimacy flows from this: a norm is legitimate because all affected could agree to it in free and equal deliberation. From this he builds discourse ethics and deliberative democracy, and criticizes Foucault as a 'crypto-normativist' — morally outraged at domination while denying all universal norms, throwing punches while sawing off the floor beneath his own feet.

assessments.text: 被视为战后最重要的哲学家之一，为民主商谈、公共理性与人权提供了系统的规范辩护。
福柯派与后现代论者认为其『理想言说情境』过于理想、抹平了真实权力差，普遍主义仍带欧洲中心之嫌。

assessments_en.text: Seen as one of the most important postwar philosophers, giving democratic deliberation, public reason and human rights a systematic normative defense.
Foucauldians and postmodernists find his 'ideal speech situation' too idealized, smoothing over real power asymmetries, and his universalism still Euro-centric.

quotes: 只服从更好的论证那一种、别无强制的力量。（大意）
一条规范唯当所有受影响者都能在理性商谈中同意时，才是正当的。（大意）
quotes_en: The unforced force of the better argument. (paraphrased)
A norm is valid only if all affected could agree to it in rational discourse. (paraphrased)
works_en: The Structural Transformation of the Public Sphere
habermas.lineage: 承法兰克福学派（阿多诺、霍克海默）而转向语言与交往；与福柯、利奥塔等后现代论者、以及罗尔斯正义论均有著名交锋。
habermas.lineage_en: He inherits the Frankfurt School (Adorno, Horkheimer) but turns to language and communication; famously debated Foucault, Lyotard and other postmoderns, as well as Rawls on justice.
habermas.trivia: 少年时因唇裂手术经历，他自陈对『沟通的脆弱与不可或缺』有切身体会，这也呼应了他一生对『交往』的哲学关切。
habermas.trivia_en: He has said his boyhood experience of cleft-palate surgery gave him a visceral sense of how fragile yet indispensable communication is — fittingly echoing his lifelong philosophical concern with 'communication.'

boroditsky.bio: 莱拉·波洛迪茨基，1976 年生于苏联时期的白俄罗斯明斯克，少年时随家移居美国，英语是她十几岁才学会的第二语言。她是认知科学家，现任加州大学圣地亚哥分校认知科学教授，此前执教于斯坦福大学与麻省理工学院。她以严谨的行为实验重新激活了一个曾被学界打入冷宫的老问题——『语言会不会影响思维』，用可测量的数据取代空泛的思辨。她的 TED 演讲《语言如何塑造我们的思维方式》被观看数以千万计，是当代把语言与认知研究带给大众的代表人物之一。
boroditsky.bio_en: Lera Boroditsky, born 1976 in Minsk, Belarus, then part of the Soviet Union, emigrated to the United States as a child; English is a second language she learned as a teenager. A cognitive scientist, she is professor of cognitive science at the University of California, San Diego, having previously taught at Stanford and MIT. With rigorous behavioral experiments she reawakened an old question the field had long banished — whether language influences thought — replacing loose speculation with measurable data. Her TED talk, 'How Language Shapes the Way We Think,' has been viewed tens of millions of times, making her one of the leading contemporary figures bringing research on language and cognition to a wide public.
boroditsky.ideas:
波洛迪茨基研究的，是一个听起来玄、其实能测的问题：你说的语言，会不会悄悄改变你怎么看、怎么记这个世界？
这个问题有段坎坷的历史。上世纪中叶，语言学家沃尔夫提出过一个『强版本』：语言决定思维，你的母语没有的东西，你就想不到。这个说法后来被大量反例推翻——它太满、太绝对。学界一朝被蛇咬，干脆把整个问题都当伪科学扔掉了。波洛迪茨基做的，是把它从极端里救回来，换成一个温和、可检验的版本：语言不锁死你的思维，但它像一副长期戴着的眼镜，反复要你注意某些区分，久而久之，你在那些方面就真的更敏锐、更容易记住。
她最爱举的例子都很具体。俄语把浅蓝和深蓝当成两个不同的基本颜色词（goluboy 和 siniy），于是俄语者在区分这两种蓝时，反应就是比英语者快一点点——语言给知觉加了道现成的界线。澳洲一个叫 Kuuk Thaayorre 的族群不说『左右』，只说绝对的东南西北，结果他们无论何时都清楚自己朝哪个方向，连把一叠照片按时间排序，都会不自觉地按太阳的轨迹从东往西摆。还有性别：德语里『桥』是阴性，德语者形容桥爱用『优雅、纤细』；西班牙语里『桥』是阳性，就更容易说它『强壮、结实』。
她也特别在意语言如何影响我们对『责任』的记忆。英语习惯说『他打碎了花瓶』，西班牙语更爱说『花瓶碎了』——结果说西班牙语的人，事后更难记起是谁弄碎的。一句话的语法，竟悄悄改写了记忆里的『谁之过』。
难得的是，她始终对自己的结论保持科学的克制：这些效应有大有小，有的重复得很稳、有的复制失败，她从不把它们夸大成『不同语言的人活在完全不同的宇宙』。她真正想说的是——人类心智惊人地灵活，而语言的多样，正是这份灵活留下的证据。
boroditsky.ideas_en:
Boroditsky studies a question that sounds mystical but can actually be measured: does the language you speak quietly change how you see and remember the world?
The question has a rocky history. In the mid-twentieth century the linguist Whorf proposed a 'strong version': language determines thought, and what your mother tongue lacks, you cannot think. That claim was overturned by counterexamples — too sweeping, too absolute — and, once bitten, the field threw the whole question out as pseudoscience. What Boroditsky did was rescue it from the extreme and recast it in a moderate, testable form: language does not lock your thinking, but like a pair of glasses worn for years it keeps asking you to notice certain distinctions, and over time you really do grow sharper at them, quicker to remember them.
Her favorite examples are concrete. Russian treats light and dark blue as two distinct basic color words (goluboy and siniy), and Russian speakers are a touch faster than English speakers at telling those two blues apart — language has drawn a ready-made line across perception. An Australian people called the Kuuk Thaayorre say not 'left/right' but only absolute north-south-east-west, and so always know which way they face; asked to arrange a set of photos in time order, they lay them out unconsciously along the sun's path, east to west. Or gender: in German 'bridge' is feminine, and German speakers describe bridges as 'elegant, slender'; in Spanish 'bridge' is masculine, and they more readily call it 'strong, sturdy.'
She is especially attentive to how language shapes our memory of responsibility. English says 'he broke the vase,' while Spanish prefers 'the vase broke' — and Spanish speakers afterward find it harder to recall who did it. The grammar of a single sentence quietly rewrites 'whose fault' in memory.
What is rare is that she keeps scientific restraint about her own conclusions: the effects vary in size, some replicate robustly and some fail, and she never inflates them into 'speakers of different languages live in wholly different universes.' What she really wants to say is that the human mind is astonishingly flexible — and the diversity of languages is the evidence that flexibility leaves behind.

assessments.text: 被广泛视为把『语言相对论』从思辨重新带回实验室的代表学者，其跨语言的行为实验推动这一问题以可测量、可争论的形式重回主流研究。
部分语言学家（如平克一系）认为她展示的效应真实但量级有限，多落在知觉与记忆的边缘，提醒不要由此滑回强决定论；这一争论至今活跃。
其 TED 演讲与文章以案例生动、论证清晰著称，被认为在向大众传播语言认知研究、又不牺牲严谨方面做得罕见地好。

assessments_en.text: Widely seen as the scholar who brought 'linguistic relativity' back from speculation into the lab; her cross-linguistic behavioral experiments returned the topic to mainstream research in measurable, arguable form.

Some linguists (in Pinker's line) hold that the effects she shows are real but limited in magnitude, mostly at the fringe of perception and memory, and warn against sliding back into strong determinism; the debate remains lively.
Her TED talk and essays, known for vivid cases and clear argument, are held to popularize research on language and cognition unusually well without sacrificing rigor.

quotes: 语言的多样之美，在于它让我们看见人类心智何其巧妙、何其灵活。（大意）
语言并不限制我们能感知什么，它更像是在替我们分配注意力。（大意）
当你学会一门新语言，你不只是学了新词，你获得了看同一件事的另一种方式。（大意）
quotes_en: The beauty of linguistic diversity is that it shows us how ingenious and how flexible the human mind is. (paraphrased)
Languages don't so much limit what we can perceive as allocate our attention for us. (paraphrased)
When you learn a new language you don't just learn new words; you gain another way of seeing the same thing. (paraphrased)
works: 《语言如何塑造我们的思维方式》（TED 演讲，2010 / 2017）
《语言如何塑造思维？》（Edge 长文，2009）
《跨语言的时间概念》等一系列跨语言认知实验论文
合编《语言与思维》相关学术文集与综述
works_en: 'How Language Shapes the Way We Think' (TED talk, 2010 / 2017)
'How Does Our Language Shape the Way We Think?' (Edge essay, 2009)
A series of cross-linguistic experimental papers, including work on how languages conceptualize time
Co-edited scholarly collections and reviews on language and thought
boroditsky.lineage: 她接续萨丕尔与沃尔夫开启、后被主流冷落的『语言相对论』传统，却以现代实验心理学的方法为之换血——用反应时、记忆测验、眼动等硬数据，把一个曾被视为不可检验的命题变成实证课题。她的工作影响了新一代跨语言认知研究者，也让语言学、心理学与人类学在这一问题上重新对话。
boroditsky.lineage_en: She continues the tradition of 'linguistic relativity' opened by Sapir and Whorf and later shunned by the mainstream, but renews it with the methods of modern experimental psychology — using hard data from reaction times, memory tests and eye-tracking to turn a once 'untestable' claim into an empirical subject. Her work has shaped a new generation of cross-linguistic cognition researchers and reopened dialogue among linguistics, psychology and anthropology on this question.
boroditsky.trivia: 她自己就是活的例证：英语是她十几岁才学的第二语言，在两种语言间来回切换的亲身经验，正是她投身这一研究的起点。她做实验时爱挑最偏远、最不像英语的语言（澳洲原住民语、亚马逊语言）下手，因为差异越大，越能照出语言留在认知上的手印。
boroditsky.trivia_en: She is a living example of her own subject: English is a second language she learned only as a teenager, and the felt experience of switching between two languages is the very starting point of her research. In her experiments she likes to reach for the most remote, least English-like languages (Aboriginal Australian, Amazonian tongues), because the greater the difference, the more clearly it reveals the fingerprints language leaves on cognition.

chomsky.bio: 诺姆·乔姆斯基，1928 年生于美国费城，语言学家、麻省理工学院荣休教授，公认的『现代语言学之父』，同时是二十世纪以来最著名、最高产的政治批评者之一。他二十多岁就以《句法结构》掀起语言学的『认知革命』，把研究重心从观察外在言语行为，转向探究人脑内部那套生成语言的规则系统。此后半个多世纪，他一面持续推进语言理论，一面以大量著作和演讲抨击强权、媒体与美国外交政策，是学界与公共领域里都极具分量、也极具争议的人物。
chomsky.bio_en: Noam Chomsky, born 1928 in Philadelphia, is a linguist and emeritus professor at MIT, widely called the 'father of modern linguistics,' and also one of the most famous and prolific political critics since the twentieth century. In his twenties, with Syntactic Structures, he set off a 'cognitive revolution' in linguistics, shifting the focus from observing outward verbal behavior to investigating the rule system inside the human mind that generates language. For more than half a century since, he has both advanced linguistic theory and, in a torrent of books and lectures, attacked power, the media and U.S. foreign policy — a figure of great weight and great controversy in both the academy and public life.
chomsky.ideas:
乔姆斯基的核心洞见，可以从他年轻时的一场论战说起。当时心理学界的主流是行为主义，认为语言就是刺激—反应—强化练出来的习惯，孩子学说话跟训练动物按杠杆没有本质区别。乔姆斯基一篇书评把这套说法彻底掀翻。他的关键论证叫『刺激的贫乏』：孩子听到的语句又少又乱，还常有错，可他们几年内就能说出、听懂无穷多句从没听过的新句子，还能凭直觉判断哪句合语法、哪句不合。仅靠模仿和记忆，绝对办不到这一点。
他由此提出震动学界的主张：人脑天生带着一套『语言官能』，仿佛一个专门的『语言器官』，里面预装了所有人类语言共享的深层原则，这套原则他称为『普遍语法』。表面上世界几千种语言千差万别，但在乔姆斯基看来，它们只是同一套普遍语法在不同『参数』上取了不同的值——就像同一台机器换了几个开关的方向。这解释了一个奇迹：任何正常孩子被丢进任何语言环境，都能毫不费力地学会当地的话。
他还区分了『语言能力』（你脑中那套无限生成句子的知识）与『语言表现』（你实际说出口、会口误会中断的话），主张语言学该研究前者。他晚年把理论不断精简，提出『最简方案』，认为人类语言的根基或许只是一个极简单却威力无穷的运算——把两个单元合并、再合并，如此递归，就能生成无限层级的句子。
必须分开讲的是他的另一重身份：政治批评者。他与赫尔曼提出著名的『宣传模型』，指出在自由社会里，思想控制未必靠审查，而靠媒体的所有权、广告、消息来源等结构性过滤，让某些结论显得理所当然、另一些根本进不了讨论——这就是『制造同意』。语言学家的乔姆斯基相信人类心智天生自由、创造力无穷；政治评论家的乔姆斯基则一生追问：是什么样的权力，在系统地辜负这份天赋。
chomsky.ideas_en:
Chomsky's central insight can be traced to a battle he fought young. The reigning psychology then was behaviorism, which held that language was a habit drilled by stimulus-response-reinforcement, a child learning to talk no different in kind from an animal trained to press a lever. A single book review by Chomsky overturned it. His key argument is the 'poverty of the stimulus': the speech a child hears is sparse, messy and often faulty, yet within a few years the child produces and understands an infinity of never-heard sentences and can judge by intuition which are grammatical and which not. Imitation and memory alone could never do this.
From here he advanced the claim that shook the field: the human brain comes equipped with a 'language faculty,' a kind of dedicated 'language organ,' preloaded with the deep principles all human languages share — principles he calls 'Universal Grammar.' On the surface the world's thousands of languages differ wildly, but to Chomsky they are one Universal Grammar with its 'parameters' set to different values — the same machine with a few switches flipped. This explains a miracle: any normal child dropped into any language environment learns the local tongue effortlessly.
He also distinguished 'competence' (the knowledge in your head that generates unlimited sentences) from 'performance' (what you actually utter, with its slips and breaks), and argued that linguistics should study the former. Late in life he pared his theory down into the 'Minimalist Program,' proposing that the root of human language may be a single, extremely simple yet immensely powerful operation — merge two units, then merge again, recursively — enough to generate sentences of unlimited depth.
His other identity must be told separately: the political critic. With Herman he proposed the famous 'propaganda model,' showing that in a free society thought control need not rely on censorship but on structural filters — media ownership, advertising, sourcing — that make some conclusions seem self-evident and keep others out of discussion altogether: this is 'manufacturing consent.' The linguist Chomsky believes the human mind is innately free and boundlessly creative; the political Chomsky spent a lifetime asking what kind of power systematically betrays that gift.

assessments.text: 被广泛尊为现代语言学的奠基者，其生成语法与普遍语法框架重塑了整个学科，并深刻推动了认知科学的诞生；也是二十世纪被引用最多的学者之一。

assessments.by: 经验主义与用法派的批评者
assessments.text: 部分语言学家（如提出皮拉罕语反例的埃弗里特，以及用法派、构式语法学者）质疑『普遍语法』是否真的存在，主张语言更多由使用与统计学习塑造——争论至今未决。
作为长期的政治异见者与『制造同意』的提出者，被视为最有影响力的当代批判知识分子之一；支持者敬其始终如一，批评者则指其立场偏激。

assessments_en.text: Widely honored as the founder of modern linguistics; his generative grammar and Universal Grammar reshaped the whole discipline and helped give birth to cognitive science — and he is among the most-cited scholars of the twentieth century.

Some linguists (Everett, who offered the Pirahã counterexample, and usage-based and construction-grammar scholars) doubt whether 'Universal Grammar' really exists, arguing language is shaped more by use and statistical learning — a debate still unsettled.

As a long-standing political dissident and author of the 'propaganda model,' he is seen as one of the most influential critical intellectuals of our time; admirers prize his consistency, critics call his positions extreme.

quotes: 无色的绿色念头狂怒地沉睡着。（他用来说明一句话可以合语法却毫无意义的著名例句）
语言首先不是一套交流系统，而是一套表达思想的系统；交流只是它的次要用途。（大意）
普通民众不知道正在发生什么，甚至不知道自己不知道。（大意）
quotes_en: Colorless green ideas sleep furiously. (his famous example that a sentence can be grammatical yet meaningless)
Language is not, in the first place, a system of communication but a system for expressing thought; communication is a secondary use. (paraphrased)
The general population does not know what is happening, and it does not even know that it does not know. (paraphrased)
works: 《制造同意：大众传媒的政治经济学》（与赫尔曼合著，1988）
works_en: Aspects of the Theory of Syntax (1965)
Manufacturing Consent: The Political Economy of the Mass Media (with Edward Herman, 1988)
chomsky.lineage: 他师从结构主义语言学家泽利格·哈里斯，却反戈一击、掀翻了行为主义与纯描写的语言学传统，转而接续笛卡尔、洪堡特等理性主义思路，主张心智天生、语言植根于人的本性——他称之为『笛卡尔语言学』。他开创的生成语法谱系影响了数代语言学家，并与认知心理学、计算机科学、哲学交叉，深刻塑造了认知科学的版图；其政治批评亦自成一脉，影响广泛的左翼与反战思想。
chomsky.lineage_en: A pupil of the structuralist linguist Zellig Harris, he turned on his teacher's field, overthrowing behaviorism and purely descriptive linguistics, and revived instead the rationalist line of Descartes and Humboldt — mind as innate, language rooted in human nature — which he called 'Cartesian linguistics.' The generative-grammar lineage he founded has shaped generations of linguists and, crossing into cognitive psychology, computer science and philosophy, deeply formed the map of cognitive science; his political criticism, too, forms a line of its own, widely influential across left and anti-war thought.
chomsky.trivia: 他造的句子『无色的绿色念头狂怒地沉睡着』成了语言学教科书里的经典——用来证明一句话可以完全合乎语法、却毫无意义，语法与意义是两回事。他一生同时经营两份几乎不相干的事业：白天是革新语言学的科学家，业余是笔耕不辍的政治异见者，且长期是在世学者中被引用次数最多的人之一。
chomsky.trivia_en: His coined sentence 'Colorless green ideas sleep furiously' became a classic of linguistics textbooks — proof that a sentence can be perfectly grammatical yet wholly meaningless, and that grammar and meaning are two different things. He ran two nearly unrelated careers at once: by day a scientist remaking linguistics, on the side a tireless political dissident — and for years among the most-cited living scholars of all.

deming.bio: W. 爱德华兹·戴明（W. Edwards Deming，1900–1993），美国统计学家、工程师与管理顾问，生于爱荷华州一个清贫家庭。他在耶鲁获物理学博士，早年在美国农业部与人口普查局做统计工作，师从贝尔实验室的沃尔特·休哈特，学到『统计过程控制』——用数据把偶然波动和真正的异常区分开。二战后，他受邀赴日本向工程师与企业高管讲授质量管理，被公认为日本战后制造业奇迹的关键推手；日本1951年即以他命名设立『戴明奖』。而在本国，他直到1980年 NBC 纪录片《日本能，我们为什么不能？》播出后才广为人知，晚年以八旬高龄开班授课、著书立说，影响了整个质量运动。
deming.bio_en: W. Edwards Deming (1900–1993) was an American statistician, engineer, and management consultant, born into a poor family in Iowa. He earned a PhD in physics at Yale and worked early on as a statistician at the U.S. Department of Agriculture and the Census Bureau, studying under Bell Labs' Walter Shewhart, from whom he learned 'statistical process control' — using data to separate ordinary fluctuation from genuine anomalies. After World War II he was invited to Japan to teach quality management to engineers and executives, and is widely credited as a key driver of Japan's postwar manufacturing miracle; Japan established the 'Deming Prize' in his name as early as 1951. In his own country he became widely known only after the 1980 NBC documentary 'If Japan Can... Why Can't We?'; in his eighties he still ran seminars and wrote books, shaping the entire quality movement.
deming.ideas:
戴明毕生要人明白一件反直觉的事：一个组织里绝大多数的好坏，不取决于人努不努力，而取决于他们被放进了一个怎样的『系统』。
他的底层工具来自老师休哈特的『统计过程控制』。任何过程的产出都会波动，戴明把波动分成两类：一类是『普通原因』——系统本身固有的、日常的随机起伏；另一类是『特殊原因』——真正出了岔子的异常。关键洞见是：只要波动还落在系统的正常范围内，去追问『这次为什么比上次差』就毫无意义，因为那只是随机。他有个著名的『红珠实验』：让工人从混着红白珠的桶里舀珠子，红珠算次品，可红珠比例是桶（系统）定死的，工人再用心也改变不了——然而管理者却照舀出的红珠数给工人排名、奖优罚劣。戴明用这个游戏证明：**给一个由系统决定的结果去排名个人，是在用随机数发奖惩，既不公也无用。** 他估计一个组织约94%的问题出在系统、只有约6%能归到个人。
由此他猛烈反对两样东西：一是年度绩效考核与员工排名，二是恐惧。他说考核『奖励了本就靠运气站在波动上端的人，惩罚了下端的人』，制造内斗、短视和造假，摧毁团队协作与长期改善的动力。他把『驱走恐惧』列为管理十四要点之一——因为『哪里有恐惧，哪里就有假数据』：人一怕，就报喜不报忧，真相被掩盖，问题永远修不好。
他晚年把这一切收进『渊博知识体系』：懂系统（各部分为共同目标协作）、懂变异（分清普通与特殊原因）、懂知识的理论（没有理论就学不到东西）、懂心理学（人如何被激励，内在动机为何比外在奖惩更持久）。他给的正解是 PDCA 循环（计划—执行—检查—处置）：持续、小步地改进系统本身。读戴明，最大的转变是学会先问『是不是系统的问题？』，而不是急着找一个人来奖或罚。
deming.ideas_en:
Deming spent his life trying to make people grasp one counterintuitive thing: most of what is good or bad in an organization depends not on how hard people try but on what kind of 'system' they have been placed in.
His foundational tool came from his teacher Shewhart's 'statistical process control.' The output of any process fluctuates, and Deming split that fluctuation into two kinds: 'common causes' — the everyday random variation inherent in the system itself — and 'special causes' — genuine anomalies where something has really gone wrong. The key insight is that as long as variation stays within the system's normal range, asking 'why was this one worse than the last' is meaningless, because it is merely random. He devised the famous 'Red Bead Experiment': workers scoop beads from a bucket mixing red and white ones, red beads count as defects, but the proportion of red beads is fixed by the bucket (the system) and no amount of effort by the worker can change it — yet managers rank workers by how many red beads they draw and reward or punish accordingly. With this game Deming showed that **ranking individuals by an outcome the system determines is handing out rewards and punishments based on random numbers — neither just nor useful.** He estimated that about 94% of an organization's problems lie in the system and only about 6% can be attributed to individuals.
From this he fiercely opposed two things: annual performance appraisal and ranking of employees, and fear. He said appraisal 'rewards those who happened, by luck, to stand at the upper end of the variation and punishes those at the lower end,' breeding infighting, short-termism, and falsified numbers while destroying teamwork and the drive for long-term improvement. He listed 'drive out fear' among his fourteen points for management — because 'wherever there is fear, you get wrong figures': once afraid, people report good news and hide the bad, the truth is buried, and problems are never fixed.
In his later years he gathered all of this into the 'System of Profound Knowledge': appreciation for a system (parts cooperating toward a shared aim), knowledge of variation (telling common from special causes), a theory of knowledge (without theory you learn nothing), and psychology (how people are motivated, and why intrinsic motivation outlasts external reward and punishment). His prescription was the PDCA cycle (Plan-Do-Check-Act): continual, small-step improvement of the system itself. The greatest shift from reading Deming is learning to ask first 'is this a problem of the system?' rather than rushing to find one person to reward or punish.

assessments.text: 被公认为日本战后质量革命的奠基者之一；1951年设立的『戴明奖』至今是日本质量管理的最高荣誉，1960年他获天皇授予二等瑞宝章。
其十四要点、PDCA 与『渊博知识体系』深刻影响了全面质量管理与后来的精益、六西格玛思想。也有批评者认为他几乎完全否定个人绩效考核过于绝对，落地时对如何评估与发展个人语焉不详。

assessments_en.text: Widely regarded as a founder of Japan's postwar quality revolution; the 'Deming Prize' established in 1951 remains Japan's highest honor in quality management, and in 1960 he received the Second Order of the Sacred Treasure from the Emperor.

His fourteen points, PDCA, and 'System of Profound Knowledge' deeply shaped total quality management and later lean and Six Sigma thinking. Critics argue his near-total rejection of individual performance appraisal was too absolute and vague on how, in practice, to assess and develop individuals.

quotes: In God we trust; all others must bring data.（据信为其名言，大意：敬畏上帝，其余请拿数据来。）
A bad system will beat a good person every time.（坏系统每一次都会打败好人。大意）
The most important figures are unknown and unknowable.（最重要的数字往往未知、且无法得知。大意）
Whenever there is fear, you will get wrong figures.（只要有恐惧，你拿到的就是假数据。大意）
quotes_en: In God we trust; all others must bring data. (widely attributed; paraphrased)
A bad system will beat a good person every time. (paraphrased)
The most important figures are unknown and unknowable. (paraphrased)
Whenever there is fear, you will get wrong figures. (paraphrased)
works: 《新经济学》(The New Economics for Industry, Government, Education, 1993)
《样本设计的若干理论》(Some Theory of Sampling, 1950)
『管理十四要点』与『七种致命恶疾』(讲义与讲座)
works_en: The New Economics for Industry, Government, Education (1993)
The 'Fourteen Points for Management' and the 'Seven Deadly Diseases' (lectures and seminars)
deming.lineage: 上承贝尔实验室沃尔特·休哈特的统计质量控制，将其从车间推广为一整套管理哲学；经由他在日本的讲学，深刻影响了石川馨、丰田生产方式等日本质量传统，又反哺欧美，成为全面质量管理（TQM）、精益生产与六西格玛的共同思想源头之一。
deming.lineage_en: Building on Walter Shewhart's statistical quality control at Bell Labs, he expanded it from the shop floor into a whole management philosophy; through his teaching in Japan he deeply influenced Kaoru Ishikawa, the Toyota Production System, and the Japanese quality tradition, then fed back into the West as one of the shared intellectual sources of total quality management (TQM), lean production, and Six Sigma.
deming.trivia: 他直到临终前几天仍在授课；八十岁后开设的四日研讨班场场爆满，常以『红珠实验』和『漏斗实验』当场演示系统的力量。他爱音乐，作过礼拜用的圣歌，还改编过《星条旗永不落》。他常说：不是你尽力就够了，你还得先知道该做什么。
deming.trivia_en: He was still teaching until a few days before his death; the four-day seminars he began running after age eighty were always packed, often using the 'Red Bead' and 'funnel' experiments to demonstrate the power of the system on the spot. He loved music, composed liturgical hymns, and even rearranged 'The Star-Spangled Banner.' He often said it is not enough to do your best — you must first know what to do.

avicenna.bio: 伊本·西那（拉丁世界称阿维森纳，约980–1037），波斯博学者，伊斯兰黄金时代最伟大的哲学家与医学家之一。生于中亚布哈拉附近，自幼早慧，十岁能诵《古兰经》，十八岁已精通医术；一生辗转于各地宫廷，任御医与大臣，动荡中笔耕不辍，著述逾百种，晚年病逝于哈马丹。
avicenna.bio_en: Ibn Sina (Latinized as Avicenna, c. 980–1037) was a Persian polymath, one of the greatest philosophers and physicians of the Islamic Golden Age. Born near Bukhara in Central Asia, a child prodigy who had memorized the Qur'an by ten and mastered medicine by eighteen, he spent his life moving among courts as physician and minister, writing ceaselessly amid upheaval, and died in Hamadan.
avicenna.ideas:
阿维森纳的哲学核心是一个看似抽象、却极其锋利的区分：『本质』与『存在』的分别。一个东西『是什么』（比如三角形的定义），和它『到底存不存在』，是两回事——你完全理解三角形，却不能因此断定世上真有一个三角形。于是他追问：万物的『存在』从何而来？由此推出他最著名的论证——『必然存在者』。世间万物都是『可能存在者』：它们本可以不存在，其存在必依赖别的原因；一路追溯，链条不能无限延伸，最终必有一个『本质即是存在』、无需任何原因、自身必然的终极者，那就是神。整个宇宙如同从这个源头『流溢』而出，层层展开。

他另有一个动人的思想实验——『飞人』：设想一个人一出生就悬浮在虚空中，四肢张开、彼此不接触，眼被蒙住、听不见、也感觉不到任何外物。这样一个人，会不会仍然确信『我存在』？阿维森纳说会。这证明：对自我的觉知并不依赖身体与感官，灵魂是一种独立的实在。这一论证比笛卡尔的『我思故我在』早了六百年，思路惊人地相近。

在医学上，他的《医典》把古希腊盖伦以来的医学知识系统化、条理化，分门别类地讨论生理、病理、药物与诊断，逻辑严整、便于查阅；它此后主导东西方医学教育长达数百年。阿维森纳的过人之处，正在于他既是构筑庞大形而上学体系的哲学家，又是俯身于病床、讲求实证与分类的医生——理性思辨与经验观察在他身上并行不悖。
avicenna.ideas_en:
At the core of Avicenna's philosophy is a distinction that looks abstract but cuts deep: the difference between 'essence' and 'existence.' What a thing *is* (the definition of a triangle) and *whether it actually exists* are two separate matters — you can grasp a triangle perfectly without knowing that any triangle exists. So he asks: where does the *existence* of things come from? This yields his most famous argument, the 'Necessary Existent.' Everything in the world is a 'possible existent': it might not have been, and its existence depends on some other cause; trace the chain back, and since it cannot regress infinitely, there must be an ultimate being whose very essence *is* existence, needing no cause, necessary in itself — and that is God. The cosmos 'emanates' from this source, unfolding in descending order.

He also devised a striking thought experiment, the 'Floating Man': imagine a person created fully formed, suspended in a void, limbs spread and not touching, eyes covered, hearing nothing, feeling no external thing. Would such a person still be certain that 'I exist'? Avicenna says yes. This shows that self-awareness does not depend on body or senses — the soul is an independent reality. The argument anticipates Descartes' 'I think, therefore I am' by six centuries, and along strikingly similar lines.

In medicine, his Canon systematized the knowledge inherited from Galen and Greek medicine, sorting physiology, pathology, drugs and diagnosis into a rigorous, searchable order; it went on to dominate medical education in East and West for centuries. Avicenna's rare gift was to be at once a philosopher building a vast metaphysical system and a physician at the bedside who prized evidence and classification — speculative reason and empirical observation ran together in him without conflict.

assessments.text: 经拉丁译本大量援引并批判性回应阿维森纳的形而上学，其『本质与存在之分』深刻影响了经院哲学对存在问题的讨论。
《医典》被译成拉丁文，成为蒙彼利埃、鲁汶等大学的标准教科书，沿用至十七世纪，被誉为『医学圣经』。
公认其为伊斯兰哲学承前启后的集大成者，把亚里士多德主义与新柏拉图主义熔铸成一个自洽而恢宏的体系。

assessments_en.text: Drew heavily on and critically engaged Avicenna's metaphysics through Latin translations; the essence–existence distinction deeply shaped Scholastic debate on being.
The Canon, translated into Latin, became the standard textbook at universities such as Montpellier and Leuven, used into the 17th century and hailed as a 'bible of medicine.'
Widely regarded as the great synthesizer of Islamic philosophy, fusing Aristotelianism and Neoplatonism into a coherent, monumental system.

quotes: 医学是一门科学，我们由此认识身体健康与失去健康时的种种状态。（《医典》开篇，大意）
存在者分两种：其存在因自身而必然者，与其存在因他者而可能者。
灵魂即使脱离一切感官与肉身，仍会确知自己存在。（『飞人』论证，大意）
quotes_en: Medicine is the science by which we learn the states of the body in health and when not in health. (opening of the Canon, paraphrased)
Existents are of two kinds: that whose existence is necessary through itself, and that whose existence is possible through another.
The soul, even stripped of every sense and of the body, would still be certain that it exists. (the Floating Man, paraphrased)
avicenna.lineage: 上承亚里士多德与法拉比，融合新柏拉图主义的流溢说，集伊斯兰东部哲学之大成；下启后世苏赫拉瓦迪的光照学派，并经拉丁译本深刻影响阿奎那、司各脱等经院哲学家，《医典》则塑造了数百年的东西方医学传统。
avicenna.lineage_en: Building on Aristotle and al-Farabi and fusing in the Neoplatonic doctrine of emanation, he crowned the philosophy of the eastern Islamic world; he opened the way to Suhrawardi's later Illuminationist school, and through Latin translation deeply shaped Scholastics such as Aquinas and Scotus, while the Canon molded centuries of medical tradition East and West.
avicenna.trivia: 相传他年少时为攻克亚里士多德《形而上学》，反复研读四十遍仍不得其解，直到偶然读到法拉比的一部小注才豁然贯通；又因治好萨曼王朝一位埃米尔的顽疾，获准出入王室藏书楼，尽览群籍。他常通宵著述，据说《治疗论》的许多章节是在辗转流亡、乃至短暂囚禁的途中凭记忆写成的。
avicenna.trivia_en: He is said to have read Aristotle's Metaphysics forty times without grasping it, until a short commentary by al-Farabi suddenly made it clear; and, having cured a stubborn illness of a Samanid emir, he was granted the run of the royal library and devoured its holdings. He often wrote through the night, and much of the Book of Healing was reportedly composed from memory while in flight, and even during a spell of imprisonment.

fisher.bio: 海伦·费舍尔（1945–2024），美国生物人类学家，金赛研究所资深研究员、罗格斯大学教授。她率先用功能性核磁共振（fMRI）扫描热恋、失恋与长期相守者的大脑，把『爱情』纳入实证神经科学的研究对象，著有《我们为何相爱》《爱的解剖》等畅销书，并长期担任婚恋网站的首席科学顾问。
fisher.bio_en: Helen Fisher (1945–2024) was an American biological anthropologist, a senior research fellow at the Kinsey Institute and a professor at Rutgers University. A pioneer in using functional MRI to scan the brains of people newly in love, freshly rejected, and in long marriages, she made romantic love an object of empirical neuroscience. She wrote the bestsellers Why We Love and Anatomy of Love and long served as chief scientific adviser to an online-dating company.
fisher.ideas:
费舍尔最核心、也最具颠覆性的主张是：浪漫爱不是一种情绪，而是一种『驱力』（drive）。情绪来去随境，而驱力像饥渴一样，是大脑深处的动机系统在推着你去追求一个特定对象。她把热恋者送进 fMRI，发现被点亮的正是与奖赏、动机相关的多巴胺通路——和让人上瘾的机制高度重叠。这解释了热恋为何有那种坐立不安、废寝忘食、满脑子都是对方的『成瘾』特质。

她进一步把我们笼统称作『爱』的东西，拆成三套相对独立、又可任意组合的脑系统。其一是『性欲』，由睾酮驱动，指向的是泛化的性满足；其二是『浪漫吸引』，由多巴胺、去甲肾上腺素和偏低的血清素驱动，表现为聚焦于某一个人的强烈痴迷与能量高涨；其三是『依恋』，由催产素与血管加压素驱动，表现为长期相守中那种安稳、平静、彼此牵挂的联结。三套系统各有各的神经化学、各有各的节奏：吸引像烈火，会随多巴胺的调节而在一两年内渐渐降温；依恋像文火，靠日积月累的相处慢慢煨成。理解这一点，就不会把激情退潮误当作『不爱了』。

她还强调，浪漫爱是跨文化的人类普遍现象——在她考察的绝大多数社会里都能找到，绝非现代或西方的发明；同时，这些天生的系统又被各自的文化、成长经历与个人选择反复塑造和组合。她因此站在一个务实的中间地带：爱情既是刻进大脑的生物学，也是可以被经营的关系。
fisher.ideas_en:
Fisher's central and most disruptive claim is that romantic love is not an emotion but a 'drive.' Emotions come and go with circumstance; a drive, like hunger or thirst, is a deep motivational system pushing you toward a specific goal. Putting infatuated people into an fMRI, she found what lit up was the dopamine reward-and-motivation pathway — the same circuitry implicated in addiction. That explains the 'addictive' texture of new love: the restlessness, the lost sleep, the mind that can think of nothing but the beloved.

She further divided what we loosely call 'love' into three semi-independent brain systems that can combine in any way. First, 'lust,' driven by testosterone and aimed at generalized sexual gratification. Second, 'romantic attraction,' driven by dopamine, norepinephrine and lowered serotonin, felt as intense, focused obsession and soaring energy directed at one person. Third, 'attachment,' driven by oxytocin and vasopressin, felt as the calm, steady, mutually caring bond of a long partnership. Each system has its own neurochemistry and its own tempo: attraction burns hot and cools within a year or two as dopamine downregulates; attachment simmers, built slowly through accumulated time together. Grasp this and you stop mistaking the ebb of passion for the end of love.

She also stressed that romantic love is a human universal across cultures — found in the overwhelming majority of societies she surveyed, hardly a modern or Western invention — even as these innate systems are endlessly shaped and recombined by culture, upbringing and personal choice. She thus occupied a pragmatic middle ground: love is at once a biology etched into the brain and a relationship that can be tended.

assessments.text: 其 TED 演讲《我们为何相爱、为何不忠》成为观看量最高的演讲之一，把爱情的神经科学带入大众视野。
赞赏她开创性地把浪漫爱纳入脑成像研究；也有批评认为把复杂的爱情还原为几套神经化学系统失之简化。
视她为把达尔文式的择偶与配对理论、与现代神经影像证据相衔接的重要桥梁。

assessments_en.text: Her TED talk on why we love and why we cheat became one of the most-watched talks, bringing the neuroscience of love to a wide audience.
Praised for pioneering the brain-imaging study of romantic love; also criticized for reducing love's complexity to a handful of neurochemical systems.
Regarded as an important bridge between Darwinian theories of mate choice and pair-bonding and modern neuroimaging evidence.

quotes: 浪漫爱不是一种情绪，它是一种驱力，来自大脑的动机核心。（大意）
我们研究的不是爱的感觉，而是爱的机制。（大意）
性欲让你四处张望，浪漫吸引让你锁定一人，依恋让你安然厮守。（大意）
quotes_en: Romantic love is not an emotion; it's a drive, coming from the motivational core of the brain. (paraphrased)
We were not studying the feeling of love so much as its machinery. (paraphrased)
Lust makes you look around, attraction makes you focus on one, attachment lets you tolerate that one long enough to raise a child. (paraphrased)
fisher.lineage: 思想上承达尔文的性选择理论与鲍尔比的依恋理论，把进化人类学与现代脑成像相结合；她与神经科学家露西·布朗、心理学家阿瑟·阿伦合作的热恋 fMRI 研究，成为爱情神经科学的奠基性工作，影响了此后一代研究者与大众对亲密关系的理解。
fisher.lineage_en: Intellectually she drew on Darwin's theory of sexual selection and Bowlby's attachment theory, wedding evolutionary anthropology to modern brain imaging; her fMRI studies of new love, done with the neuroscientist Lucy Brown and the psychologist Arthur Aron, became foundational to the neuroscience of love and shaped a generation of researchers and popular understanding of intimacy.
fisher.trivia: 她为婚恋网站设计的一套依据神经化学倾向划分气质类型（探索者、建造者、指挥者、协商者）的性格测验，被全球数以千万计的用户填答，成为她把实验室理论推向现实交友市场的一次大规模实践。她本人是同卵双胞胎，曾说这段经历让她一生着迷于『是什么让两个基因几乎相同的人，爱上完全不同的对象』。
fisher.trivia_en: A personality questionnaire she designed for a dating company, sorting people by neurochemical temperament into Explorer, Builder, Director and Negotiator types, was completed by tens of millions worldwide — a large-scale test of her lab theories in the real dating market. An identical twin herself, she said the experience left her lifelong fascination with what makes two people of nearly identical genes fall for entirely different partners.

thoreau.bio: 1817–1862，美国作家、哲学家、博物学家，超验主义代表人物。曾在马萨诸塞州瓦尔登湖畔独居两年，写下《瓦尔登湖》；另著《论公民的不服从》。
thoreau.bio_en: 1817–1862, an American writer, philosopher and naturalist, a key figure of Transcendentalism. He lived alone for two years by Walden Pond in Massachusetts, producing Walden, and also wrote Civil Disobedience.
thoreau.ideas:
梭罗做过一个著名的实验：1845 年他跑到瓦尔登湖边，亲手盖了间小木屋，种豆、钓鱼、观察四季，独居两年零两个月，只为回答一个问题——生活最本质的必需品到底是什么，其余的会不会都是多余？他的答案是那句口号：『简化，简化，再简化』。他算过一笔账：为了买下更大的房子、更多的物件，人得出卖大量的时间与生命去挣钱，于是『多数人过着平静的绝望的生活』——被自己并不真正需要的东西奴役。在他看来，真正的财富不是你拥有多少，而是你有多少可以自由支配、用来清醒地活着的时间；一个人越是能把欲望降下来，就越自由。所以他不是简单地反对钱，而是反对『用生命去换取不必要之物』这笔糟糕的交易。
梭罗的另一条主线是『个人良知高于国家』。他因拒交人头税（抗议蓄奴与对墨西哥的战争）被关了一夜，由此写下《论公民的不服从》：当法律要求你参与不义，正当的做法是拒绝服从、甘愿承担后果。这篇短文后来深刻影响了甘地与马丁·路德·金。把这两条合起来看，梭罗其实在讲同一件事：无论面对市场还是国家，人都该夺回对自己生活的主权，审慎地、按良心地、尽量简单地活。
thoreau.ideas_en:
Thoreau ran a famous experiment: in 1845 he went to Walden Pond, built a cabin with his own hands, grew beans, fished and watched the seasons, living alone for two years and two months to answer one question — what are life's true essentials, and might everything else be surplus? His answer was the slogan 'Simplify, simplify, simplify.' He did the arithmetic: to buy a bigger house and more things, a person must sell off huge amounts of time and life to earn money, so 'the mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation,' enslaved by things they do not really need. Real wealth, he held, is not how much you own but how much time you have free to live deliberately; the more one can lower one's wants, the freer one becomes. So he is not simply against money but against the bad bargain of trading life for the unnecessary.
His other main line is that individual conscience outranks the state. Jailed for a night for refusing the poll tax (protesting slavery and the war on Mexico), he wrote Civil Disobedience: when a law demands your complicity in injustice, the right response is to refuse and bear the consequences. That essay went on to shape Gandhi and Martin Luther King. Put together, both lines say one thing: whether facing the market or the state, a person should reclaim sovereignty over their own life and live deliberately, by conscience, and as simply as possible.

assessments.text: 《瓦尔登湖》被奉为自然写作与自愿简朴运动的圣经，影响深远。
有人指出他的『极简』有退路——小屋离镇不远、家人常接济，质疑这是有条件者才玩得起的浪漫。

assessments_en.text: Walden is treated as a bible of nature writing and voluntary simplicity, with lasting influence.
Some note his 'minimalism' had a safety net — the cabin was near town and family often helped — questioning it as a romance only the cushioned can afford.

quotes: 我步入丛林，因为我希望活得审慎……只面对生活最本质的事实。（大意）
多数人过着平静的绝望的生活。（大意）
一个人放下的东西越多，他就越富有。（大意）
quotes_en: I went to the woods because I wished to live deliberately, to front only the essential facts of life. (paraphrased)
The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation. (paraphrased)
A man is rich in proportion to the number of things he can let alone. (paraphrased)
thoreau.lineage: 承爱默生与超验主义；其简朴与自然观影响了环保运动，公民不服从思想直接启发了甘地与马丁·路德·金。
thoreau.lineage_en: He extends Emerson and Transcendentalism; his ethic of simplicity and nature shaped environmentalism, and his civil disobedience directly inspired Gandhi and Martin Luther King.
thoreau.trivia: 他在瓦尔登湖其实并非与世隔绝——小屋离康科德镇约两英里，他常回家、也常有访客，母亲还帮他洗衣；这份『不彻底』常被拿来调侃，也让他的实验更像一场刻意的示范而非苦修。
thoreau.trivia_en: His Walden life was not truly cut off — the cabin sat about two miles from Concord, he often walked home and had visitors, and his mother helped with laundry; this 'incompleteness' is often teased, and makes his experiment read more as a deliberate demonstration than an ascetic ordeal.

diogenes.bio: 约前412–前323，古希腊锡诺普人，犬儒学派最著名的实践者。相传住在一个大陶瓮里，以近乎一无所有的极端简朴生活戏剧性地宣扬自足与自由。
diogenes.bio_en: c. 412–323 BC, a Greek from Sinope and the most famous practitioner of Cynicism. Said to have lived in a large ceramic jar, he dramatized self-sufficiency and freedom through an extreme, near-propertyless simplicity.
diogenes.ideas: 第欧根尼把一个哲学主张活成了行为艺术：幸福来自『自足』(autarkeia)，而自足来自把欲望降到最低。他几乎一无所有——住在一个大陶瓮里，白天打着灯笼在市集上『寻找一个诚实的人』；据说他本来还留着一只木碗，直到看见一个孩子直接用手捧水喝，便把碗也扔了，说这孩子在简朴上还赢了他。在他看来，文明堆起来的那套礼俗、财产、名声、体面，大多是枷锁和表演，把人变成自己欲望和他人眼光的奴隶；真正的自由，是敢于不要这些、当众戳穿它们的虚伪（犬儒的『无耻』anaideia 正指这种不畏羞辱的坦荡）。他自称『世界公民』(kosmopolitês)，不认某一城邦的规矩。最有名的一幕：亚历山大大帝慕名来访，问他想要什么恩赐，正在晒太阳的第欧根尼只回了一句『请别挡住我的阳光』。他不是要人人住进陶瓮，而是用最极端的方式逼你看清：你以为的必需品，有多少其实只是被驯化出来的欲望。
diogenes.ideas_en: Diogenes turned a philosophical claim into performance art: happiness comes from self-sufficiency (autarkeia), and self-sufficiency comes from cutting wants to the bone. He owned almost nothing — lived in a large jar and walked the marketplace by day with a lamp 'looking for an honest man'; the story goes that he still kept a wooden bowl until he saw a boy drink water with his cupped hands, whereupon he threw the bowl away, saying the child had beaten him at simplicity. Civilization's heap of convention, property, reputation and respectability, he held, is mostly shackles and theatre, making people slaves to their own desires and to others' eyes; true freedom is daring to refuse all that and to puncture its hypocrisy in public (the Cynic's 'shamelessness,' anaideia, names exactly this fearless candor). He called himself a 'citizen of the world' (kosmopolitês), owing allegiance to no single city's rules. His most famous scene: Alexander the Great sought him out and asked what favor he wanted; sunbathing, Diogenes replied only, 'Stand out of my sunlight.' He did not want everyone in a jar — he used the most extreme means to force you to see how much of what you call a necessity is only a domesticated desire.

assessments.text: 被视为犬儒学派的化身，其轶事经第欧根尼·拉尔修等流传，成为『以行动为哲学』的典范。
批评者认为其反文明姿态华而不实、近乎表演，且完全依赖它所鄙夷的城邦供养（乞食为生）。

assessments_en.text: Seen as the embodiment of Cynicism, his anecdotes (via Diogenes Laertius and others) became the model of 'philosophy as action.'
Critics call his anti-civilization posture showy, near-theatrical, and wholly dependent — by begging — on the very polis he scorned.

quotes: 请别挡住我的阳光。（对亚历山大，大意）
我在找一个诚实的人。（大意）
拥有得最少而无所求的人，最接近神。（大意）
quotes_en: Stand out of my sunlight. (to Alexander, paraphrased)
I am looking for an honest man. (paraphrased)
He who has fewest wants is nearest to the gods. (paraphrased)
works: 无传世著作，言行经《名哲言行录》(第欧根尼·拉尔修) 等古代文献流传
works_en: No surviving writings; his words and deeds survive via ancient sources such as Diogenes Laertius's Lives of the Eminent Philosophers
diogenes.lineage: 承苏格拉底一脉（经安提斯泰尼），开犬儒学派；其自足与少欲思想深刻影响了后来的斯多葛学派。
diogenes.lineage_en: He descends from Socrates (via Antisthenes) and founds Cynicism; his ideas of self-sufficiency and minimal want deeply shaped the later Stoics.
diogenes.trivia: 据说他曾在大白天点着灯笼走遍雅典，说自己『在找一个真正的人』；死后锡诺普人为他立了一根大理石柱，顶上刻着一条狗——正对应『犬儒』(kynikos＝像狗一样) 的名号。
diogenes.trivia_en: He is said to have walked Athens in broad daylight with a lit lamp, saying he was 'looking for a real human being'; after his death Sinope raised a marble column topped with a dog — fitting the very name 'Cynic' (kynikos, dog-like).

lembke.bio: 当代美国精神科医生，斯坦福大学精神医学与行为科学教授、斯坦福成瘾医学门诊主任，《多巴胺国度》与《药贩子医生》的作者，长期在阿片类药物危机中担任临床与政策方面的专家证人。
lembke.bio_en: A contemporary American psychiatrist, professor of psychiatry and behavioral sciences at Stanford and chief of the Stanford Addiction Medicine clinic. She wrote Dopamine Nation and Drug Dealer, MD, and has long served as a clinical and policy expert on the opioid crisis.
lembke.ideas:
伦布克最广为人知的一个说法是：快感与痛苦不是两件事，而是同一架跷跷板的两端。大脑处理愉悦和处理疼痛用的是重叠的区域，而它最在乎的不是让你快乐，是让你回到平衡。所以每当你尝到一次快感，跷跷板往快乐那边压下去，大脑随即在痛苦那一端悄悄加上砝码，把它扳回水平——而且往往会扳过头。那点『过头』，就是刷完一小时短视频后的空虚、聚会散场后的失落、吃完整包薯片后的懊丧。
真正麻烦的是重复。同样的刺激反复来，大脑就把砝码永久留在痛苦那侧，这在临床上叫耐受：从前一份剂量给你的快乐，现在要三份才有；再往后，三份只够让你感觉『正常』。人于是被困在一个跑步机上——不是为了变得更快乐，只是为了不难受。伦布克说，今天最危险的地方在于环境：短视频、糖、游戏、购物、色情内容都被工程化得更强效、更快速、更唾手可得，用她的话说，整个世界被『药物化』了。所以成瘾不再是少数人的道德缺陷，而是普通人放在这种环境里的可预期结果。
她给的解法同样具体。第一是禁断与重置：临床经验里，离开某个刺激大约三十天，多数人的奖赏基线才开始回升——头两周通常更难受，那正是跷跷板在回位。第二是『自我约束』(self-binding)：不要指望意志力当场取胜，而是提前在自己和诱惑之间放进物理的、时间的或类别的屏障——把手机放到另一个房间，比每次告诉自己『再刷五分钟』有效得多。第三条最反直觉：主动去按痛苦那一端。运动、冷水、专注啃一件难事，这些先带来不适的活动会让跷跷板往快乐那侧回弹，而且这种快乐来得慢、去得也慢，比直接摄取的快感稳定。她始终把话说在机制和剂量上，不做道德训诫：她也强调诚实——向别人说出真话本身就能改变奖赏回路，这是她在诊室里最看重的一味药。
lembke.ideas_en:
Lembke's best-known claim is that pleasure and pain are not two separate things but two ends of one balance. The brain processes them in overlapping regions, and what it cares about most is not making you happy but returning you to equilibrium. So every time you take a hit of pleasure and the balance tips that way, the brain quietly adds weights to the pain side to level it again — and usually overshoots. That overshoot is the emptiness after an hour of short videos, the flatness after the party ends, the regret at the bottom of the chip bag.
The real trouble is repetition. Deliver the same stimulus again and again and the brain leaves those weights permanently on the pain side; clinically this is tolerance. What one dose used to give you now takes three, and eventually three only makes you feel normal. People end up on a treadmill they run not to get happier but to stop feeling bad. What makes today especially dangerous, Lembke argues, is the environment: short video, sugar, games, shopping and pornography have all been engineered to be more potent, faster and more available — the world, in her phrase, has been drugified. Addiction is therefore no longer a moral failing of the few but a predictable outcome for ordinary people placed in that environment.
Her remedies are equally concrete. First, abstinence and reset: in her clinical experience it takes roughly thirty days away from a given stimulus before most people's reward baseline begins to recover, and the first two weeks usually feel worse — that is the balance swinging back. Second, self-binding: do not expect willpower to win in the moment; put physical, temporal or categorical barriers between yourself and the temptation in advance. Leaving the phone in another room beats telling yourself 'five more minutes' every time. Third, and most counterintuitive, press deliberately on the pain side. Exercise, cold water, sustained work on something hard all hurt first and let the balance rebound toward pleasure — a slower-arriving, slower-fading kind of pleasure, steadier than what you can simply consume. She keeps the discussion on mechanism and dosage rather than moral instruction, and she insists on one more ingredient she prizes in the consulting room: honesty, because telling another person the truth about yourself changes the reward circuitry too.

assessments.by: 成瘾医学与公共卫生界
assessments.text: 被视为把成瘾从『少数人的道德失败』重新界定为『被过量供给的环境中的可预期反应』的重要临床声音，在阿片类药物危机中屡被援引。
有研究者认为把日常的短视频、购物、糖统统纳入『成瘾』框架，有过度扩张诊断之嫌；『多巴胺』一词在通俗传播中也常被简化成万能解释。

assessments_en.text: Widely regarded as a clinical voice that redefined addiction from 'a moral failure of the few' to 'a predictable response to an oversupplied environment,' frequently cited during the opioid crisis.

Some researchers argue that folding everyday short video, shopping and sugar into an 'addiction' frame overextends the diagnosis, and that in popular use 'dopamine' has become a catch-all explanation.

quotes: 追逐快感、逃避痛苦，最终带来的是痛苦。（大意）
我们都住进了一个被药物化的世界——从手机到糖，一切都被做得更强效、更易得。（大意）
别指望在诱惑面前赢下意志力的对决，先在你和它之间放一道屏障。（大意）
quotes_en: The relentless pursuit of pleasure, and avoidance of pain, leads to pain. (paraphrased)
We are all living in a drugified world — from phones to sugar, everything has been made more potent and more available. (paraphrased)
Don't count on winning a contest of willpower in the moment; put a barrier between yourself and the thing first. (paraphrased)
works: 《多巴胺国度：在放纵的时代寻找平衡》(Dopamine Nation, 2021)
《药贩子医生：医生如何被骗、病人如何上钩》(Drug Dealer, MD, 2016)
关于阿片类处方与成瘾治疗的大量临床研究论文
works_en: Dopamine Nation: Finding Balance in the Age of Indulgence (2021)
Drug Dealer, MD: How Doctors Were Duped, Patients Got Hooked, and Why It's So Hard to Stop (2016)
Numerous clinical papers on opioid prescribing and addiction treatment
lembke.lineage: 临床上承成瘾医学与精神药理学传统，理论上接过所罗门(Richard Solomon)的『对抗过程』理论——任何强烈的愉悦都会激起一个相反的、更持久的余波，以及奥尔兹、舒尔茨以来关于多巴胺与奖赏预测的神经科学；同时与勒斯蒂格(糖)、马泰(创伤与成瘾)等人同属把成瘾从个人德性问题移向神经机制与环境供给的一路。她的独特位置在于始终站在门诊里说话：理论是为了给病人一套第二天就能用的动作。
lembke.lineage_en: Clinically she stands in the tradition of addiction medicine and psychopharmacology; theoretically she inherits Richard Solomon's opponent-process theory — that any intense pleasure provokes an opposite and longer-lasting aftereffect — along with the neuroscience of dopamine and reward prediction running from Olds to Schultz. She belongs with figures such as Robert Lustig (sugar) and Gabor Maté (trauma and addiction) in moving addiction away from personal virtue toward neural mechanism and environmental supply. What sets her apart is that she always speaks from the clinic: the theory exists to give a patient something they can do tomorrow.
lembke.trivia: 她在书里坦白自己的一段沉迷——不是酒也不是药，而是深夜一本接一本读言情小说读到影响工作，用来说明成瘾从来不是『别人的毛病』。她也是纪录片《社会困境》的受访者之一，在片中谈平台如何按成瘾的逻辑设计产品。
lembke.trivia_en: In her book she confesses an addiction of her own — not alcohol or drugs but reading one romance novel after another late into the night until it affected her work — as evidence that addiction is never merely 'other people's problem.' She also appears in the documentary The Social Dilemma, discussing how platforms design products along the logic of addiction.
